§1   PURPOSE
This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) system.
TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
scope of this document.
§2   SCOPE
TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.
TCS-02 applies to:
•
a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).
•
b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).
•
c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.
•
d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.

§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS
§3.1   Ownership and installation
Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
installation drawing.
§3.3   Functional requirements

restoration.

d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
diagnostic points.

e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
SCADA/EMS Engineering only.

drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.
§3.5   Time synchronization
The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.
§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification
§3.2   Approved models
The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU
service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power
plant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the
utility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).

corrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected
equipment.
§4.4   Address and IP management
All IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and
Alleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate

Local and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to
Alleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication

1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
•
IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
•
IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
•
IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
•
ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.


--- page 2 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 2
•
Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.
•
Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.
4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.
4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the
control cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of
communications shall not defeat local protection.
Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.


--- page 3 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 3
5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect
operable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of
clearance holds.
6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location
accessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer
premises.
4.3 DER-Side Protection
DER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection
protection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI
recloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.
DER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.
4.4 Grounding
The DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with
the grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's
grounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.
4.5 Anti-Islanding
The DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone
requirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage
and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive
scheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;
otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.
5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS
5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing
The POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:
(a) The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream
recloser.
(b) The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per
the site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the
site's operating procedure.
(c) Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study
prior to energization.
5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection
DER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent
reasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the
POI recloser shall trip as backup protection.
5.3 Direct Transfer Trip
Direct transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable
non-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening
of the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications
channel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.
5.4 Reclosing Blocking
Automatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the
DER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the


--- page 4 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 4
affected feeder warrants such a change. The determination shall be made per site by Distribution Protection
5.5 Settings Governance
All protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the
DER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in
the field without a written revision order.
6. TESTING
6.1 Factory Acceptance
The POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard
test protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to
shipment.
6.2 Site Acceptance
Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed
by Alleniom Utilities:
1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.
2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.
3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,
and reset.
4. End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.
5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.
6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.
7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.
6.3 Commissioning and Cutover
Cutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and
accepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system
operator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.
6.4 Periodic Testing
The POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. DER-side protective
devices shall be tested by the DER owner on a schedule not to exceed that of comparable utility-owned
equipment, with test records made available to Alleniom Utilities on request.
6.5 Post-Event Testing
Following any operation of the POI recloser attributable to a system disturbance, a DER-side event, or a
mis-operation, Distribution Protection Engineering shall review the event records and direct such retesting or
resetting as it determines appropriate before the site is returned to service.
End of DPS-07 Rev 2 — Distribution Protection Standard. Distribution: Alleniom Standards Engineering master file;
Distribution Protection Engineering; Distribution Operations; DER Program Office; APUC filing (informational).
Engineering and recorded in the site's interconnection file.

Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "
              "scanner does not fully cover.")
        return 0
    print("Unreviewed candidates, strongest first (add each hard requirement to requirements.csv citing its ID, or "
          "list the ID with a reason in rejected.csv; a statement with a number in a document that is not marked "
          "void needs its own ID even if you rejected the document):")
    for r in open_rows[:limit]:
        print(f"- {r['id']} [{r['doc']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}] {r['text'][:220]}")
    if len(open_rows) > limit:
        by = {}
        for r in open_rows[limit:]:
            by[r["doc"]] = by.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
        print(f"... and {len(open_rows) - limit} more: " + ", ".join(f"{d} ({c})" for d, c in sorted(by.items())))
    return 1


SRC_COL = re.compile(r"source|clause|document|doc\b|ref|citation|basis|standard|section", re.I)
VAL_COL = re.compile(r"value|limit|threshold|criterion|criteria|requirement|min|max|allow", re.I)
CLAUSE_REF = re.compile(r"(§\s*[\w.()-]+|\b(?:clause|section|sec\.|para\.?|table|article|art\.)\s*[\w.()-]+)", re.I)


def norm_num(x):
    x = x.replace(",", "")
    try:
        v = float(x)
    except ValueError:
        return {x}
    out = {x, f"{v:g}"}
    if v == int(v):
        out.add(str(int(v)))
    return out


def read_register(path):
    if path.lower().endswith((".xlsx", ".xlsm")):
        try:
            import openpyxl
        except ImportError:
            sys.exit("--register on .xlsx needs openpyxl; export the sheet to CSV")
        wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True, read_only=True)
        rows = []
        for ws in wb.worksheets:
            rows += [["" if c is None else str(c) for c in r] for r in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True)]

§1 PURPOSE
ERP-9 establishes the procedure by which an interconnection application encountering a standards
conflict, a silence between standards, or site conditions falling outside the assumptions of a tabulated
requirement is referred to a per-site protection/SCADA engineering determination. The procedure exists so
that documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against
active applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,
on a schedule stated in §4.
This procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER
Program. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection
Standard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.


--- page 2 ---
§2 SCOPE
ERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one
or more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system
impact study:
(1)  Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to
the affected site.
(2)  An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic
on which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an
exception).
(3)  The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in
light of the site's specific protection arrangement.
Sub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application
of ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration
warrants site-specific protection engineering input.
Nothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a
determination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).
§3 REFERRAL ROUTING
Any standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site
protection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;
each site is resolved on its own protection scheme.
The reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11
(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection
diagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's
protection arrangement. Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11 to Distribution
Protection Engineering; where SCADA/EMS input is required, the Manager, Distribution Protection
Engineering routes a copy to the SCADA/EMS Engineering group for concurrent review.
Referral does not itself alter the application's status in the DER Program queue. The affected application
remains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the
referred question shall proceed in parallel.
The per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection
Engineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and is filed with the application record. The determination is binding for the
referred site and does not create a general rule across the program; a subsequent site presenting a similar
question is referred and determined on its own facts.
Where the site's protection arrangement, as determined under this section, differs from the tabular default
of DIS-01 §5 Table 5-1, the engineering determination on Form ER-11 supplements the site's
protective-equipment scoping and is provided to the DER Program Office and to the contracts desk for
incorporation into the interconnection service agreement.
Where the referral resolves a recurring pattern that Standards Engineering considers appropriate to reflect
in a future revision of a standard, the determinations are logged and reviewed as provided in §5.

Where the reviewer requests reclassification, the request is decided in writing within two business days.
Extensions to the timelines above are permitted only in writing, are issued by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and are copied to the DER Program Manager and Regulatory Affairs. Applications
shall not be held in queue pending revision of a standard where this procedure provides a determination
path; extensions do not authorize a screening hold outside this procedure.
§5 DOCUMENTATION
The completed Form ER-11, the engineering determination, and any supporting studies are filed with the
application record retained by Interconnection Studies for the retention period established by Regulatory
Affairs. A copy of the completed Form ER-11 is filed in the Standards Engineering ERP-9 register of
per-site determinations.
The ERP-9 register records, at minimum: the referral number, the receipt date, the Project ID, the site type
and feeder, the standards documents at issue, the assigned engineer, the determination date, and a short
summary of the determination. The register is reviewed by Standards Engineering quarterly for recurring
patterns; where a pattern warrants a standards revision proposal, Standards Engineering initiates that
revision separately from, and in parallel with, ongoing per-site determinations under this procedure. A
pending revision proposal does not stay determinations issued under this procedure and does not
authorize a screening hold on affected applications.
Determinations issued under ERP-9 are cited in the interconnection service agreement (ISA) drafted for
the affected site by reference to the ER-11 referral number and determination date. Modifications to the
site's protection arrangement subsequent to ISA execution are handled under the change-order provisions

Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
Doc no. POL-QM-05  ·  Rev 3  ·  Date 03/15/2025  ·  Owner: DER Program Office

Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy
Applies to:  All DER Interconnection Program applications (≥500 kW) administered by the DER Program Office.
Supersedes:  POL-QM-05 Rev 2 (07/12/2023).
Owner:  DER Program Office.
Approving Authority:  Manager, Interconnection Studies.

§1  Purpose
This policy sets out the internal procedures by which the DER Program Office administers queue integrity and orderly withdrawal of applications from the active DER interconnection queue. It is intended to ensure that:
(a)applications are closed only on a documented basis;
(b)queue positions are established, retained, and released in a manner consistent with the Company's APUC-filed interconnection tariff (in particular §12.3, §12.4, and §12.6) and with the DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01);
(c)staff processing intake, screening, and case-management actions apply a single, uniform standard when an application appears stalled, abandoned, superseded, or replaced by a subsequent filing at the same site; and
(d)the record supporting each queue action is complete and auditable.
Nothing in this policy modifies the tariff. Where any provision of this policy is read to conflict with the tariff or with an applicable engineering standard, the tariff and the standard control, and the conflict shall be referred to Regulatory Affairs for reconciliation.
§2  Withdrawal upon Customer Request
A stalled or abandoned application is closed only upon receipt of the customer's official withdrawal confirmation, provided in writing by letter or email. Where a new filing is submitted for the same site while a prior application remains open, the program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing; the new application takes its own queue date at time of filing. No queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§2.1  Scope of §2
This §2 governs closure of applications that have not been the subject of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under tariff §12.4. It applies where:
(a)the customer has ceased substantive engagement with the program (whether by prolonged non-response, express indication of intent not to proceed, or otherwise);
(b)the customer or an authorized developer has requested closure of an application without such a notice having issued; or
(c)a new application is filed for the same site (as identified by service address, meter, or point of common coupling) while a prior application for that site remains in the active queue.
§2.2  Form of the Withdrawal Confirmation
To constitute an “official withdrawal confirmation” for purposes of this §2, the writing must:
(a)be from the applicant of record (or from a person whose authority to act for the applicant has been established on the record — e.g., the developer named as the applicant's designated representative on the intake form);
(b)be received by the DER Program Office by letter or email, addressed to der.program@alleniom.com or delivered to the DER Program Office at the letterhead address above;
(c)identify the application by application identifier (PXA-YYYY-NNNN) and site; and
(d)state expressly that the applicant withdraws the identified application.
Neither an oral communication (telephone, meeting, or voicemail), nor a status note recorded by staff, nor the mere filing of a new application at the same site, shall by itself constitute the official withdrawal confirmation required under this §2.
§2.3  Procedure — Stalled or Abandoned Application (Non-Notice Path)
Where staff identify an application within the scope of §2.1(a) or §2.1(b), the case handler shall:
1.Confirm the application's status in the active queue and document the basis for concluding that the application is stalled or abandoned;
2.Prepare and send a written communication (letter or email) to the applicant of record requesting the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation in the form specified in §2.2;
3.Log the request in the case file and in the queue-management system;
4.On receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, close the application and record the closure date, the closure basis (“§2 — customer request”), and the reference to the writing on file; and
5.Preserve the withdrawal writing in the case file in accordance with §4.
Absent receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, the application shall not be closed under this §2. If the applicant does not provide the confirmation and non-response persists, the case handler may refer the matter for issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §3.
§2.4  Duplicate Filings at the Same Site
Where a new application is filed for the same site while a prior application for that site remains open in the queue:
(a)The DER Program Office shall accept the new application in the ordinary course and shall assign the new application its own queue date determined as of the date the new application is determined to be complete. No queue-date inheritance is permitted between the prior and the new application.
(b)The program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing in the form specified in §2.2. That request may be combined with the completeness/acknowledgement communication for the new application.
(c)The prior application shall remain open in the queue until the official withdrawal confirmation is received, or until the prior application is otherwise closed by operation of §3 or under another tariff mechanism. The two applications shall not be merged, consolidated, or treated as continuations of a single filing.
(d)Where the applicant states a preference or expectation that the earlier queue date apply to the new filing, staff shall respond in writing that the new application's queue date is fixed by §12.3 of the tariff and by this §2.4, and that closure of the prior application does not alter the queue date of the new application.
§2.5  Consistency with DIS-01 §7 and Tariff §12.6
Nothing in this §2 authorizes the use of a customer-requested withdrawal to reopen or amend an executed Interconnection Service Agreement. Post-execution changes to material terms of an ISA — including nameplate capacity and point of interconnection — require withdrawal-and-reapplication in accordance with DIS-01 §7 and tariff §12.6. A customer-requested withdrawal in that context establishes a new queue date for the successor application; no queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§3  Deemed Withdrawal (Procedural Restatement of Tariff §12.4)
Following issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation, if the applicant fails to respond within 30 business days, the application is deemed withdrawn.
§3.1  Relationship to the Tariff
This §3 is a procedural restatement, for internal use, of the deemed-withdrawal mechanism established by tariff §12.4. In the event of any inconsistency between this §3 and §12.4, the tariff controls. Staff shall consult §12.4 for the authoritative statement of the mechanism.
§3.2  Prerequisites to Issuance of a Notice
The DER Program Office shall not issue a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation unless:
(a)the application has been open in the queue and staff have been unable to advance it because of the applicant's non-response or failure to supply required information or documentation;
(b)at least one prior written follow-up has been sent to the applicant identifying the item or items required and requesting response by a stated date; and
(c)the case handler has confirmed that the matter does not fall within the construction-payment default procedure under tariff §12.5, which is a distinct mechanism (project on hold, not withdrawn, while a 30-business-day payment deadline runs).
§3.3  Form and Service of the Notice
Every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall:
(a)be issued in writing on Alleniom Utilities letterhead;
(b)be served by certified mail or by verified electronic delivery, in accordance with tariff §12.4;
(c)identify the application by identifier and site;
(d)state the item(s) requiring response;
(e)state the date of issuance and the date on which the 30 business-day response window expires, computed under §3.4; and
(f)state the consequence of non-response, i.e., that the application shall be deemed withdrawn and closed from the active queue without further action.
§3.4  Computation of 30 Business Days
For purposes of this §3 and of tariff §12.4:
(a)“Business days” excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and federal legal public holidays observed within the response window;
(b)Day 1 is the first business day after the date of issuance stated on the notice;
(c)The following federal holidays observed within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized as non-business days and are not counted:
Holiday | Observed Date
Memorial Day | 05/26/2025
Juneteenth National Independence Day | 06/19/2025
Independence Day | 07/04/2025


(d)Where a response window straddles a federal holiday not listed above, the case handler shall exclude that holiday from the count and document the calculation in the case file.
§3.5  Effect of Non-Response
If the applicant fails to submit a substantive response curing the matter identified in the notice within 30 business days computed under §3.4, the application shall be deemed withdrawn as of the day following expiration of the window. The DER Program Office shall:
(a)mark the application “deemed withdrawn — §12.4” in the queue-management system;
(b)record the notice-issuance date, the expiration date, and the closure date in the withdrawal-notice log; and
(c)preserve the notice, proof of service, and the closure entry in the case file in accordance with §4.
§3.6  Effect of Timely Response
A substantive response received on or before expiration of the 30 business-day window suspends the deemed-withdrawal consequence. The case handler shall evaluate the response and, if the identified matter is cured, release the application to resume processing. If the response is non-substantive or does not cure the identified matter, the case handler shall so document and, if warranted, issue a further follow-up or a subsequent Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation.
§3.7  Non-Substitution
Issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation is not a substitute for the customer-request path under §2, and the customer-request path under §2 is not a substitute for the deemed-withdrawal path under §3. Case handlers shall not use one mechanism to accomplish what should be effected under the other.
§4  Record-Keeping Requirements
§4.1  Case File Contents
For every application closed under §2 or §3, the DER Program Office shall maintain a case file containing, at minimum:
(a)the original application and all completeness/acknowledgement communications;
(b)for §2 closures: the writing (letter or email) requesting official withdrawal confirmation from the applicant; the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation (letter or email) as received; and any related correspondence bearing on the applicant's intent to withdraw;
(c)for §3 closures: the prior follow-up correspondence relied upon under §3.2(b); the Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation as issued; proof of service (certified mail receipt or verified electronic delivery record); the 30 business-day computation worksheet; and any response received;
(d)the queue-management system entry recording the closure basis, closure date, and (for §2 duplicate-filing cases) the queue-date determination applied to the successor application under §2.4(a); and
(e)any related engineering or standards correspondence relied upon in the closure decision.
§4.2  Queue-Management System Entries
Every closure shall be recorded in the queue-management system with:
(a)application identifier and site;
(b)closure basis, expressed as one of: “§2 — customer request (letter)”, “§2 — customer request (email)”, “§2.4 — superseded by successor application”, “§12.4 — deemed withdrawn”, or such other codes as the DER Program Office may prescribe;
(c)closure date;
(d)case handler; and
(e)reference to the writing(s) supporting the closure basis.

1. Purpose and decision summary
This package records the municipal-array determination that Standards Engineering requested
before the 08/15/2025 response to the Alleron Municipal League: which arrays remain in the
municipal commissioning batch, whether the inverter or power conversion equipment actually
installed at each array is carried on the current Certified Equipment List (CEL), and — for every
array that is not carried — the witness-test scope, the parties who perform and witness it, the
records that must be on file first, and a proposed schedule. It also identifies the array(s) the System
Operations Center (SOC) can be asked to release on the record as of 07/14/2025.
The determination is deliberately split into two questions. Carriage on the CEL is a Standards
Engineering eligibility question; whether to grant a waiver remains a Standards Engineering
disposition and is not made here. Release readiness is a separate gate: an array must be both
witness-clear and telemetry-live before the SOC can be asked to issue Permission to Operate (PTO).
Bottom line
     Five arrays remain in scope: Cravenwood High, Darnwick Elementary, Holcott Library,
      Lockmere Middle and Marden Falls WRF. Tresbay Community Center withdrew its request on
      07/09/2025 and is out of the batch.
     Two arrays are carried on CEL-2025-Q2: Cravenwood High (Solmery Power SM-215K-3P) and
      Marden Falls WRF (Solmery Power SM-245K-3P). Carriage call: YES for both.
     Three arrays are not carried: Darnwick Elementary (Arvexa PV-750 — absent from the current
      CEL), Holcott Library (Selvix SV-720 — only on the superseded CEL-2024-Q4) and Lockmere
      Middle (the inverter actually installed is a Selvix SV-720, not the Torvane TE-180K shown on the
      checklist). Carriage call: NO for all three.
     Witness tests are required for Darnwick, Holcott and Lockmere. Proposed dates are 07/24/2025,
      07/22/2025 and 07/29/2025 respectively, with reserves on 07/31/2025, 07/25/2025 and
      08/05/2025.
     Only Marden Falls is ready to be put to the SOC for release on 07/14/2025. It is carried on the
      current CEL and its checklist records telemetry complete. Standards Engineering must first sign
      the waiver, and the SOC must confirm live telemetry at the moment PTO is requested.
      Cravenwood is carried but its telemetry is still pending; Lockmere has live telemetry but
      requires a witness test; Darnwick and Holcott require both a witness test and telemetry.
     Three scheduling items stand on case WP45 — WP47 (Holcott), WP48 (Darnwick) and WP49
      (Lockmere). They exactly match the three arrays named in this package. WP45 was closed on
      07/14/2025 on that basis.
    As-of rule: The package is a record determination as of 07/14/2025. No document dated after that
    date has been used. The CEL edition in force on the eventual waiver signature date controls; if
    Standards Engineering signs after a successor CEL takes effect, the carriage lookup must be rerun
    against that edition before signature (ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §3, corollary 1).

2.3 Governing rule applied
ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §3 is the controlling rule. A witness-test waiver applies only to equipment
listed on the current CEL edition at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current edition
requires an on-site witness test before PTO. The corollaries applied here are:
  The waiver date is the date Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
   application, ISA or construction date.
 Every protective device and every inverter or power conversion system installed at the facility
   must appear on the current CEL edition; one unlisted component makes the facility ineligible.
 A listing that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor
   edition confers no eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
 Front-matter footnotes, cross-references and historical annotations in the current CEL are
   informational only; they do not extend eligibility to models not listed in the body.
 The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model listed when the
   application was filed but no longer listed on the waiver date requires the on-site witness test.
The current edition on 07/14/2025 is CEL-2025-Q2, published 04/30/2025. It supersedes CEL-2024-
Q4 (published 10/31/2024). The next scheduled edition is CEL-2025-Q3, planned for 07/31/2025; it
was not in force on the as-of date. The CEL body — not its front matter — is the listing reference
(ENG-PRC-014 §4.1).

Only Marden Falls is ready to be put to the SOC for release on 07/14/2025. It is carried on the current CEL and its checklist records telemetry complete. Standards Engineering must first sign the waiver, and the SOC must confirm live telemetry at the moment PTO is requested. Cravenwood is carried but its telemetry is still pending; Lockmere has live telemetry but requires a witness test; Darnwick and Holcott require both a witness test and telemetry.
ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §3 is the controlling rule. A witness-test waiver applies only to equipment listed on the current CEL edition at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current edition requires an on-site witness test before PTO. The corollaries applied here are:
Front-matter footnotes and historical annotations are informational only; they do not extend eligibility.
The determination must follow the equipment actually installed, not the checklist’s original entry (ENG-PRC-014 §4.1 requires the exact make and model installed; DIS-01 §3.3 requires classification on the facility as physically configured). Selvix SV-720 is not on CEL-2025-Q2; its only listing is the superseded CEL-2024-Q4 Inverters row 29. Lockmere therefore fails the carriage test, notwithstanding the TE-180K row. The checklist serials and as-built/O&M documentation must also be corrected: they currently describe four TE-180K units that are not the installed plant.
Consequence: no witness test is required on carriage grounds. Standards Engineering may proceed with the waiver disposition. Marden Falls is one of the two arrays in the batch (with Lockmere) whose checklist records live telemetry end-to-end with the SOC (telemetry provisioning row: “Pass — utility-owned RTU installed and provisioned; SCADA points verified end-to-end with SOC per TCS-02 §5”). Because Marden Falls is also carried, it is the only array that satisfies both the witness and telemetry gates and can be put to the SOC for release on 07/14/2025, subject to the signed waiver and the SOC’s live confirmation at the moment of PTO.
This section applies to Darnwick Elementary, Holcott Library and Lockmere Middle only. It follows ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §4.2: testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip tests, the anti-islanding test and the ride-through verifications. The site-specific test plan must cover each enabled protection function and the equipment actually installed.
Protection standards conflict. 3.1 Capacity Basis Statement (from Applicant)
The Applicant proposes to operate this DER facility at a Stated Capacity of 480 kW — export-limited
operation at the point of common coupling. Output is constrained through the on-site inverter fleet's
programmable power-control settings, which the Developer will configure at commissioning to cap
real-power delivery at the point of common coupling to the stated 480 kW value under all operating
conditions. On this basis the Applicant requests the Application be reviewed at the stated 480 kW figure.

4.1 Connection Description
The proposed PV system ties into the customer-owned side of the site's existing electrical service. Power
flow from the six commercial three-phase inverters (see the companion inverter datasheets file for per-unit
ratings) is aggregated at PVC-1, routed through the pad-mount lockable AC disconnect (PVD-1), and
lands on a new 800 A back-fed breaker in MDS-1. MDS-1 is fed from the plant's existing utility service
transformer through the site's existing 480 V main service disconnect and the existing utility revenue
meter.
The new PV interconnection is behind the existing service meter — the same point of common coupling
as the site's existing electrical service — on the load side of the utility revenue meter and upstream of the
warehouse's process and refrigeration load buses.
No new utility-side equipment, no new service transformer, no new service drop, and no separate revenue
meter is requested. The Applicant proposes to net the PV generation against warehouse load through the
existing bidirectional revenue meter of record and to hold export at the point of common coupling to the
Stated Capacity of 480 kW under all operating conditions.
Section 5 — Equipment Schedule
The proposed facility uses a fleet of commercial three-phase string inverters. Individual inverter nameplate
ratings, model-level specifications, and manufacturer certifications are provided in the companion file
Inverter Nameplate & Spec Sheets — PXA-2025-0231 (filed with this Application). The equipment
schedule below is a reference roster and does not restate the per-unit nameplate ratings recorded on

System Description
Rooftop-mounted photovoltaic generating facility connected behind the existing customer service meter at the Merrow
Creamery dairy processing plant. Array totals 800 kW nameplate AC, distributed across the north and south
production-building roof planes. Three-phase, 480 V output tied into the customer's existing 480 V main distribution
switchboard via a dedicated PV feeder breaker; no modifications to the utility service entrance conductors or the
revenue meter. Generation is intended to offset on-site process load; no export-focused equipment installed.

Inverters: 8 × 100 kW three-phase string inverters (UL 1741 listed; IEEE 1547 anti-islanding).
AC combining: 800 A PV subpanel feeding a 1,000 A PV feeder breaker in the existing 480 V main switchboard.
Point of common coupling: Load side of the existing utility service meter.

**From:** Corey Lindqvist <corey.lindqvist@hailbouysolar.com>
**To:** der.program@alleniom.com
**Date:** Tue, 08 Jul 2025 09:14:22 -0500
**Subject:** Harkwell Ridge — ISA capacity update request
**Cc:** Meera Vellanki <meera.vellanki@alleniom.com>

---

Program Office,

Following execution of the Interconnection Service Agreement on 07/03/2025 for Harkwell Ridge Solar (Application PXA-2024-0117) at 2.2 MW, Hailbouy Solar is writing to request that the executed ISA be updated to reflect a nameplate export capacity of 2.8 MW. Our preference — and, we believe, the only workable path given the project's construction and financing calendar — is to effect this change via a short addendum to the executed ISA.

Background and rationale:

- The ISA as executed on 07/03/2025 fixes capacity at 2.2 MW on Feeder ALN-042. Post-execution offtake refinements and updated production modeling from our EPC support a revised design point of 2.8 MW at the same point of interconnection.

- The equipment schedule and site plan are unchanged in configuration. The single-axis-tracker layout, module count per string, row geometry, inverter locations, MV collection topology, POI structure, and interconnection facilities scope on file with the DER Program Office are all as-approved. The delta is a firmware-level export setting and dc:ac ratio adjustment within the equipment already listed in the original application and reflected in the executed Interconnection Service Agreement.

- Because the physical configuration and POI are unchanged, no re-study should be needed. The prior system impact and facilities study work performed under PXA-2024-0117 remains the applicable technical basis, and a short capacity-only addendum executed against the existing ISA is the appropriate instrument to memorialize the update.

Requested action:

1. Please prepare an addendum to ISA-Harkwell-Ridge revising the Article 2 nameplate export capacity from 2.2 MW to 2.8 MW, with all other terms of the executed ISA to remain in full force and effect.

2. Please route the addendum for countersignature by end of week (07/11/2025). Our construction mobilization sequence, EPC commitment schedule, and tax-equity funding milestones are built around the 07/03/2025 execution and cannot tolerate slippage. Any process that reopens the study queue on this project is not viable for us on this timeline.

3. If the Program Office needs a supplemental technical memo from our engineer of record confirming that the equipment schedule and site plan are unchanged in configuration, we can have that in your hands by close of business 07/09/2025. Please advise by return email if this would expedite the addendum.

I would appreciate confirmation of receipt today and a target date for the addendum draft. Meera — copying you directly so Interconnection Studies has visibility; I understand the addendum sits with the contracts desk, but if there is anything on the studies side that needs a signoff to unblock the drafting please let me know today and we will accommodate.

Given the timing sensitivity, we consider expedited turnaround essential and are prepared to make our team available for a same-day call at Alleniom's convenience.

Regards,

Corey Lindqvist
Project Director
Hailbouy Solar
2200 Ridge Point Road, Suite 400
Halston, Alleron 03HA
(612) 817-0554

ISA-Harkwell-Ridge · Rev Final · Date 07/03/2025 · Owner: DER Program Office — Contracts\nAgreement No.: ISA-Harkwell-Ridge\nProject: Harkwell Ridge Solar\nApplication No.: PXA-2024-0117\nThis Interconnection Service Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into by and between Alleniom Utilities, an investor-owned electric utility organized under the laws of the State of Alleron, with principal offices at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA (EIN 36-4820917) (the “Company”), and Hailbouy Solar, with offices at 2200 Ridge Point Road, Suite 400, Halston, Alleron 03HA (the “Interconnection Customer”), each a “Party” and collectively the “Parties.” This Agreement is effective as of the date last executed below.\nRECITALS\nWHEREAS, the Interconnection Customer filed with the Company an application for interconnection service, designated PXA-2024-0117, on 06/17/2024, in respect of a 2.2 MW single-axis-tracker ground-mount photovoltaic generating facility known as facilities studies for the Facility in accordance with the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4, and issued a final study determination approving the Facility for execution of an Interconnection Service Agreement at the capacity and point of interconnection described in the application as filed;\nWHEREAS, the Company's tariff, as filed with and approved by the Alleron Public Utilities Commission, governs the interconnection of distributed energy resources of the Facility's class and forms an integral part of the terms and conditions of interconnection service provided hereunder;\nWHEREAS, the Parties intend by this Agreement to establish the terms, conditions, rights and obligations under which the Facility will be permitted to parallel with, and export energy to, the Company's distribution system;\nNOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and undertakings set forth herein, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:\nARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS\n1.1 Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Company's filed tariff (the “Tariff”) and in the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4 (the “DIS”).\n1.2 For the purposes of this Agreement, and without limitation of the foregoing:\n“Facility” means the generating equipment, ancillary equipment, and all interconnection facilities described in Article 2 hereof.\n“Point of Interconnection” or “POI” means the physical point at which the Facility is electrically connected to the Company's distribution system, as identified in Article 2.\n“Standards” means the standards and specifications identified in Article 4, each as in effect on the Effective Date and as such may be amended, superseded, or reissued by the Company in accordance with its ordinary regulatory practice.\n“Effective Date” has the meaning given in Article 3.\n“Certified Equipment List” or “CEL” means the Company's then-current Certified Equipment List published by Standards Engineering.\nARTICLE 2 — DESCRIPTION OF FACILITY\n2.1 Project designation. Harkwell Ridge Solar (Application PXA-2024-0117).\n2.2 Interconnection Customer. Hailbouy Solar.\n2.3 Facility technology. Photovoltaic generation, single-axis-tracker ground-mount configuration.\n2.4 Nameplate export capacity. 2.2 MW (AC) at the Point of Interconnection.\n2.5 Point of Interconnection (POI). A three-phase primary tap on Feeder ALN-042, at the pole FKDN54D.\n2.6 Point of Common Coupling (PCC). Coincident with the Point of Interconnection identified in Section 2.5.\n2.7 Material terms. The capacity, technology, and Point of Interconnection stated in this Article are material terms of this Agreement.\nARTICLE 3 — TERM AND EFFECTIVE DATE\n3.1 Effective Date. This Agreement is effective as of 07/03/2025 (the “Effective Date”), being the date on which the last of the two Parties has executed this Agreement.\n3.2 Term. This Agreement shall remain in full force and effect from the Effective Date until terminated in accordance with its terms or superseded by a successor agreement between the Parties.\n3.3 Continuing obligations. The obligations of the Parties in respect of indemnity, limitation of liability, confidentiality, and dispute resolution shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement.\nARTICLE 4 — INTERCONNECTION STANDARDS\n4.1 Governing standards. The Facility shall at all times be designed, constructed, commissioned, operated, and maintained in conformity with the following Company standards and any successor or superseding editions thereof:\n(a) DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard (effective 03/01/2024);\n(b) DPS-07 Rev 2 — Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023);\n(c) TCS-02 — Telemetry and Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021); and\n(d) CEL-2025-Q2 — Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025), as such may be superseded from time to time.\n4.2 Order of precedence. In the event of any inconsistency among the documents constituting this Agreement, the following order of precedence shall govern: (i) the Tariff; (ii) the applicable Company Standards enumerated in Section 4.1; (iii) the body of this Agreement.\n4.3 Compliance with successor standards. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to relieve the Interconnection Customer from the obligation to conform the Facility to successor or superseding editions of the Standards as and when they take effect, in accordance with the transition provisions of the applicable Standard.\nARTICLE 5 — METERING AND TELEMETRY\n5.1 Metering. Revenue-quality metering shall be provided at the Point of Interconnection in accordance with the Tariff and the Company's metering specifications. Meters shall be owned, installed, tested, and maintained by the Company at the Interconnection Customer's cost, and shall be sealed at all times.\n5.2 Telemetry. In accordance with TCS-02 §5, the Interconnection Customer shall install, at its cost, provisions for a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) and shall make available all analog and binary status DNP3 points required by the Company's Telemetry and Communications Standard, together with such communication paths and standing-power provisions as the Company requires for SCADA integration.\n5.3 Commissioning of monitoring and control. Satisfactory commissioning and continuous availability of the telemetry described in Section 5.2 are conditions precedent to Permission to Operate. INTERCONNECTION SERVICE AGREEMENT
Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
Doc no. ISA-Harkwell-Ridge · Rev Final · Date 07/03/2025 · Owner: DER Program Office — Contracts
Agreement No.: ISA-Harkwell-Ridge
Project: Harkwell Ridge Solar
Application No.: PXA-2024-0117
This Interconnection Service Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into by and between Alleniom Utilities, an investor-owned electric utility organized under the laws of the State of Alleron, with principal offices at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA (EIN 36-4820917) (the “Company”), and Hailbouy Solar, with offices at 2200 Ridge Point Road, Suite 400, Halston, Alleron 03HA (the “Interconnection Customer”), each a “Party” and collectively the “Parties.” This Agreement is effective as of the date last executed below.
RECITALS
WHEREAS, the Interconnection Customer filed with the Company an application for interconnection service, designated PXA-2024-0117, on 06/17/2024, in respect of a 2.2 MW single-axis-tracker ground-mount photovoltaic generating facility known as Harkwell Ridge Solar (the “Facility”), to be interconnected to the Company's distribution system at a point on Feeder ALN-042;
WHEREAS, the Company completed technical screening, system impact and facilities studies for the Facility in accordance with the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4, and issued a final study determination approving the Facility for execution of an Interconnection Service Agreement at the capacity and point of interconnection described in the application as filed;
WHEREAS, the Company's tariff, as filed with and approved by the Alleron Public Utilities Commission, governs the interconnection of distributed energy resources of the Facility's class and forms an integral part of the terms and conditions of interconnection service provided hereunder;
WHEREAS, the Parties intend by this Agreement to establish the terms, conditions, rights and obligations under which the Facility will be permitted to parallel with, and export energy to, the Company's distribution system;
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and undertakings set forth herein, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS
1.1 Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Company's filed tariff (the “Tariff”) and in the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4 (the “DIS”).
1.2 For the purposes of this Agreement, and without limitation of the foregoing:
“Facility” means the generating equipment, ancillary equipment, and all interconnection facilities described in Article 2 hereof.
“Point of Interconnection” or “POI” means the physical point at which the Facility is electrically connected to the Company's distribution system, as identified in Article 2.
“Standards” means the standards and specifications identified in Article 4, each as in effect on the Effective Date and as such may be amended, superseded, or reissued by the Company in accordance with its ordinary regulatory practice.
“Effective Date” has the meaning given in Article 3.
“Certified Equipment List” or “CEL” means the Company's then-current Certified Equipment List published by Standards Engineering.
ARTICLE 2 — DESCRIPTION OF FACILITY
2.1 Project designation. Harkwell Ridge Solar (Application PXA-2024-0117).
2.2 Interconnection Customer. Hailbouy Solar.
2.3 Facility technology. Photovoltaic generation, single-axis-tracker ground-mount configuration.
2.4 Nameplate export capacity. 2.2 MW (AC) at the Point of Interconnection.
2.5 Point of Interconnection (POI). A three-phase primary tap on Feeder ALN-042, at the pole FKDN54D.
2.6 Point of Common Coupling (PCC). Coincident with the Point of Interconnection identified in Section 2.5.
2.7 Material terms. The capacity, technology, and Point of Interconnection stated in this Article are material terms of this Agreement.
ARTICLE 3 — TERM AND EFFECTIVE DATE
3.1 Effective Date. This Agreement is effective as of 07/03/2025 (the “Effective Date”), being the date on which the last of the two Parties has executed this Agreement.
3.2 Term. This Agreement shall remain in full force and effect from the Effective Date until terminated in accordance with its terms or superseded by a successor agreement between the Parties.
3.3 Continuing obligations. The obligations of the Parties in respect of indemnity, limitation of liability, confidentiality, and dispute resolution shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement.
ARTICLE 4 — INTERCONNECTION STANDARDS
4.1 Governing standards. The Facility shall at all times be designed, constructed, commissioned, operated, and maintained in conformity with the following Company standards and any successor or superseding editions thereof:
(a) DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard (effective 03/01/2024);
(b) DPS-07 Rev 2 — Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023);
(c) TCS-02 — Telemetry and Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021); and
(d) CEL-2025-Q2 — Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025), as such may be superseded from time to time.
4.2 Order of precedence. In the event of any inconsistency among the documents constituting this Agreement, the following order of precedence shall govern: (i) the Tariff; (ii) the applicable Company Standards enumerated in Section 4.1; (iii) the body of this Agreement.
4.3 Compliance with successor standards. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to relieve the Interconnection Customer from the obligation to conform the Facility to successor or superseding editions of the Standards as and when they take effect, in accordance with the transition provisions of the applicable Standard.
ARTICLE 5 — METERING AND TELEMETRY
5.1 Metering. Revenue-quality metering shall be provided at the Point of Interconnection in accordance with the Tariff and the Company's metering specifications. Meters shall be owned, installed, tested, and maintained by the Company at the Interconnection Customer's cost, and shall be sealed at all times.
5.2 Telemetry. In accordance with TCS-02 §5, the Interconnection Customer shall install, at its cost, provisions for a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) and shall make available all analog and binary status DNP3 points required by the Company's Telemetry and Communications Standard, together with such communication paths and standing-power provisions as the Company requires for SCADA integration.
5.3 Commissioning of monitoring and control. Satisfactory commissioning and continuous availability of the telemetry described in Section 5.2 are conditions precedent to Permission to Operate. The Facility shall not be paralleled with the Company's distribution system in the absence of live utility telemetry, and any loss of telemetry after Permission to Operate shall be reported and remediated as provided in TCS-02.
5.4 Data and access rights. The Interconnection Customer grants the Company such rights of access to the Facility, and such rights to receive and use metering and telemetry data, as are necessary for the Company to discharge its obligations under the Tariff and applicable Standards.
ARTICLE 6 — PAYMENT TERMS
6.1 Construction work order. The Interconnection Customer shall pay the Company for the construction of upgrades and interconnection facilities in accordance with the construction work order issued under this Agreement, on the schedule and in the amounts set forth therein, and in accordance with Tariff §12.5.
6.2 Invoicing. Invoices shall be issued by the Company and shall be due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the invoice date, unless otherwise expressly provided in the construction work order. Amounts not paid when due shall bear interest at the rate set forth in the Tariff.
6.3 Payment default. In the event of non-payment, the Company shall provide the Interconnection Customer written notice and a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days in accordance with Tariff §12.5. Business days exclude weekends and federal holidays. During the pendency of any such deadline the Facility shall remain subject to any construction or commissioning hold ordered by the Company.
6.4 Ongoing operational charges. All charges, credits, and settlements applicable to interconnection service and associated ancillary services shall be as set forth in the Tariff.
ARTICLE 7 — AME

SUBJECT:	Backlog Review — Commercial DER Interconnection Program

Effective immediately, I am ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. The scope covers the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population — every application currently sitting in the program queue. I want each one accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action.
