**From:** Rosa Camarena <rosa.camarena@brookfenusd.org>
**To:** der.program@alleniom.com
**Date:** Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:42:18 -0500
**Subject:** Urgent: school array energization priority
**Cc:** Dana Whitcomb <dana.whitcomb@alleniom.com>, Harriet Ngoyi <harriet.ngoyi@alleniom.com>

---

To the DER Program Office:

I am writing again — and I want to be direct about the fact that this is not the first, second, or third time I have raised this with your office — to ask for a firm answer on when Alleniom Utilities intends to energize the two solar arrays serving Brookfen Unified School District. This message is dated 06/30/2025 and I would like a written response before the end of next week.

The two arrays in question, and their status on our side, are as follows:

  • Brookfen North High School Array — 720 kW. Construction was declared complete by our contractor on 04/18/2025. The local electrical inspector closed out the installation the same week. The system has been standing idle, energized-ready, for more than ten weeks.

  • Brookfen West Elementary Array — 640 kW. Construction was declared complete on 05/23/2025. Inspection was closed out shortly thereafter. This system has now been standing idle for over a month.

Neither array has been energized. Neither array has a firm energization date on record with the District. Each time our office contacts your program inbox we are told that a component — variously described as a "telemetry unit" or an "RTU" — has not yet been delivered by your supplier, and that we are somewhere in a queue behind other sites. What we have never been given, in writing, is the position of our sites in that queue, the identity of the sites ahead of us, or the basis on which those sites are being served ahead of ours.

I have to tell you plainly that the patience of the Brookfen school board and the District's superintendent is exhausted. The 2025–2026 school year begins for our students on 08/26/2025. Both of these arrays were financed, in significant part, on the strength of first-year operating-cost savings that were built into the District's adopted budget for that same school year and presented to our board and to the community at public meetings. Every additional week that these systems sit dark is a week of budgeted savings the District will not realize and will have to explain to the board, to our parents, and to the taxpayers of Brookfen who approved the underlying bond measure. Our high school's building-systems curriculum was also structured around students being able to observe the array in operation from the beginning of the term; that piece of the school year is now at risk of slipping into the second semester or being cut altogether.

You will by now have received the Alleron Municipal League's letter of 06/20/2025, signed by Executive Director Alden Pryce, escalating this same set of concerns on behalf of the District and thirteen other League members. Brookfen USD is one of the members named in that letter and stands fully behind the requests it contains. This message is not a substitute for the League's letter; it is intended to make the District's individual position, and the specifics of our two sites, unmistakable to your office.

What I am asking for, directly, is this: in the next allocation of the equipment your program office is holding up as the constraint — the RTU / telemetry units your staff have referenced in prior calls — I am asking Alleniom Utilities to advance the District's two waiting arrays ahead of the other sites presently competing for those units. Brookfen North completed construction on 04/18/2025 and Brookfen West on 05/23/2025. Both are public school facilities. Both have children returning to the building in eight weeks. Neither array can wait for a second or third delivery cycle without meaningful harm to the District's fiscal position and to the educational program these systems were installed to support.

If there is a formal process for requesting that our two sites be advanced in your next equipment allocation, please tell me what that process is and I will follow it today. If there is not, please treat this message as our written request under whatever mechanism your program uses to weigh these decisions, and please confirm receipt.

I am copying Ms. Whitcomb and Ms. Ngoyi so that this request is on the record with senior distribution operations and regulatory affairs, and so that no one at your program office is later in a position to say the District did not put this in writing in time.

I would like a written reply — not a call-back, a written reply — by close of business Friday, 07/11/2025. Silence past that date will require the District to raise this matter again through the League and, if necessary, directly with the Commission's Energy Resources Division, whose staff we understand is already tracking this program.

I am available at (612) 448-0311 during District business hours if it would help to talk any of this through. I would strongly prefer to resolve it with your office.

Regards,

Rosa Camarena
Facilities Director
Brookfen Unified School District
1725 Grantway Drive, Brookfen, Alleron 12BR
(612) 448-0311

Alleniom Utilities — Regulatory Affairs
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
TO: DER Program Manager
CC: Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations
Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
FROM: Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
DATE: 07/01/2025
SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking
1. Confirmation of directive
This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
4. Reporting cadence
The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.
Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
5. General provisions
Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as written. Standards or procedural conflicts route through the established referral process; they are not to be resolved informally in the queue. Queue-date treatment must remain within what the tariff and program policy permit.
Regulatory Affairs will coordinate with Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki) on queue and notice records, and with the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham) on study status, on any input required for the League response or the APUC briefing. The DER Program Manager remains the single point of accountability for the queue-cleanup inputs enumerated in §3.
Escalate obstacles to Regulatory Affairs in writing and, where the obstacle bears on the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates, to the VP office concurrently.
/s/
Harriet Ngoyi
Director, Regulatory Affairs
Alleniom Utilities

ALLERON PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION
Energy Resources Division
Docket:  APUC-2025-ER-014
Ref:  ERD-IR-2025-07-014
Date:  07/07/2025
Ms. Harriet Ngoyi
Director, Regulatory Affairs
Alleniom Utilities
Re:  APUC Information Request — Alleniom Utilities DER Interconnection Program Backlog
Docket APUC-2025-ER-014
Dear Ms. Ngoyi:
The Energy Resources Division of the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC) is in receipt of
correspondence from the Alleron Municipal League dated 06/20/2025 (AML Ref:
AML-2025-0620-DER), copied to the Division, escalating on behalf of fourteen member municipalities
and school districts a program-level concern with the current pace of commercial-scale Distributed
Energy Resource (DER) interconnection processing on the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The
League's letter identifies delays affecting projects at public schools, municipal water and wastewater
facilities, community centers, and public libraries across multiple communities within the Company's
service territory, and raises questions regarding queue status, hold posture, and expected energization
timelines that fall within the Division's continuing oversight of the Company's APUC-filed
interconnection tariff.
The Division intends to be in a position to brief the Commission on the matter at the previously
scheduled DER program briefing on 09/10/2025. In advance of that briefing, and to permit the Division
to assess the Company's DER interconnection program on the basis of the Company's own records
rather than the League's characterization, this letter requests the following information from Alleniom
Utilities.
1.  Commercial DER queue accounting.
For the commercial DER interconnection program (i.e., the ≥500 kW program-scope portfolio
administered by the Company's DER Program Office; simplified small-systems process filings are
outside the scope of this request), the Company is requested to provide a complete queue accounting as
of the most recent full week preceding the response date, including at minimum the following,
presented at the individual-application level and separately summarized in totals:
a.  The count and identity of all applications currently in active processing status, together with each
application's assigned application number, applicant name, site, nameplate capacity, filing date,
current processing step, and the study or decision milestone next due.
One Capitol Plaza, Suite 900  ·  Cordwyn, Alleron 14CW  ·  (651) 555-0180  ·  apuc.alleron.gov
Halston, Alleron 01HA
4200 Veldmere Boulevard

---

b.  The count and identity of all applications currently on on-hold, pending-customer,
pending-standards, or suspended status, together with the specific hold reason of record for
each, the party responsible for the next action, the information or resource required to release the
hold, and the date the hold was established.
c.  The count and identity of all applications for which one or more study or processing timelines
established under the Company's filed interconnection tariff, procedures, or executed study
agreements have been exceeded as of the reporting date, together with the timeline of record, the
actual elapsed time, and the current cause of the overrun.
d.  The count and identity of all applications withdrawn — whether by written applicant request, by
application of the tariff's deemed-withdrawal provision, or otherwise — during the twelve
months preceding the reporting date, together with the effective date of each withdrawal and the
recorded basis for it.
e.  The count and identity of all formal Notices of Impending Withdrawal, Notices of
Cancellation, or equivalent written notices issued by the Company to applicants during the
twelve months preceding the reporting date, together with the notice date, the date sent, the
method of service, the response deadline computed under the tariff, and the current disposition
(response received / no response / deemed withdrawn / other).
Where any of the foregoing counts is materially affected by data-integrity items known to the Company
requested to identify those items and provide the counts both as they presently appear in the Company's
queue records and as the Company understands the underlying facts to be.
2.  Backlog-cause summary.
The Company is further requested to provide a written summary describing, in the Company's own
characterization, the principal causes of the current backlog in the commercial DER interconnection
program. The summary should address at a minimum: application volume relative to processing
capacity; the availability and lead time of utility-owned equipment required for energization (including
but not limited to RTU and protection equipment); the status of any internal standards reconciliation
activity affecting screening or protection determinations; the sufficiency of certified-equipment
references relied upon by the Company; the sufficiency of hosting-capacity information made available
to prospective applicants; and any other factors the Company identifies as materially contributing to the
current queue posture. Supporting quantitative material (equipment delivery schedules, staffing
utilization, study cycle times, and the like) is welcome and, where practicable, requested.
3.  Format and timing.
Responses should be provided in writing, addressed to the undersigned at the Division's Cordwyn
office, with electronic copies to the docket. Line-item responses under Item 1 above may be provided
by workbook attachment provided each attachment is unambiguously cross-referenced to the
corresponding item. Responses should be received by the Division sufficiently in advance of the
09/10/2025 briefing to allow the Division adequate review; the Division requests that the Company
provide its response no later than 08/22/2025, and, where any portion of the response cannot be
furnished by that date, that the Company so advise the Division in writing no later than 08/08/2025 with
an explanation and a proposed alternative date.
4.  Continuing dialogue.
(for example, timing differences, reconciliation items, or other known data-quality issues), the Company is

---

This request is issued in the ordinary course of the Division's monitoring of interconnection program
performance under the Company's APUC-filed tariff. The Division has no present view as to the merits
of the underlying matter and takes no position on the specific project-level concerns raised in the
League's 06/20/2025 letter, which remain properly a matter between the League's member entities and
the Company in the first instance. The Division's interest at this stage is limited to the queue accounting
and backlog-cause information described above, together with the Company's plan for restoring
predictable processing to the program. The Division remains available to discuss scope, format, or
timing questions at Company request.
The Division appreciates the Company's continued cooperation and looks forward to the Company's
response.
Sincerely,
Nia Fairweather
Nia Fairweather
Director, Energy Resources Division

Feeder ALN-108 Planning Study — Post-Publication Update Q3 2024
Alleniom Utilities — Distribution Planning
DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
Doc no. PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 · Rev 1 · Date 10/15/2024 · Owner: Distribution Planning
Prepared by: June Halloway, Distribution Planning Engineer
Contact: june.halloway@alleniom.com
1. Purpose
This memorandum constitutes an interim update to the published Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map (HCM-2024-Q2, published 05/15/2024) with respect to Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine substation, 13.2 kV, pure-generation category). It is issued between scheduled quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map to record a material queue addition on the subject feeder that has occurred since the last published map release, so that Distribution Planning staff, applicant-facing correspondence, and pre-application dialogue may be informed of a working interim figure until the next full refresh cycle.
The scope of this document is limited to Feeder ALN-108. It does not modify the published values shown on any other feeder in HCM-2024-Q2, nor does it substitute for a formal feeder-level planning study in support of any specific interconnection application. Applicants and pre-application requesters seeking definitive feeder guidance for project scoping decisions should continue to consult Distribution Planning directly, and any project of consequential size on Feeder ALN-108 will require a full feeder-level planning study following the standard Alleniom Distribution Planning methodology.
2. Baseline: Published Available Capacity
The Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map was published on 05/15/2024. The map reflects, on a per-feeder basis, the published available capacity value derived from the most recent completed planning study of record for each feeder as of the publication date, incorporating recorded peak and minimum load, existing interconnected DER of record at the time of the underlying study, and standard thermal, voltage, and protection screens.
For Feeder ALN-108, the published values on HCM-2024-Q2 are as follows:
The 3.0 MW figure shown above is the baseline against which subsequent queue activity is netted for the purposes of this interim update. It remains, until the next scheduled quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map or an intervening full feeder re-study, the sole published available capacity of record for Feeder ALN-108.
3. Post-Publication Queue Activity
Distribution Planning has reviewed the Active Queue Report as of the date of this document to identify interconnection applications assigned to Feeder ALN-108 that have been queued subsequent to publication of the Hosting Capacity Map. The following post-publication queue entry has been identified on Feeder ALN-108:
The 1.2 MW project queued on 09/18/2024 is a pure-generation interconnection request, consistent with the DER category assigned to the feeder in HCM-2024-Q2. It represents the sole queue addition on Feeder ALN-108 identified in the Active Queue Report between the publication date of the map (05/15/2024) and the date of this study.
No other pending applications, executed interconnection service agreements, or in-service DER additions on Feeder ALN-108 have been identified since publication of HCM-2024-Q2 that would materially alter the baseline figure or the interim netted position stated below.
4. Interim Netted Figure
Applying the post-publication queue entry identified in Section 3 against the published available capacity of record stated in Section 2, the interim netted available capacity figure for Feeder ALN-108 as of the date of this document is calculated as follows:
Interim available capacity: 3.0 MW − 1.2 MW = 1.8 MW.
This interim figure is provided as a working reference for Distribution Planning staff and for use in pre-application correspondence concerning Feeder ALN-108 where such correspondence is issued between quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map. The figure is not a substitute for, and does not supersede, the published available capacity value of record on HCM-2024-Q2; the published value remains 3.0 MW until the next map republication.
The interim figure carries the following stated limitations:
It reflects the state of the queue as of the date of this document only. Any subsequent queue additions, withdrawals, or reassignments affecting Feeder ALN-108 that post-date this study are not reflected in the figure above and will require Distribution Planning to reassess the interim position accordingly.
It applies a straight-line nameplate netting against the published available capacity. A full feeder re-study, when performed, may yield a different available capacity value on Feeder ALN-108 depending on updated load recordings, revised existing-DER accounting, and the outcome of thermal, voltage, and protection screens as re-run against current data.
The 1.2 MW queue entry is at the application/queue stage. Should that application be withdrawn or should its final capacity change following study or agreement negotiation, the interim netted figure would require corresponding adjustment.
5. Recommendation
Distribution Planning recommends the following:
Distribution Planning staff should treat 1.8 MW as the working interim available capacity for Feeder ALN-108 in any pre-application dialogue, applicant correspondence, or internal scoping analysis conducted between the date of this document and the next scheduled refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. The published 3.0 MW figure on HCM-2024-Q2 remains the value of record for the map itself and should not be altered on the published map absent republication.
A refreshed feeder-level planning study for Feeder ALN-108 should be scheduled to be undertaken in advance of, and its results incorporated into, the next full quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. Feeder ALN-108 should be included among the feeders prioritized for re-study on the criteria stated in the map front matter: application date of pending queue entries, capacity requested relative to published available headroom, and DER category (pure generation is weighted more heavily against feeder headroom than net-metering behind-the-meter interconnections at equivalent nameplate).
This document should be reissued or superseded if any further queue activity on Feeder ALN-108 arises before the next quarterly map refresh, so that the working interim figure remains accurate as of its date of issue. Distribution Planning will monitor the Active Queue Report accordingly.
Applicants inquiring about Feeder ALN-108 between the date of this document and the next scheduled map republication should be directed to Distribution Planning for confirmation of the interim position before finalizing project sizing decisions, consistent with the general applicability note carried in the front matter of HCM-2024-Q2.

data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":196,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"success\":true,\"page\":{\"id\":41,\"path\":\"der-program/standards/dis-01-rev4-der-interconnection-standard\",\"title\":\"DIS-01 Rev4 DER Interconnection Standard\",\"description\":\"Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard Rev 4 effective 03/01/2024 based on IEEE 1547-2018\",\"content\":\"# DIS-01 Rev4 DER Interconnection Standard\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard\\nPage 1\\nALLENIOM UTILITIES\\nDER INTERCONNECTION STANDARD\\nDoc no.\\nRev\\nEffective date\\nOwner\\nDIS-01\\nRev 4\\n03/01/2024\\nAlleniom Standards Engineering — Evan Solberg\\nDocument control\\nItem\\nValue\\nDocument number\\nDIS-01\\nRevision\\nRev 4\\nEffective date\\n03/01/2024\\nSupersedes\\nDIS-01 Rev 3 (12/01/2021)\\nBasis\\nIEEE 1547-2018\\nOwner\\nAlleniom Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)\\nApproved by\\nManager, Standards Engineering\\nDistribution\\nAlleniom DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; DER Planning Group;\\nSCADA/EMS Engineering; Regulatory Affairs; contracted developers on request\\nNext scheduled review\\n03/01/2027\\nRevision history\\nRev\\nDate\\nSummary\\nRev 1\\n06/01/2016\\nInitial issue.\\nRev 2\\n09/01/2018\\nAlignment with IEEE 1547-2018. Introduced Category 1/2/3 protective-equipment table.\\nRev 3\\n12/01/2021\\nProgram-scope threshold set at 500 kW; added §3.4 aggregation.\\nRev 4\\n03/01/2024\\nAdded §3.5 shared-POI eligibility; added §3.6 controlled-capacity recognition (UL 1741 / UL\\n3141 PCS + Control Narrative); §7 restated to require withdrawal and reapplication for\\npost-execution capacity or POI changes; Table 5-1 rewritten by category.\\n§1 Purpose and Scope\\nThis standard establishes the technical and procedural requirements for interconnection of distributed energy\\nresources (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. It is based on IEEE 1547-2018 and applicable state\\ninterconnection rules filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC), and it applies to all DER classes\\ndefined in §3.\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 governs:\\n classification of DER facilities by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling (§3);\\n eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);\\n recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);\\n protective and control equipment requirements by class and category (§5);\\n\\n\\n---\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard Page 2\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024\\n treatment of post-execution changes to executed interconnection service agreements (§7).\\nThis standard is read together with the APUC-filed interconnection tariff (§12). Where a topic is addressed by both\\nthis standard and the tariff, the tariff controls. Requirements for real-time monitoring and communications integration\\nare established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.\\n§2 References\\nThe following documents are referenced within this standard. Unless otherwise noted, the latest published revision\\napplies.\\n IEEE 1547-2018 — IEEE Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources\\nwith Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.\\n DPS-07 Rev 2 — Alleniom Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023). Establishes distribution\\nprotection requirements including protective devices at points of interconnection with export-capable in-scope\\nfacilities.\\n TCS-02 — Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021). Governs utility-owned RTU\\ninstallation and SCADA telemetry for DER at and above the program-scope threshold; establishes the condition\\nfor permission to operate.\\n CEL-2025-Q2 — Alleniom Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025). Listing basis: UL 1741-SB and UL\\n3141. The CEL front matter restates §3.6 of this standard.\\n ERP-9 — Alleniom Engineering Referral Procedure (Form ER-11). §3 routes any standards \\n§3 DER Classification\\nDER facilities are classified by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling, in accordance with\\nIEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.\\nCommercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW; medium-scale 1 MW–5 MW; program scope ≥500 kW; sub-500 kW DER\\n(commercial and residential) is handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process, outside the DER Program.\\nDefinitions of terms used in this standard follow IEEE 1547-2018 and, where applicable, the definitions in the\\nAPUC-filed tariff. The terms aggregate nameplate capacity and point of common coupling (PCC) have the meanings\\nassigned by IEEE 1547-2018 and reflected in Company practice. The terms point of interconnection (POI),\\nexport-capable, and pure-generation site are used in accordance with their ordinary meaning in utility\\ninterconnection practice.\\n\\n---\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard\\nPage 3\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024\\nTable 3-1 — DER classes\\nClass\\nAggregate\\nnameplate at PCC\\nProgram status\\nReview path\\nProtective\\nequipment\\nreference\\nResidential / small\\ncommercial\\n< 500 kW\\nSimplified Small-Systems\\nProcess — outside the\\nDER Program\\nSimplified small-systems\\nscreening\\nTable 5-1, Category\\n1\\nCommercial small-scale\\n500 kW – 1 MW\\nIn DER Program scope\\nInitial screening +\\nsupplemental review under\\nSRP-3\\nTable 5-1, Category\\n2\\nMedium-scale\\n1 MW – 5 MW\\nIn DER Program scope\\nInitial screening + system\\nimpact study\\nTable 5-1, Category\\n3\\nLarge-scale (out of scope\\nfor this standard)\\n> 5 MW\\nHandled under transmissio\\nn-interconnection\\nprocedures\\nFull study process\\nNot addressed\\nThe program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer\\nclass, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.\\n§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity\\nAggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment\\ninterconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets\\ngovern; derated or \\\"operating\\\" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.\\n§3.2 Point of common coupling\\nThe point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's\\ndistribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),\\nthe latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.\\n§3.3 Determination on the basis of application\\nClassification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,\\nand cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and\\nthe address of record govern.\\n§3.4 Aggregation\\nCo-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.\\nPreviously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission\\nto operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form\\nin which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the\\nresulting program-scope determination.\\nAn applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the\\napplication form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,\\nthe existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against\\nthe Company existing-DER register.\\n§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility\\nA new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought\\nto current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the\\nexisting system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its\\nown service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.\\n\\n\\n---\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard\\nPage 4\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024\\nThe two dispositions available under §3.5 are:\\n1.  Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to\\ncurrent monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The\\napplicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where\\nfeasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.\\n2.  Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind\\nthe meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and\\nits own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.\\nClass placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.\\nRetrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the\\napplicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path\\nunder §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.\\n§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition\\nA limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control\\nNarrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the\\nrecognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI\\n32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.\\nRequired submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for\\nprogram-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:\\n1.  A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where\\napplicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the\\nsetpoint range.\\n2.  An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system\\nenforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response\\ntimes, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.\\nThese two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.\\nRecognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.\\nEnforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the\\nrecognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:\\n Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry\\nmonitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation\\ntriggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.\\n POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which\\nno customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per\\nTable 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips\\nthe site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require\\nadditional utility hardware.\\nEnforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does\\nnot reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.\\nNo controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and\\nan approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.\\nCertified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL\\ndoes not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific\\ncertification and Control Narrative are always required.\\n\\n\\n---\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard Page 5\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024\\n§4 Screening and Study Process\\nApplications in DER Program scope proceed through initial technical screening under Interconnection Studies.\\nFacilities not passing initial screens may be evaluated under supplemental review per SRP-3 or advance to a system\\nimpact study. This standard does not restate SRP-3; the daytime minimum-load convention and other screen\\nmethodologies are prescribed there.\\n§5 Protective and Control Equipment\\nProtective equipment requirements are stated by category in Table 5-1, keyed to the classes of §3.\\nTable 5-1 — Protective equipment by category\\nItem Category 1 (< 500 kW) Category 2 (500 kW – 1 MW\\nexport sites)\\nCategory 3 (1 MW – 5 MW\\nexport sites)\\nApplicable class Residential / small\\ncommercial\\nCommercial small-scale Medium-scale\\nDER-side disconnect Required (customer-owned\\nlockable visible-break)\\nRequired (customer-owned\\nlockable visible-break)\\nRequired (customer-owned\\nlockable visible-break)\\nInterconnection protective\\nfunctions (IEEE 1547-2018\\nclause 4)\\nProvided by certified inverterProvided by certified inverter\\nand/or dedicated protection\\nrelay\\nDedicated protection relay\\nrequired\\nDER breaker with protection\\nrelay scheme (for\\nload/generation-decoupling\\narrangements)\\nNot required As specified per site by\\nprotection engineering\\nAs specified per site by\\nprotection engineering\\nPOI recloser (utility-owned)Not required Category 2 export sites —\\nPOI recloser: not required\\nRequired\\nAnti-islanding Certified inverter functions\\nper IEEE 1547-2018\\nCertified inverter functions per\\nIEEE 1547-2018;\\nsupplemented by relay scheme\\nwhere dedicated relay is\\ninstalled\\nDedicated relay scheme with\\ntransfer trip where required by\\nprotection engineering\\nDirectional-power element\\n(ANSI 32) — pure-generation\\nsites\\nNot applicable Set on POI recloser where\\ninstalled; used to enforce a\\n§3.6 controlled limit where\\napplicable\\nSet on POI recloser; used to\\nenforce a §3.6 controlled limit\\nwhere applicable\\nMetering Bidirectional revenue meterBidirectional revenue meterBidirectional revenue meter,\\nprimary or secondary as\\nfeeder configuration requires\\nUtility RTU and SCADA\\ntelemetry\\nNot required Required per TCS-02 (≥500\\nkW)\\nRequired per TCS-02\\nNotes to Table 5-1.\\n1.  Category placement reflects the export configuration prevailing at the site. Where a site's configuration warrants\\nrequirements differing from the tabular default — including, for example, load/generation-decoupling\\narrangements in which generation is isolated by a DER breaker with a dedicated protection relay scheme —\\nprotection engineering may specify the applicable requirements through the Engineering Referral Procedure\\n(ERP-9 §3, Form ER-11).\\n\\n---\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard\\nPage 6\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024\\n2.  Table 5-1 addresses protective and control equipment. Monitoring and communications requirements are\\nestablished under TCS-02.\\n3.  Where §3.6 recognition is in effect at a pure-generation site with a utility POI recloser, the ANSI 32\\ndirectional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips on violation.\\n§6 Monitoring and Control\\nFacilities at or above the TCS-02 program threshold shall provide real-time monitoring and control integration through\\na utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry as prescribed by TCS-02. Live telemetry to the Company system\\noperations center is a condition of permission to operate. This standard does not restate TCS-02; refer to TCS-02 §5\\nfor the telemetry rule and to Alleniom system operations for RTU installation scheduling.\\nSite-level control functions required by §3.6 (Power Control System recognition), by Table 5-1 (dedicated protection\\nrelay schemes, DER breaker arrangements), and by ERP-9 site determinations, together satisfy the\\ncontrol-integration expectations of this section as applied to the specific facility.\\n§7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions\\nPost-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not\\npermitted for capacity or POI changes.\\nScope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by\\nboth parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without\\ninvoking this section.\\nPrincipal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection\\nservice agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as\\nexecuted.\\nRequired path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of\\ninterconnection after ISA execution shall:\\n1.  Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;\\n2.  File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and\\n3.  Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.\\nThe new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested\\nchange is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the\\napplicant as involving new or existing equipment.\\nOther post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within\\nthe same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the\\nchange-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.\\nDownstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment\\nreservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in\\nqueue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application\\nreceives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.\\n§8 Records and Compliance\\nInterconnection Studies retains the application file, executed ISA, and study record for each in-scope facility for the\\nretention period established by Regulatory Affairs. Standards Engineering maintains the current revision of this\\nstandard, the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2 and subsequent editions), and the Engineering Referral\\nProcedure (ERP-9) register of per-site determinations.\\n\\n\\n---\\n\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard\\nPage 7\\nDIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024\\nAny conflict between this standard and the APUC-filed tariff is resolved in favor of the tariff. data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":197,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{"success":true,"page":{"id":42,"path":"der-program/standards/dps-07-rev2-distribution-protection-standard","title":"DPS-07 Rev2 Distribution Protection Standard","description":"Distribution Protection Standard Rev 2 effective 09/15/2023 with POI recloser requirements","content":"# DPS-07 Rev2 Distribution Protection Standard\n\nDPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023\nPage 1\nALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING\nDISTRIBUTION PROTECTION STANDARD\nDoc no.\nRev\nDate\nOwner\nDPS-07\nRev 2\n09/15/2023\nAlleniom Standards Engineering\nEffective date: 09/15/2023\nSupersedes: DPS-07 Rev 1 (11/04/2019)\nClassification: Engineering Standard — Distribution Protection\nApproved by: Manager, Standards Engineering\n1. PURPOSE\nDPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources\n(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault\nclearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the\nutility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to\nthe distribution network.\nThis standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective\ndevices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards\nEngineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope\nprojects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.\n2. SCOPE\nThis standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service\nterritory, including but not limited to:\n1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).\n2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).\n3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to\nthe distribution system through the point of common coupling.\nSub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this\nstandard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall\napply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.\nNon-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any\noperating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection\nguidance.\n3. REFERENCES\nThe following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:\n IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with\nAssociated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.\n IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.\n IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible\nAutomatic Circuit Reclosers.\n ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.\n\n\n---\n\nDPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023 Page 2\n Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.\n Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.\n4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS\n4.1 General\nEvery distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment\nsufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:\n(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility\nreclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.\n(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on\nthe utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection\nstandard.\n(c)Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption\nbetween the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.\n(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is\ncleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary\ntripping of either.\n4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement\nEvery export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection\n(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.\nThe POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:\n1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,\ncurrent and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and\noperated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary\nconductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications\nbackhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.\n2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit\ninterrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per\nDistribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.\n3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,\nwith settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:\n— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),\n— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,\n— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,\n— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,\n— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power\nbackstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,\n— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.\n4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the\ncontrol cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of\ncommunications shall not defeat local protection.\nWhere a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering\ndetermination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.\n\n---\n\nDPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023\nPage 3\n5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect\noperable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of\nclearance holds.\n6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location\naccessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer\npremises.\n4.3 DER-Side Protection\nDER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection\nprotection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI\nrecloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.\nDER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.\n4.4 Grounding\nThe DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with\nthe grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's\ngrounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.\n4.5 Anti-Islanding\nThe DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone\nrequirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage\nand frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive\nscheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;\notherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.\n5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS\n5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing\nThe POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:\n(a) The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream\nrecloser.\n(b) The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per\nthe site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the\nsite's operating procedure.\n(c) Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study\nprior to energization.\n5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection\nDER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent\nreasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the\nPOI recloser shall trip as backup protection.\n5.3 Direct Transfer Trip\nDirect transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable\nnon-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening\nof the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications\nchannel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.\n5.4 Reclosing Blocking\nAutomatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the\nDER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the\n\n\n---\n\nDPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023 Page 4\naffected feeder warrants such a change. The determination shall be made per site by Distribution Protection\n5.5 Settings Governance\nAll protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the\nDER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in\nthe field without a written revision order.\n6. TESTING\n6.1 Factory Acceptance\nThe POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard\ntest protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to\nshipment.\n6.2 Site Acceptance\nPrior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed\nby Alleniom Utilities:\n1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.\n2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.\n3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,\nand reset.\n4. End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.\n5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.\n6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.\n7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.\n6.3 Commissioning and Cutover\nCutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and\naccepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system\noperator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.\n6.4 Periodic Testing\nThe POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. 1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
 IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
 IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
 IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
 ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.

4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c)Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),

— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,

backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.

GUIDELINE

§1  SCOPE
This guideline governs deployment sequencing of constrained utility equipment (RTUs, reclosers) across
completed sites awaiting energization. It applies to Alleniom-owned devices installed by Distribution
Operations for the purpose of energizing a construction-complete distributed energy resource (DER) site,
when supplier lead times or quarterly delivery quantities constrain the number of sites that can be
equipped in a given deployment window.
This guideline does NOT apply to application processing. Nondiscriminatory queue-order treatment of
interconnection applications is governed by Interconnection Tariff §12.7 and by the procedures
administered by Interconnection Studies; nothing in this guideline modifies, displaces, or supplements
those procedures. The rankings established under §2 operate solely on sites for which interconnection
application processing is complete, the interconnection agreement (where required) is executed, and
construction is certified complete by the customer or its contractor.
Devices out of scope: customer-owned protective equipment; utility-owned equipment already installed at
the site; distribution-system reinforcement equipment scheduled under an approved capital work order.
Program scope for the underlying DER remains as defined in DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 and Interconnection Tariff
§12.2.
§2  COMMISSIONING CRITICALITY
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA
As a general rule, deployment priority for constrained equipment follows interconnection queue order,
consistent with the nondiscriminatory treatment principles of Interconnection Tariff §12.7.
A site may be advanced ahead of queue order under certain circumstances — the urgent nature of a
request, in particular for public infrastructure (schools, hospitals, water/wastewater facilities), or an
expedited deployment pathway on reasonable customer request — but only where substantiated by the
site's own recorded attributes (per §3), in order of priority: (1) essential-service function (water/wastewater,
emergency, health); (2) committed in-service or grant-funding deadline; (3) construction-complete date.
Among sites of the same critical nature, the deciding factor is interconnection queue order; requests not
substantiated by these attributes remain in queue order.

a hospital, emergency-response, or first-responder facility; or a public-health facility for which loss of
service is treated as an emergency by the responsible jurisdiction. Essential-service status is
evidenced by the customer's facility classification of record and, where applicable, the served-load
designation on the interconnection application.
 Committed in-service or grant-funding deadline. A contractually committed in-service date, or a
date on which grant funding lapses if the site is not in service, established in a fully executed written
instrument between the customer and a governmental funder, project sponsor, or off-taker. Internal
customer construction targets, marketing dates, budget-cycle expectations, and school-year,
fiscal-year, or seasonal preferences do not constitute a committed deadline under this factor.
 Construction-complete date. The calendar date on which the customer's construction of the site
was certified complete and ready for utility energization steps. Where more than one date is recorded,
the earlier of (a) the customer's written notice of construction completion and (b) the utility's on-site
verification, controls.

received in relation to a site do not enter the ranking. Ranking is determined from the raw attributes above,
evidenced by the source documents in §3.
§3  DOCUMENTATION

 Construction-complete date and source of certification (project construction file).
 Contracted in-service or grant-funding deadline, if any, with the executed instrument establishing it
attached by reference (customer submission).
 Essential-service classification, if any, with the customer's facility classification of record attached by
reference (application file).
 Interconnection queue date (DER Program queue).
The worksheet shall record the §2 factor on which each ranked site qualifies. Sites that do not qualify at

the applicable window and provided to the SOC concurrent with the coordination step described in §5.

§1   Purpose
This procedure defines the supplemental review process applied to distributed energy resource (DER)
interconnection applications that fail one or more of the fast-track technical screens set out in the Alleniom DER
Interconnection Standard (DIS-01 Rev 4). It establishes the ordered screens, data sources, and documentation to
be produced by the interconnection engineer conducting supplemental review, and identifies the conditions under
which a study agreement is required before the application may proceed.
Supplemental review is intended to allow an application that fails an initial fast-track screen to be evaluated
against a bounded set of additional technical criteria without incurring the cost and schedule of a full system
impact study, where that evaluation can be completed from existing feeder data and standard engineering
judgment.
Nothing in this procedure alters the substantive interconnection standards contained in DIS-01, the protection
requirements contained in DPS-07, or the telemetry and communications requirements contained in TCS-02.
§2   Scope
This procedure applies to:
(a)  all in-scope DER interconnection applications (≥500 kW) as defined in DIS-01 §3 that have entered
supplemental review following failure of an initial screen; and
(b)  all DER classes recognized in DIS-01 §3 — commercial small-scale (500 kW – 1 MW) and medium-scale (1
MW – 5 MW).
This procedure does not apply to:
(a)  sub-500 kW installations processed under the Simplified Small-Systems Process;
(b)  capacity or point-of-interconnection changes to an executed interconnection service agreement, which are
governed by DIS-01 §7; or
(c)  domestic rooftop solar, which is out of scope for the DER Program.
Where a supplemental-review screen result is inconclusive on the record before the engineer, the application shall
be advanced to a study agreement rather than passed or failed under this procedure.
§3   Screens


---

SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure  ·  Effective 02/10/2025  ·  Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering
Page 2
Applications entering supplemental review shall be evaluated under the following screens, in the order given. An
application that fails any screen shall be considered a candidate for a study agreement; the reviewing engineer
shall document the failing screen, the underlying data, and the recommended disposition per §6.
Screen A — Aggregate DER penetration on the feeder. Total nameplate DER (existing plus queued plus
requested) on the subject feeder shall not exceed the applicable penetration threshold set in DIS-01. Queue
positions are those on record with the DER Program Office at the date of screen evaluation.
Screen B — Voltage regulation and flicker. Reviewed against the feeder's most recent planning study or, where
none is on file for the subject feeder within twenty-four (24) months, against a screening voltage-rise calculation
performed using conductor and transformer impedance from the distribution planning record.
Screen C — Short-circuit contribution. DER short-circuit contribution shall not cause any feeder-protective
device to exceed 87.5% of its interrupting rating, nor cause any downstream protection coordination margin to
fall below the values specified in DPS-07.
Screen D — 100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. Governed by §4.
Screen E — Reverse power flow at substation. Where the aggregate DER on the subject feeder exceeds the
substation transformer's certified reverse-power capability, or where reverse-power protective settings are not in
place, the application shall be routed to study.
Passing all applicable screens is a necessary but not sufficient condition for interconnection; the application
remains subject to the balance of the DIS-01 evaluation, including protection and telemetry requirements.
§4   100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar
100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. For solar DER, the minimum load used in this screen shall be the
minimum load within the daytime window 10:00–16:00, determined from feeder AMI interval data. The absolute
overnight minimum shall NOT be used. Requested DER capacity must be ≤ this daytime-window minimum for
the site to pass the screen.
The daytime-window minimum shall be computed from feeder AMI interval data covering the most recent
complete twelve (12) calendar months, aggregated to fifteen-minute intervals aligned to the feeder AMI
collection cadence, and evaluated only over intervals whose start time falls within 10:00–16:00 local clock time
on the feeder. Intervals affected by known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching shall be excluded
and the exclusion documented in the reviewer's worksheet. Where fewer than twelve (12) months of AMI interval
data are available, the reviewer shall use the longest continuous complete period available and note the
data-window length in the supplemental review memo.
The daytime-window minimum determined under this section is the sole minimum-load figure used for the solar
100%-of-minimum-load screen. Feeder minimum-load figures produced for other purposes — planning studies,
hosting-capacity map inputs, protection coordination — are not substitutes for the value computed under this
section and shall not be carried into the Screen D determination without recomputation on the AMI record.
Where a prior supplemental review memo on the same feeder has applied a different minimum-load basis, the
reviewer shall recompute the value under this section and, if the two disagree, supersede the earlier memo in the
file.
§5   Data sources
The following data sources are authoritative for supplemental review under this procedure:


---

SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure  ·  Effective 02/10/2025  ·  Alleniom Utilities — Standards EngineeringPage 3
(a)  Feeder AMI interval data — from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse, at the meter aggregation level
published for the subject feeder. AMI interval data is the sole authoritative source for the Screen D
minimum-load determination described in §4.
(b)  Distribution planning record — most recent feeder planning study, conductor and transformer impedance
data, and protection coordination settings, held by Distribution Planning.
(c)  DER queue — active-queue and on-hold registers maintained by the DER Program Office as of the screen
evaluation date. Queue entries not yet reflected in a published hosting-capacity map remain applicable to Screen
A.
(d)  Certified Equipment List (CEL) — current edition, for verification that proposed inverters and PCS
equipment are eligible to be considered under the screens.
(e)  Interconnection application record — the applicant's filed capacity, single-line diagram, inverter
specifications, and control narrative (where controlled-capacity operation is asserted under DIS-01 §3.6).
Substitution of a source not listed above shall be documented in the memo produced under §6, together with the
reason for the substitution.
§6   Documentation
The reviewing engineer shall produce a supplemental review memo for each application processed under this
procedure. The memo shall contain, at minimum:
(a)  application identifier, applicant, subject feeder, and requested capacity;
(b)  the screens applied and the pass/fail determination for each;
(c)  for Screen D, the daytime-window minimum load determined per §4, the data window used, the count of
intervals evaluated, and any interval exclusions with reason;
(d)  the recommended disposition — advance without study agreement, advance to study agreement, or return to
applicant with specified deficiency;
(e)  reviewer signature and date; and
(f)  the identifiers of any earlier supplemental review memos superseded.
The memo shall be filed to the interconnection application record within five (5) business days of screen
completion. Where a memo supersedes an earlier determination on the same application or the same feeder, the
superseded memo shall be flagged in the file and a cross-reference to the superseding memo added to its cover.
