data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":203,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{"success":true,"page":{"id":48,"path":"der-program/standards/tcs-02-telemetry-comms-standard","title":"TCS-02 Telemetry Comms Standard","description":"Telemetry and Communications Standard effective 06/01/2021 requiring RTU and SCADA for sites 500 kW and above","content":"# TCS-02 Telemetry Comms Standard\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 1Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02\nALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING\nTELEMETRY & COMMUNICATIONS STANDARD\nDoc no. Rev Date Owner\nTCS-02 Rev 1 06/01/2021 Alleniom Standards Engineering\nDocument title: Telemetry & Communications Standard\nApplies to: Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities interconnected to the Alleniom Utilities\ndistribution system within the DER Program scope\nEffective date: 06/01/2021\nApproving authority: Manager, Standards Engineering\n§1   PURPOSE\nThis standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time\ntelemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities\nand the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data\ncontent, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a\nDER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data\nAcquisition (SCADA) system.\nTCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited\nto telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective\nfunctions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the\nstandards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the\nscope of this document.\n§2   SCOPE\nTCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose\nnameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER\nhandled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.\nTCS-02 applies to:\n a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).\n b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).\n c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the\naggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.\n d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER\ncommissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or\ncapacity change requiring a new interconnection application.\n4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 2Telemetry & Communications Standard TCS-02\nWhere a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common\ncoupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the\naggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.\n§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS\n§3.1   Ownership and installation\nEach in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)\ninstalled at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,\nowned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.\nThe customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC\nservice, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU\ninstallation drawing.\n§3.3   Functional requirements\nEach RTU shall, at minimum:\n a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station\ninstrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.\n b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end\nprocessors over an approved communications path (§4).\n c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum\nof seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon\nrestoration.\n d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as\ndiagnostic points.\n e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom\nSCADA/EMS Engineering only.\n§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements\nThe RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation\ndrawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a\ndedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour\noutage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.\n§3.5   Time synchronization\nThe RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)\ntime or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a\ntimestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.\n§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification\n§3.2   Approved models\nThe utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU\nservice: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power\nplant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the\nutility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 3\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\nPrior to the RTU being accepted as commissioned, Alleniom shall perform an end-to-end\npoint-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,\nexercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.\nCommissioning of the RTU is a prerequisite to the telemetry condition stated in §5.\n§4   COMMUNICATIONS\n§4.1   Communications transport\nThe RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by\nSCADA/EMS Engineering:\n a.   Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or\n b.   Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or\n c.   Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held\nby Alleniom.\nCustomer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.\nWhere site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for\ninterconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.\n§4.2   SCADA protocol\nThe RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure\nAuthentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration\nparameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —\nshall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.\n§4.3   Availability\nThe end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a\nmonthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent\nloss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be\ncorrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected\nequipment.\n§4.4   Address and IP management\nAll IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and\nAlleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate\nconnections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration\nrecord.\n§5   TELEMETRY CONDITION FOR PERMISSION TO OPERATE\n§5.   ≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry.\nThis requirement applies to all in-scope DER sites, including aggregated facilities under\nDIS-01 §3.4.\nLive telemetry, for the purposes of §5, means that the RTU installed under §3 is:\n a.   Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;\n\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 4\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\n b.   Communicating with Alleniom SCADA over an approved transport (§4) at the refresh\ncadence required by §6; and\n c.   Presenting all required data points (§6) as valid (not stale, not forced, not flagged\nbad-quality) at the SCADA operator display at the moment Permission to Operate (PTO) is\nissued.\nCompliance with §5 is confirmed by the SOC Shift Supervisor on shift at the time PTO is\nrequested. The SOC's confirmation is recorded against the interconnection file. PTO shall not be\nissued to any in-scope DER site until §5 is satisfied.\n§6   DATA POINTS AND REFRESH RATES\n§6.1   Required data points\nEach in-scope DER site shall present, at minimum, the following analog and status points to\nAlleniom SCADA. Where the site's arrangement includes multiple inverter blocks or multiple\naggregated facilities behind a common POI, values shall be reported both individually per block\nand as a facility total.\nAnalog values (per site, and per block where applicable):\nPoint\nUnits\nSign convention\nReal power, net export at POI\nkW\nExport positive\nReactive power, net at POI\nkVAr\nAbsorbing positive\nPOI voltage, per phase\nV\n—\nPOI current, per phase\nA\n—\nFrequency at POI\nHz\n—\nGross generation (per inverter block)\nkW\nGeneration positive\nAuxiliary/parasitic load (where separately metered)\nkW\nLoad positive\nCumulative energy delivered\nkWh\nExport positive\nCumulative energy received\nkWh\nImport positive\nAmbient / cabinet temperature (RTU health)\n°C\n—\nStatus and diagnostic points:\nPoint\nDescription\nSite online / offline\nAggregate operating state of the DER\nInverter/PCS block status\nPer block: run, standby, fault\nCommunications heartbeat\nRTU-to-SCADA path health\nTime-sync quality\nGNSS/NTP discipline status\nConfiguration version\nActive RTU configuration identifier\nAlarm summary\nRolled-up device alarm state\n§6.2   Refresh rates\n\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 5\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\nAnalog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3\nClass 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than\nevery sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an\nintegrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be\nreported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.\n§6.3   Data quality\nEvery value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,\nrestart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the\nRTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be\nreported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.\n§6.4   Retention\nAlleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six\n(36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,\nengineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.\n§7   CYBERSECURITY\n§7.1   Applicability\nThe RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any\ncustomer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this\nsection. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security\nprogram consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.\n§7.2   Access control\nLocal and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to\nAlleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication\nagainst Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are\nmanaged by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.\n§7.3   Communications security\nDNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All\ncommunications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an\nAlleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates\nshall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.\n§7.4   Firmware, configuration, and change management\nRTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following\nthe Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a\ncryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or\nreconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.\n§7.5   Logging and monitoring\nThe RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,\nand firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.\nAnomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response\nprocedure.\n\n\n---\n\nTCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021\nAlleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering\nPage 6\nTelemetry & Communications Standard\nTCS-02\n§7.6   Physical security\nThe RTU shall be housed in a locked, tamper-evident enclosure. Enclosure keys, cores, and any\nphysical access tokens are held by Alleniom. Physical intrusion of the enclosure shall generate a\nstatus point (tamper alarm) reported to SCADA under §6.\n§7.7   Incident response\nThe customer shall report, without delay, any known or suspected compromise of the RTU, its\nenclosure, its communications transport, or any interface between customer equipment and\nutility-owned telemetry equipment. Reports shall be directed to the Alleniom SOC and to\nSCADA/EMS Engineering.\n§7.8   Decommissioning\nAt end of life, the RTU and its cryptographic material are returned to Alleniom for secure disposal.\nCustomer equipment previously interfaced to the RTU shall be sanitized of any Alleniom-provided\ncredentials before it is repurposed or disposed of.\nEnd of TCS-02.","content_type":"markdown","editor":"markdown","is_published":true,"is_private":false,"locale":"en","created_at":"2026-11-20T11:40:53.219780+00:00","updated_at":"2026-11-20T11:40:53.219780+00:00","tags":["standards","telemetry"],"author_name":"Evan Solberg","author_email":"evan.solberg@alleniom.com"},"error":""}"}],"structuredContent":{"success":true,"page":{"id":48,"path":"der-program/standards/tcs-02-telemetry-comms-standard","title":"TCS-02 Telemetry Comms Standard","description":"Telemetry and Communications Standard effective 06/01/2021 requiring RTU and SCADA for sites 500 kW and above","content":"# TCS-02 Telemetry Comms Standard

data: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":204,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{"success":true,"page":{"id":49,"path":"der-program/standards/tariff-excerpt-s12-interconnection","title":"Tariff Excerpt S12 Interconnection","description":"Excerpt of APUC-filed tariff section 12 covering withdrawal, payment defaults, and queue-order processing","content":"# Tariff Excerpt S12 Interconnection\n\nAPUC Tariff Filing — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Vol. III, §12 Page 1 of 6\nALLENIOM UTILITIES\nAPUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff\n§12 Interconnection Provisions\nFiled with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission\nElectric Tariff — Volume III · Original Sheet No. 214 · Effective: March 1, 2024\nSECTION 12 — INTERCONNECTION OF DISTRIBUTED ENERGY\nRESOURCES\n§12.1 Applicability\nThis section governs the interconnection to Alleniom Utilities' (the “Company”) distribution system\nof distributed energy resources (“DER”) within the Alleron service territory. Technical\nrequirements, screens, study procedures, and equipment standards referenced herein are set out\nin the Company's DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01) and companion standards, each of\nwhich is incorporated by reference. Nothing in this section shall be construed to modify or\nsupersede any applicable safety, reliability, or protection requirement of the Company's\nengineering standards.\nFiled by: Alleniom Utilities · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA\n\n---\n\nAlleniom Utilities — APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff · §12 Interconnection\nVolume III · Sheet No. 214\nAPUC Tariff Filing — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Vol. III, §12\nPage 2 of 6\n§12.2 Scope of the DER Interconnection Program\nThe DER Interconnection Program administered under this section applies to applications for DER\ninterconnection at or above five hundred kilowatts (≥500 kW). Within the Program, DER shall be\nclassified according to the DER Interconnection Standard as follows:\n(a)  Commercial small-scale DER — five hundred kilowatts to one megawatt (500 kW – 1\nMW);\n(b)  Medium-scale DER — one megawatt to five megawatts (1 MW – 5 MW).\nThe Program scope threshold is ≥500 kW. DER below five hundred kilowatts (sub-500 kW),\nwhether commercial or residential, are not administered under this section and shall instead be\nprocessed under the Company's Simplified Small-Systems Process, which is filed separately\nand is outside the DER Interconnection Program.\nAggregation, controlled-capacity recognition, and shared point-of-interconnection eligibility are\naddressed in the DER Interconnection Standard and shall control the classification of any facility\nwhose nameplate rating, aggregate site rating, or point of common coupling brings it within\nProgram scope.\n\n\n---\n\nAlleniom Utilities — APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff · §12 Interconnection\nVolume III · Sheet No. 214\nAPUC Tariff Filing — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Vol. III, §12\nPage 3 of 6\n§12.3 Application Intake and Queue Position\nA complete application shall establish the applicant's queue position as of the date the Company\ndetermines the application to be complete. Applications determined to be incomplete shall be\nreturned with a written deficiency notice identifying each item requiring cure and the date by which\ncure is required. Queue position is not transferable between applications except as expressly\nprovided in the DER Interconnection Standard.\n§12.4 Deemed Withdrawal Following Notice of Impending Withdrawal or Cancellation\nUpon issuance of a formal written Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation by the\nCompany, the applicant shall have thirty (30) business days from the date of the notice to submit\na substantive response curing the matter identified therein. If the applicant fails to respond within\nthirty (30) business days, the application shall be deemed withdrawn and shall be closed from the\nactive queue without further action of the Company.\nFor purposes of this section, “business days” shall exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and federal\nlegal public holidays observed within the response window. Without limitation, the following\nfederal holidays falling within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized\nas non-business days and shall not be counted:\nHoliday\nObserved Date\nMemorial Day\n05/26/2025\nJuneteenth National Independence Day\n06/19/2025\nIndependence Day\n07/04/2025\nThe Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall be served in writing (certified mail or\nverified electronic delivery) and shall state the date of issuance, the response deadline computed\nunder this section, and the consequence of non-response. The Company shall maintain a log of all\nnotices issued, dates of service, and dispositions.\n\n\n---\n\nAlleniom Utilities — APUC-Filed Interconnection Tariff · §12 Interconnection\nVolume III · Sheet No. 214\nAPUC Tariff Filing — Alleniom Utilities Electric Tariff, Vol. III, §12\nPage 4 of 6\n§12.5 Construction-Payment Defaults\nWhere a construction work order or interconnection facilities invoice becomes payable and the\ncustomer has not remitted the amount due, the Company shall inform the customer in writing of\nthe outstanding balance and shall issue a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days from\nthe date of that written notice.\nFor so long as the thirty (30) business-day payment deadline is running, the affected project shall\nremain on hold in the queue and shall NOT be deemed withdrawn. The construction-payment\ndefault procedure under this §12.5 is distinct from, and shall not be conflated with, the\ndeemed-withdrawal procedure under §12.4; the two mechanisms have different triggers, different\nconsequences, and different cure paths.\nUpon receipt of full payment prior to expiration of the deadline, the Company shall promptly\nrelease the hold and resume the affected work in queue order. ALLENIOM UTILITIES

§12 Interconnection Provisions
Filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission
Electric Tariff — Volume III · Original Sheet No. 214 · Effective: March 1, 2024
SECTION 12 — INTERCONNECTION OF DISTRIBUTED ENERGY
RESOURCES
§12.1 Applicability
This section governs the interconnection to Alleniom Utilities' (the “Company”) distribution system
of distributed energy resources (“DER”) within the Alleron service territory. Technical
requirements, screens, study procedures, and equipment standards referenced herein are set out
in the Company's DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01) and companion standards, each of
which is incorporated by reference. Nothing in this section shall be construed to modify or
supersede any applicable safety, reliability, or protection requirement of the Company's
engineering standards.
Filed by: Alleniom Utilities · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA

§12.2 Scope of the DER Interconnection Program
The DER Interconnection Program administered under this section applies to applications for DER
interconnection at or above five hundred kilowatts (≥500 kW). Within the Program, DER shall be
classified according to the DER Interconnection Standard as follows:
(a)  Commercial small-scale DER — five hundred kilowatts to one megawatt (500 kW – 1
MW);
(b)  Medium-scale DER — one megawatt to five megawatts (1 MW – 5 MW).
The Program scope threshold is ≥500 kW. DER below five hundred kilowatts (sub-500 kW),
whether commercial or residential, are not administered under this section and shall instead be
processed under the Company's Simplified Small-Systems Process, which is filed separately
and is outside the DER Interconnection Program.
Aggregation, controlled-capacity recognition, and shared point-of-interconnection eligibility are
addressed in the DER Interconnection Standard and shall control the classification of any facility
whose nameplate rating, aggregate site rating, or point of common coupling brings it within
Program scope.

§12.3 Application Intake and Queue Position
A complete application shall establish the applicant's queue position as of the date the Company
determines the application to be complete. Applications determined to be incomplete shall be
returned with a written deficiency notice identifying each item requiring cure and the date by which
cure is required. Queue position is not transferable between applications except as expressly
provided in the DER Interconnection Standard.
§12.4 Deemed Withdrawal Following Notice of Impending Withdrawal or Cancellation
Upon issuance of a formal written Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation by the
Company, the applicant shall have thirty (30) business days from the date of the notice to submit
a substantive response curing the matter identified therein. If the applicant fails to respond within
thirty (30) business days, the application shall be deemed withdrawn and shall be closed from the
active queue without further action of the Company.
For purposes of this section, “business days” shall exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and federal
legal public holidays observed within the response window. Without limitation, the following
federal holidays falling within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized
as non-business days and shall not be counted:
Holiday
Observed Date
Memorial Day
05/26/2025
Juneteenth National Independence Day
06/19/2025
Independence Day
07/04/2025
The Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall be served in writing (certified mail or
verified electronic delivery) and shall state the date of issuance, the response deadline computed
under this section, and the consequence of non-response. The Company shall maintain a log of all
notices issued, dates of service, and dispositions.

§12.5 Construction-Payment Defaults
Where a construction work order or interconnection facilities invoice becomes payable and the
customer has not remitted the amount due, the Company shall inform the customer in writing of
the outstanding balance and shall issue a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days from
the date of that written notice.
For so long as the thirty (30) business-day payment deadline is running, the affected project shall
remain on hold in the queue and shall NOT be deemed withdrawn. The construction-payment
default procedure under this §12.5 is distinct from, and shall not be conflated with, the
deemed-withdrawal procedure under §12.4; the two mechanisms have different triggers, different
consequences, and different cure paths.
Upon receipt of full payment prior to expiration of the deadline, the Company shall promptly
release the hold and resume the affected work in queue order. If the deadline expires without
payment, the Company may pursue such remedies as are available under the applicable
Interconnection Service Agreement and this tariff, including, as a separate and subsequent step,
issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §12.4.

terms require withdrawal of the affected application and re-application in accordance with the DER
Interconnection Standard.
§12.7 Nondiscriminatory Queue-Order Processing of Applications
Applications shall be processed by the Company in queue order on a nondiscriminatory basis.
No applicant shall be advanced or disadvantaged in the processing sequence by reason of
identity, affiliation, customer class, geography, or any other factor not expressly provided for in this
tariff or in the DER Interconnection Standard.
Scope note. This §12.7 applies to APPLICATION PROCESSING only — that is, to the
sequencing of screening, technical review, study assignment, and issuance of interconnection
determinations. Utility construction sequencing and the scheduling and allocation of constrained
utility-owned equipment (including, without limitation, remote terminal units,
point-of-interconnection reclosers, and other supply-limited devices) are not governed by this
section. Such matters are addressed under the Company's operating guidelines, including OG-17
(Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline), which sets forth the criticality factors and
prioritization criteria applicable to constrained equipment. Nothing in this §12.7 shall be construed
to require the Company to sequence construction or equipment deployment in queue order where
OG-17 or another operating guideline provides a different criticality-based ordering.

DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1. The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2. Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3. Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4. Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.
Alleniom Utilities · DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com

an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.
§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.
Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.
§4.3  Documentation.
The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
include, at minimum:

the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;

for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
by the Standards Engineer of record;


for witness-tested facilities, the witness engineer’s test record, including instrument identifiers,
measured values, pass/fail dispositions per test point, and the witness engineer’s signature and
date;

the manufacturer’s certificate of conformance, factory test report, or equivalent evidence supporting
the CEL listing relied upon;

correspondence with the customer or commissioning agent bearing on scheduling, deferrals, or
test-plan negotiation.
The commissioning record is retained in the facility interconnection file and is a prerequisite to PTO
issuance by the System Operations Center. PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed
witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination
against the current CEL edition.

To:      Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
From:   Priya Ranganathan, Interconnection Studies
Date:   06/25/2025
Subject: Bramwick Commons Solar (1.8 MW, Feeder ALN-214) — Supplemental Review Screen Determination
1. Project
The application was routed to supplemental review following failure of an initial fast-track screen. This memo records the disposition of the 100%-of-minimum-load screen applied under SRP-3 Rev 3.
2. Screen applied
100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar, per §4 of SRP-3 (Rev 3, effective 02/10/2025). Under this screen, the requested DER capacity is compared against the minimum load observed on the subject feeder from AMI interval data.
3. Analysis
Reviewed AMI interval load data for Feeder ALN-214 from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse and identified a minimum feeder load of 1.1 MW. The value was drawn from the feeder AMI record available on file for ALN-214. No intervals were excluded for known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching during the period reviewed.
4. Comparison
1.8 MW requested exceeds 1.1 MW minimum feeder load — screen FAILED.
5. Recommendation
Study Agreement required prior to advancement. The application should not proceed on the supplemental-review track. A Study Agreement should be offered to Bramwick Commons Solar LLC, with the scope covering the technical conditions that gave rise to the failed screen on Feeder ALN-214.
6. Disposition
Return supplemental review file to Interconnection Studies queue with a failed-screen flag on Feeder ALN-214.
Notify the applicant of the screen result and forward the Study Agreement package.
Hold advancement of PXA record for Bramwick Commons Solar until Study Agreement is executed.

ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office Page 1
ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1. The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2. Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3. Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4. Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.
Alleniom Utilities · DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com

The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.
§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.
Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.
§4.3  Documentation.
The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
include, at minimum:

the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;

for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
by the Standards Engineer of record;

Page 3

for witness-tested facilities, the witness engineer’s test record, including instrument identifiers,
measured values, pass/fail dispositions per test point, and the witness engineer’s signature and
date;

the manufacturer’s certificate of conformance, factory test report, or equivalent evidence supporting
the CEL listing relied upon;

correspondence with the customer or commissioning agent bearing on scheduling, deferrals, or
test-plan negotiation.
The commissioning record is retained in the facility interconnection file and is a prerequisite to PTO
issuance by the System Operations Center. PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed
witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination
against the current CEL edition.
End of procedure. See DIS-01 Rev 4 for interconnection standards, TCS-02 for telemetry requirements, and the
current CEL edition for the list of qualifying equipment. Revisions to this procedure are issued by Standards
Engineering and take effect on the date shown in the document-control block above.","content_type":"markdown","editor":"markdown","is_published":true,"is_private":false,"locale":"en","created_at":"2026-11-20T11:40:53.219780+00:00","updated_at":"2026-11-20T11:40:53.219780+00:00","tags":["standards","commissioning","witness-test"],"author_name":"Evan Solberg","author_email":"evan.solberg@alleniom.com"},"error":""},"isError":false}}

**To:** DER Program Office <der.program@alleniom.com>

**Cc:** Meera Vellanki <meera.vellanki@alleniom.com>

---

DER Program Office —

Attached please find the City of Elmsworth's DER interconnection application for the Municipal Service Center PV project (Form DIS-APP-01), assigned Application ID PXA-2025-0198 on your intake page. Nameplate is 900 kW AC, behind-the-meter with export capability, mounted on the Municipal Service Center rooftop and adjacent parking canopy.

For your records, this filing follows our earlier application PXA-2023-0412 dated 04/12/2023 for the same Municipal Service Center site. The 2023 filing sat with our office through a budget cycle change and a facilities director turnover on our side, and we did not push it forward during that period. The scope in the current package is materially the same site, the same 900 kW envelope, and the same point of interconnection area on the mid-town Elmsworth feeder — the update is the CEL-2025-Q2 inverter selection and refreshed drawings dated 05/16/2025.

Given the continuity of the project, we would like to retain our original 2023 queue position. Council approved the capital allocation in the FY25 budget on the assumption that we would be in construction this fall, and every month we slide back in the queue is a month that pushes mechanical completion past the winter shutdown window and into next spring. We would appreciate your team's confirmation on that point at your earliest convenience so we can lock in permit and procurement dates.

We are targeting the following applicant-side milestones (also carried in Section 7 of the application):

  - Permit set complete: 08/2025
  - Construction start: 10/2025
  - Mechanical completion: 02/2026
  - Ready for witness test: 03/2026

If any of those dates look unworkable against your screening or study calendar, please tell us now rather than later — we would much rather adjust on the front end than discover a slip in September. I am reachable at the number below any weekday, and Meera has my mobile if something needs a faster turn.

Thank you for the continued partnership. We appreciate the DER Program Office's attention on this one — it is a visible project for the City and the Council is watching the schedule closely.

Best regards,

Bill Tran
Energy Manager
City of Elmsworth
300 City Center Way
Elmsworth, Alleron 07EL
(612) 236-0402
bill.tran@cityofelmsworth.gov

3.1 Capacity Basis Statement (from Applicant)
The Applicant proposes to operate this DER facility at a Stated Capacity of 480 kW — export-limited
operation at the point of common coupling. Output is constrained through the on-site inverter fleet's
programmable power-control settings, which the Developer will configure at commissioning to cap
real-power delivery at the point of common coupling to the stated 480 kW value under all operating
conditions. On this basis the Applicant requests the Application be reviewed at the stated 480 kW figure.

4.1 Connection Description
The proposed PV system ties into the customer-owned side of the site's existing electrical service. Power
flow from the six commercial three-phase inverters (see the companion inverter datasheets file for per-unit
ratings) is aggregated at PVC-1, routed through the pad-mount lockable AC disconnect (PVD-1), and
lands on a new 800 A back-fed breaker in MDS-1. MDS-1 is fed from the plant's existing utility service
transformer through the site's existing 480 V main service disconnect and the existing utility revenue
meter.
The new PV interconnection is behind the existing service meter — the same point of common coupling
as the site's existing electrical service — on the load side of the utility revenue meter and upstream of the
warehouse's process and refrigeration load buses.
No new utility-side equipment, no new service transformer, no new service drop, and no separate revenue
meter is requested. The Applicant proposes to net the PV generation against warehouse load through the
existing bidirectional revenue meter of record and to hold export at the point of common coupling to the
Stated Capacity of 480 kW under all operating conditions.

schedule below is a reference roster and does not restate the per-unit nameplate ratings recorded on

NORTHERN GRID SOLAR SERVICES
Commercial & Industrial Photovoltaic Contracting

DER COMMISSIONING CERTIFICATE
Document: NGSS-COM-2017-0348
Issued: 09/28/2017
Project Identification
Site Name Merrow Creamery Legacy PV
Site Address
Customer Merrow Creamery
Utility Alleniom Utilities
Nameplate Capacity 800 kW
Commissioning Date 09/28/2017
Contractor of Record Northern Grid Solar Services
NGSS Project No. NGSS-2017-118
System Description
Rooftop-mounted photovoltaic generating facility connected behind the existing customer service meter at the Merrow
Creamery dairy processing plant. Array totals 800 kW nameplate AC, distributed across the north and south
production-building roof planes. Three-phase, 480 V output tied into the customer's existing 480 V main distribution
switchboard via a dedicated PV feeder breaker; no modifications to the utility service entrance conductors or the
revenue meter. Generation is intended to offset on-site process load; no export-focused equipment installed.
Modules: 2,580 × 310 W crystalline-silicon PV modules, mounted on ballasted low-tilt racking.
Inverters: 8 × 100 kW three-phase string inverters (UL 1741 listed; IEEE 1547 anti-islanding).
AC combining: 800 A PV subpanel feeding a 1,000 A PV feeder breaker in the existing 480 V main switchboard.
Point of common coupling: Load side of the existing utility service meter.

monitoring, or communications equipment is installed at the point of common coupling.

**From:** Corey Lindqvist <corey.lindqvist@hailbouysolar.com>
**To:** der.program@alleniom.com
**Date:** Tue, 08 Jul 2025 09:14:22 -0500
**Subject:** Harkwell Ridge — ISA capacity update request
**Cc:** Meera Vellanki <meera.vellanki@alleniom.com>

---

Program Office,

Following execution of the Interconnection Service Agreement on 07/03/2025 for Harkwell Ridge Solar (Application PXA-2024-0117) at 2.2 MW, Hailbouy Solar is writing to request that the executed ISA be updated to reflect a nameplate export capacity of 2.8 MW. Our preference — and, we believe, the only workable path given the project's construction and financing calendar — is to effect this change via a short addendum to the executed ISA.

Background and rationale:

- The ISA as executed on 07/03/2025 fixes capacity at 2.2 MW on Feeder ALN-042. Post-execution offtake refinements and updated production modeling from our EPC support a revised design point of 2.8 MW at the same point of interconnection.

- The equipment schedule and site plan are unchanged in configuration. The single-axis-tracker layout, module count per string, row geometry, inverter locations, MV collection topology, POI structure, and interconnection facilities scope on file with the DER Program Office are all as-approved. The delta is a firmware-level export setting and dc:ac ratio adjustment within the equipment already listed in the original application and reflected in the executed Interconnection Service Agreement.

- Because the physical configuration and POI are unchanged, no re-study should be needed. The prior system impact and facilities study work performed under PXA-2024-0117 remains the applicable technical basis, and a short capacity-only addendum executed against the existing ISA is the appropriate instrument to memorialize the update.

Requested action:

1. Please prepare an addendum to ISA-Harkwell-Ridge revising the Article 2 nameplate export capacity from 2.2 MW to 2.8 MW, with all other terms of the executed ISA to remain in full force and effect.

2. Please route the addendum for countersignature by end of week (07/11/2025). Our construction mobilization sequence, EPC commitment schedule, and tax-equity funding milestones are built around the 07/03/2025 execution and cannot tolerate slippage. Any process that reopens the study queue on this project is not viable for us on this timeline.

3. If the Program Office needs a supplemental technical memo from our engineer of record confirming that the equipment schedule and site plan are unchanged in configuration, we can have that in your hands by close of business 07/09/2025. Please advise by return email if this would expedite the addendum.

I would appreciate confirmation of receipt today and a target date for the addendum draft. Meera — copying you directly so Interconnection Studies has visibility; I understand the addendum sits with the contracts desk, but if there is anything on the studies side that needs a signoff to unblock the drafting please let me know today and we will accommodate.

Given the timing sensitivity, we consider expedited turnaround essential and are prepared to make our team available for a same-day call at Alleniom's convenience.

Regards,

Corey Lindqvist
Project Director
Hailbouy Solar
2200 Ridge Point Road, Suite 400
Halston, Alleron 03HA
(612) 817-0554

INTERCONNECTION SERVICE AGREEMENT
Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
Doc no. ISA-Harkwell-Ridge · Rev Final · Date 07/03/2025 · Owner: DER Program Office — Contracts
Agreement No.: ISA-Harkwell-Ridge
Project: Harkwell Ridge Solar
Application No.: PXA-2024-0117
This Interconnection Service Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into by and between Alleniom Utilities, an investor-owned electric utility organized under the laws of the State of Alleron, with principal offices at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA (EIN 36-4820917) (the “Company”), and Hailbouy Solar, with offices at 2200 Ridge Point Road, Suite 400, Halston, Alleron 03HA (the “Interconnection Customer”), each a “Party” and collectively the “Parties.” This Agreement is effective as of the date last executed below.
RECITALS
WHEREAS, the Interconnection Customer filed with the Company an application for interconnection service, designated PXA-2024-0117, on 06/17/2024, in respect of a 2.2 MW single-axis-tracker ground-mount photovoltaic generating facility known as Harkwell Ridge Solar (the “Facility”), to be interconnected to the Company's distribution system at a point on Feeder ALN-042;
WHEREAS, the Company completed technical screening, system impact and facilities studies for the Facility in accordance with the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4, and issued a final study determination approving the Facility for execution of an Interconnection Service Agreement at the capacity and point of interconnection described in the application as filed;
WHEREAS, the Company's tariff, as filed with and approved by the Alleron Public Utilities Commission, governs the interconnection of distributed energy resources of the Facility's class and forms an integral part of the terms and conditions of interconnection service provided hereunder;
WHEREAS, the Parties intend by this Agreement to establish the terms, conditions, rights and obligations under which the Facility will be permitted to parallel with, and export energy to, the Company's distribution system;
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and undertakings set forth herein, and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:
ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS
1.1 Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Company's filed tariff (the “Tariff”) and in the Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard, DIS-01 Rev 4 (the “DIS”).
1.2 For the purposes of this Agreement, and without limitation of the foregoing:
“Facility” means the generating equipment, ancillary equipment, and all interconnection facilities described in Article 2 hereof.
“Point of Interconnection” or “POI” means the physical point at which the Facility is electrically connected to the Company's distribution system, as identified in Article 2.
“Standards” means the standards and specifications identified in Article 4, each as in effect on the Effective Date and as such may be amended, superseded, or reissued by the Company in accordance with its ordinary regulatory practice.
“Effective Date” has the meaning given in Article 3.
“Certified Equipment List” or “CEL” means the Company's then-current Certified Equipment List published by Standards Engineering.
ARTICLE 2 — DESCRIPTION OF FACILITY
2.1 Project designation. Harkwell Ridge Solar (Application PXA-2024-0117).
2.2 Interconnection Customer. Hailbouy Solar.
2.3 Facility technology. Photovoltaic generation, single-axis-tracker ground-mount configuration.
2.4 Nameplate export capacity. 2.2 MW (AC) at the Point of Interconnection.
2.5 Point of Interconnection (POI). A three-phase primary tap on Feeder ALN-042, at the pole FKDN54D.
2.6 Point of Common Coupling (PCC). Coincident with the Point of Interconnection identified in Section 2.5.
2.7 Material terms. The capacity, technology, and Point of Interconnection stated in this Article are material terms of this Agreement.
ARTICLE 3 — TERM AND EFFECTIVE DATE
3.1 Effective Date. This Agreement is effective as of 07/03/2025 (the “Effective Date”), being the date on which the last of the two Parties has executed this Agreement.
3.2 Term. This Agreement shall remain in full force and effect from the Effective Date until terminated in accordance with its terms or superseded by a successor agreement between the Parties.
3.3 Continuing obligations. The obligations of the Parties in respect of indemnity, limitation of liability, confidentiality, and dispute resolution shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement.
ARTICLE 4 — INTERCONNECTION STANDARDS
4.1 Governing standards. The Facility shall at all times be designed, constructed, commissioned, operated, and maintained in conformity with the following Company standards and any successor or superseding editions thereof:
(a) DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard (effective 03/01/2024);
(b) DPS-07 Rev 2 — Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023);
(c) TCS-02 — Telemetry and Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021); and
(d) CEL-2025-Q2 — Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025), as such may be superseded from time to time.
4.2 Order of precedence. In the event of any inconsistency among the documents constituting this Agreement, the following order of precedence shall govern: (i) the Tariff; (ii) the applicable Company Standards enumerated in Section 4.1; (iii) the body of this Agreement.
4.3 Compliance with successor standards. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to relieve the Interconnection Customer from the obligation to conform the Facility to successor or superseding editions of the Standards as and when they take effect, in accordance with the transition provisions of the applicable Standard.
ARTICLE 5 — METERING AND TELEMETRY
5.1 Metering. Revenue-quality metering shall be provided at the Point of Interconnection in accordance with the Tariff and the Company's metering specifications. Meters shall be owned, installed, tested, and maintained by the Company at the Interconnection Customer's cost, and shall be sealed at all times.
5.2 Telemetry. In accordance with TCS-02 §5, the Interconnection Customer shall install, at its cost, provisions for a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) and shall make available all analog and binary status DNP3 points required by the Company's Telemetry and Communications Standard, together with such communication paths and standing-power provisions as the Company requires for SCADA integration.
5.3 Commissioning of monitoring and control. Satisfactory commissioning and continuous availability of the telemetry described in Section 5.2 are conditions precedent to Permission to Operate. The Facility shall not be paralleled with the Company's distribution system in the absence of live utility telemetry, and any loss of telemetry after Permission to Operate shall be reported and remediated as provided in TCS-02.
5.4 Data and access rights. The Interconnection Customer grants the Company such rights of access to the Facility, and such rights to receive and use metering and telemetry data, as are necessary for the Company to discharge its obligations under the Tariff and applicable Standards.
ARTICLE 6 — PAYMENT TERMS
6.1 Construction work order. The Interconnection Customer shall pay the Company for the construction of upgrades and interconnection facilities in accordance with the construction work order issued under this Agreement, on the schedule and in the amounts set forth therein, and in accordance with Tariff §12.5.
6.2 Invoicing. Invoices shall be issued by the Company and shall be due and payable within thirty (30) calendar days of the invoice date, unless otherwise expressly provided in the construction work order. Amounts not paid when due shall bear interest at the rate set forth in the Tariff.
6.3 Payment default. In the event of non-payment, the Company shall provide the Interconnection Customer written notice and a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days in accordance with Tariff §12.5. Business days exclude weekends and federal holidays. During the pendency of any such deadline the Facility shall remain subject to any construction or commissioning hold ordered by the Company.
6.4 Ongoing operational charges. All charges, credits, and settlements applicable to interconnection service and associated ancillary services shall be as set forth in the Tariff.
ARTICLE 7 — AME

Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
INTERNAL DIRECTIVE
TO:	Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
DER Program Manager
CC:	Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
Marcus Deele, SCADA/EMS Engineering
FROM:	Dana Whitcomb, VP, Distribution Operations
DATE:	06/27/2025
SUBJECT:	Backlog Review — Commercial DER Interconnection Program
The Alleron Municipal League's letter of 06/20/2025, submitted on behalf of fourteen member municipalities and school districts and copied to the APUC Energy Resources Division, is the trigger. We are not going to litigate its tone. We are going to fix the underlying condition that produced it.
Effective immediately, I am ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. The scope covers the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population — every application currently sitting in the program queue. I want each one accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action.
The following non-negotiable dates govern this work:
1. 08/15/2025 — Formal written response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs owns the response letter. Harriet Ngoyi is the signatory. The response must address the League's five enumerated requests substantively and by project, not in aggregate.
2. 09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. Queue accounting must be complete before we walk into that room. I will not brief the Commission on partial data. If a project's disposition is not final by 09/10/2025, I want the reason documented in the file, not explained at the podium.
Ground rules for every disposition reached in this review:
Every disposition must be tariff-defensible. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, or operating guideline that supports the action. If the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as they are written. Do not shortcut them, and do not extend them beyond what the tariff contemplates.
Where standards or procedural conflicts exist, route them through the established referral process. Do not resolve them informally in the queue.
No interim energization, no political prioritization, and no queue-date inheritance outside of what the tariff and program policy permit.
Reporting cadence. I want weekly progress updates to the VP office, in writing, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025. Format: counts by disposition category, exceptions requiring VP attention, and any item at risk of missing the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates. Meera, Ivo, and Marcus will support the DER Program Manager with the data pulls, study status, and telemetry/equipment inputs their groups own.
Escalate obstacles to me directly. I would rather field a problem on a Tuesday than read about it in a League follow-up letter.
/s/
Dana Whitcomb
Vice President, Distribution Operations
Alleniom Utilities

**From:** Rosa Camarena <rosa.camarena@brookfenusd.org>
**To:** der.program@alleniom.com
**Date:** Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:42:18 -0500
**Subject:** Urgent: school array energization priority
**Cc:** Dana Whitcomb <dana.whitcomb@alleniom.com>, Harriet Ngoyi <harriet.ngoyi@alleniom.com>

---

To the DER Program Office:

I am writing again — and I want to be direct about the fact that this is not the first, second, or third time I have raised this with your office — to ask for a firm answer on when Alleniom Utilities intends to energize the two solar arrays serving Brookfen Unified School District. This message is dated 06/30/2025 and I would like a written response before the end of next week.

The two arrays in question, and their status on our side, are as follows:

  • Brookfen North High School Array — 720 kW. Construction was declared complete by our contractor on 04/18/2025. The local electrical inspector closed out the installation the same week. The system has been standing idle, energized-ready, for more than ten weeks.

  • Brookfen West Elementary Array — 640 kW. Construction was declared complete on 05/23/2025. Inspection was closed out shortly thereafter. This system has now been standing idle for over a month.

Neither array has been energized. Neither array has a firm energization date on record with the District. Each time our office contacts your program inbox we are told that a component — variously described as a "telemetry unit" or an "RTU" — has not yet been delivered by your supplier, and that we are somewhere in a queue behind other sites. What we have never been given, in writing, is the position of our sites in that queue, the identity of the sites ahead of us, or the basis on which those sites are being served ahead of ours.

I have to tell you plainly that the patience of the Brookfen school board and the District's superintendent is exhausted. The 2025–2026 school year begins for our students on 08/26/2025. Both of these arrays were financed, in significant part, on the strength of first-year operating-cost savings that were built into the District's adopted budget for that same school year and presented to our board and to the community at public meetings. Every additional week that these systems sit dark is a week of budgeted savings the District will not realize and will have to explain to the board, to our parents, and to the taxpayers of Brookfen who approved the underlying bond measure. Our high school's building-systems curriculum was also structured around students being able to observe the array in operation from the beginning of the term; that piece of the school year is now at risk of slipping into the second semester or being cut altogether.

You will by now have received the Alleron Municipal League's letter of 06/20/2025, signed by Executive Director Alden Pryce, escalating this same set of concerns on behalf of the District and thirteen other League members. Brookfen USD is one of the members named in that letter and stands fully behind the requests it contains. This message is not a substitute for the League's letter; it is intended to make the District's individual position, and the specifics of our two sites, unmistakable to your office.

What I am asking for, directly, is this: in the next allocation of the equipment your program office is holding up as the constraint — the RTU / telemetry units your staff have referenced in prior calls — I am asking Alleniom Utilities to advance the District's two waiting arrays ahead of the other sites presently competing for those units. Brookfen North completed construction on 04/18/2025 and Brookfen West on 05/23/2025. Both are public school facilities. Both have children returning to the building in eight weeks. Neither array can wait for a second or third delivery cycle without meaningful harm to the District's fiscal position and to the educational program these systems were installed to support.

If there is a formal process for requesting that our two sites be advanced in your next equipment allocation, please tell me what that process is and I will follow it today. If there is not, please treat this message as our written request under whatever mechanism your program uses to weigh these decisions, and please confirm receipt.

I am copying Ms. Whitcomb and Ms. Ngoyi so that this request is on the record with senior distribution operations and regulatory affairs, and so that no one at your program office is later in a position to say the District did not put this in writing in time.

I would like a written reply — not a call-back, a written reply — by close of business Friday, 07/11/2025. Silence past that date will require the District to raise this matter again through the League and, if necessary, directly with the Commission's Energy Resources Division, whose staff we understand is already tracking this program.

I am available at (612) 448-0311 during District business hours if it would help to talk any of this through. I would strongly prefer to resolve it with your office.

Regards,

Rosa Camarena
Facilities Director
Brookfen Unified School District
1725 Grantway Drive, Brookfen, Alleron 12BR
(612) 448-0311

Alleniom Utilities — Regulatory Affairs
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
TO: DER Program Manager
CC: Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations
Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
FROM: Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
DATE: 07/01/2025
SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking
1. Confirmation of directive
This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
4. Reporting cadence
The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.
Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
5. General provisions
Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as written. Standards or procedural conflicts route through the established referral process; they are not to be resolved informally in the queue. Queue-date treatment must remain within what the tariff and program policy permit.
Regulatory Affairs will coordinate with Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki) on queue and notice records, and with the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham) on study status, on any input required for the League response or the APUC briefing. The DER Program Manager remains the single point of accountability for the queue-cleanup inputs enumerated in §3.
Escalate obstacles to Regulatory Affairs in writing and, where the obstacle bears on the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates, to the VP office concurrently.
/s/
Harriet Ngoyi
Director, Regulatory Affairs
Alleniom Utilities
