1. Confirmation of directive
This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
4. Reporting cadence
The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.
Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
5. General provisions
Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.

The DER Program Manager remains the single point of accountability for the queue-cleanup inputs enumerated in §3.
Escalate obstacles to Regulatory Affairs in writing and, where the obstacle bears on the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates, to the VP office concurrently.

import docx

from docx.oxml.ns import qn
body=d.element.body
i=0
for child in body.iterchildren():
    if child.tag==qn('w:p'):
        # find paragraph
        p=None
        for pp in d.paragraphs:
            if pp._p is child: p=pp; break
        if p and p.text.strip(): print(f'[P{i}] {p.style.name}: {p.text}')

    elif child.tag==qn('w:tbl'):
        # find table
        t=None
        for tt in d.tables:
            if tt._tbl is child: t=tt; break
        print('=== TABLE ===')
        for r in t.rows:
            print(' | '.join(c.text.replace('\n',' / ') for c in r.cells))
        print('=== END TABLE ===')
EOF

[P13] Normal: This package records the municipal-array determination that Standards Engineering requested before the 08/15/2025 response to the Alleron Municipal League: which arrays remain in the municipal commissioning batch, whether the inverter or power conversion equipment actually installed at each array is carried on the current Certified Equipment List (CEL), and — for every array that is not carried — the witness-test scope, the parties who perform and witness it, the records that must be on file first, and a proposed schedule. It also identifies the array(s) the System Operations Center (SOC) can be asked to release on the record as of 07/14/2025.
[P14] Normal: The determination is deliberately split into two questions. Carriage on the CEL is a Standards Engineering eligibility question; whether to grant a waiver remains a Standards Engineering disposition and is not made here. Release readiness is a separate gate: an array must be both witness-clear and telemetry-live before the SOC can be asked to issue Permission to Operate (PTO).
[P15] Normal: Bottom line
[P16] List Bullet: Five arrays remain in scope: Cravenwood High, Darnwick Elementary, Holcott Library, Lockmere Middle and Marden Falls WRF. Tresbay Community Center withdrew its request on 07/09/2025 and is out of the batch.

Carriage call: NO for all three.
[P19] List Bullet: Witness tests are required for Darnwick, Holcott and Lockmere. Proposed dates are 07/24/2025, 07/22/2025 and 07/29/2025 respectively, with reserves on 07/31/2025, 07/25/2025 and 08/05/2025.
[P20] List Bullet: Only Marden Falls is ready to be put to the SOC for release on 07/14/2025. It is carried on the current CEL and its checklist records telemetry complete. Standards Engineering must first sign the waiver, and the SOC must confirm live telemetry at the moment PTO is requested. Cravenwood is carried but its telemetry is still pending; Lockmere has live telemetry but requires a witness test; Darnwick and Holcott require both a witness test and telemetry.
[P21] List Bullet: Three scheduling items stand on case WP45 — WP47 (Holcott), WP48 (Darnwick) and WP49 (Lockmere). They exactly match the three arrays named in this package. WP45 was closed on 07/14/2025 on that basis.

If Tresbay re-files, it will be a new filing with its own queue date and a fresh current-CEL lookup; the prior VX-140C listing cannot be carried forward as a waiver basis. The Withdrawal Notice Log does not contain a Tresbay entry; that record gap is carried as finding F-07 in Section 9.
[P27] Heading 2: 2.3 Governing rule applied
[P28] Normal: ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §3 is the controlling rule. A witness-test waiver applies only to equipment listed on the current CEL edition at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current edition requires an on-site witness test before PTO. The corollaries applied here are:
[P29] List Bullet: Waiver date = the date Standards Engineering signs the waiver, not the application, ISA or construction date.
[P30] List Bullet: Every protective device and every inverter/PCS installed must be on the current CEL; one unlisted component disqualifies the facility.
[P31] List Bullet: A prior-edition listing not carried forward gives no eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
[P32] List Bullet: Front-matter footnotes and historical annotations are informational only; they do not extend eligibility.
[P33] List Bullet: The current CEL at the waiver date controls; a model listed at application but not at waiver requires the witness test.
[P34] Normal: The current edition on 07/14/2025 is CEL-2025-Q2, published 04/30/2025; it supersedes CEL-2024-Q4 (10/31/2024). CEL-2025-Q3 is planned for 07/31/2025 and was not in force on the as-of date. The CEL body, not its front matter, is the listing reference (ENG-PRC-014 §4.1).
[P35] Heading 1: 3. Carriage determinations
[P36] Normal: The table below records the one-way carriage call for every array in scope. “Actual installed” is the equipment evidenced by the commissioning record and, for Lockmere, by the commissioning wiki file note. A checklist entry that is contradicted by the site record is not accepted as the installed configuration.

[P38] Normal: Cravenwood’s checklist identifies the inverter as installed as a Solmery Power SM-215K-3P (cover sheet and §1.3), with an 860 kW nameplate consistent with four 215 kW units. CEL-2025-Q2 lists Solmery Power SM-215K-3P in the Inverters tab at row 6: 215 kW, UL 1741-SB, effective 11/18/2024. No substitution or field change is recorded. The model is therefore carried on the current CEL and Cravenwood is waiver-eligible under ENG-PRC-014 §3.
[P39] Normal: Consequence: the witness test is not required on carriage grounds. Standards Engineering may proceed with the waiver disposition. Cravenwood is not on the 07/14/2025 SOC release list because its checklist Section 5 telemetry items 5.1–5.4 are still pending; PTO cannot issue until they pass and the SOC confirms live telemetry (TCS-02 §5).
[P40] Heading 2: 3.2 Darnwick Elementary School — carried: NO
[P41] Normal: The Darnwick checklist identifies the installed inverter as an Arvexa PV-750 (cover sheet; §2.3 refers to the “Arvexa PV-750 factory profile”). The Arvexa PV-750 does not appear anywhere in the CEL-2025-Q2 workbook — neither the Inverters tab nor the Power Control Systems tab — and it also does not appear in CEL-2024-Q4. There is no CEL row reference that could support the checklist’s pre-marked “waiver eligible” box. The pre-mark is a copy-forward at batch level, not an equipment determination, and is not a valid basis under ENG-PRC-014 §4.1.
[P42] Normal: Consequence: Darnwick is not carried and is ineligible for a witness-test waiver. An on-site witness test is required before PTO. The checklist must be corrected to record “witness test required” and must carry the current-CEL non-listing reference before the test record is closed.
[P43] Heading 2: 3.3 Holcott Public Library — carried: NO
[P44] Normal: The Holcott checklist identifies the installed inverter as a Selvix SV-720. Footnote 1 on the cover sheet expressly relies on “Selvix SV-720 listed in CEL-2024-Q4 (published 10/31/2024).” That is the superseded edition. Selvix SV-720 is present in CEL-2024-Q4 at Inverters row 29 (720 kW, UL 1741-SB, effective 10/31/2024), but it is not present in CEL-2025-Q2. Under ENG-PRC-014 §3 corollary 3 and §4.1, a model that appears solely on a superseded edition is not eligible; the old-edition footnote does not extend eligibility.
[P45] Normal: Consequence: Holcott is not carried and requires an on-site witness test before PTO. The field crew’s “waiver eligible” pre-mark must be withdrawn and the checklist corrected before the test. The CEL row to record for the historical listing is CEL-2024-Q4, Inverters row 29 — recorded as a superseded listing, not as a current eligibility basis.
[P46] Heading 2: 3.4 Lockmere Middle School — carried: NO (actual installed equipment)
[P47] Normal: The submitted Lockmere checklist records a Torvane Electric TE-180K, quantity four, with serial numbers TE180K-24-11482, -11487, -11491 and -11502, and states that TE-180K appears on CEL-2025-Q2. That statement is true of TE-180K in the abstract (CEL-2025-Q2 Inverters row 14), but it is not true of the equipment actually installed. The commissioning wiki page for Lockmere contains a file note by Evan Solberg (comment 15): “the inverter installed at Lockmere Middle is a Selvix SV-720. It was substituted on site after this checklist was submitted and the checklist still shows the original unit.”
[P48] Normal: The determination must follow the equipment actually installed, not the checklist’s original entry (ENG-PRC-014 §4.1 requires the exact make and model installed; DIS-01 §3.3 requires classification on the facility as physically configured). Selvix SV-720 is not on CEL-2025-Q2; its only listing is the superseded CEL-2024-Q4 Inverters row 29. Lockmere therefore fails the carriage test, notwithstanding the TE-180K row. The checklist serials and as-built/O&M documentation must also be corrected: they currently describe four TE-180K units that are not the installed plant.
[P49] Normal: Consequence: Lockmere is not carried and requires an on-site witness test before PTO. Because the substitution may also affect the approved protection settings (27/59, 81U/81O, 25, 32 and reclose-block) and the as-built single-line, the revised settings and as-built documents for the actual Selvix SV-720 must be on file before the test. Marden Falls is carried on the current CEL and is waiver-eligible under ENG-PRC-014 §3.
[P52] Normal: Consequence: no witness test is required on carriage grounds. Standards Engineering may proceed with the waiver disposition. Marden Falls is one of the two arrays in the batch (with Lockmere) whose checklist records live telemetry end-to-end with the SOC (telemetry provisioning row: “Pass — utility-owned RTU installed and provisioned; SCADA points verified end-to-end with SOC per TCS-02 §5”). Because Marden Falls is also carried, it is the only array that satisfies both the witness and telemetry gates and can be put to the SOC for release on 07/14/2025, subject to the signed waiver and the SOC’s live confirmation at the moment of PTO.
[P53] Heading 1: 4. Witness-test scope for the three non-carried arrays
[P54] Normal: This section applies to Darnwick Elementary, Holcott Library and Lockmere Middle only. It follows ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §4.2: testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip tests, the anti-islanding test and the ride-through verifications. The site-specific test plan must cover each enabled protection function and the equipment actually installed.
[P55] Heading 2: 4.1 Minimum test matrix
=== TABLE ===
Test family | What is tested / recorded | Basis | Acceptance and record
Protective-function trip tests | Over/under voltage (27/59), over/under frequency (81U/81O); overcurrent (50/51, 50N/51N) and directional (32) where provided; synchronism check (25) where provided. Record pickup, timing and reset for each enabled element. | IEEE 1547.1; DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 Category 2; DPS-07 Rev 2 §6.2 items 3–4 | Operation within the approved settings sheet; pass/fail per test point; measured values recorded.
Anti-islanding | Passive and/or active anti-islanding function under an open-utility condition; trip time and non-detection behaviour. | IEEE 1547.1; DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.5; approved settings | Trip within the approved time; method and trip time recorded; no sustained island.
Voltage and frequency ride-through | Category II voltage ride-through and frequency ride-through points, trip thresholds and reconnect thresholds. | IEEE 1547-2018 Category II; IEEE 1547.1; approved settings sheet | No trip outside the Category II envelope; trip inside the envelope; each test point recorded pass/fail.
Reconnect and synchronization | Reconnect delay after stable utility restoration; synchronism check (25); reclose-block logic where provided. | IEEE 1547.1; DPS-07 Rev 2 §5.1 and §6.2 item 6 | Reconnect only after the approved delay and stable source; sync/reclose logic correct.
Protection end-to-end | Each enabled protection element through its trip path; local and remote control, status and metering where provided. | DPS-07 Rev 2 §6.2 items 4–5 (where applicable) | Correct trip, status and metering response; instrument and breaker identifiers recorded.
Grounding, labels and visual | Equipment grounding continuity and bonding; utility disconnect, placards and warning labels; visible-break and lockout provisions. | Commissioning checklist Sections 1–4; DIS-01 Rev 4 §5; NEC 690/705 as referenced by the checklist | Continuity and bonding verified; labels and disconnect access correct; no open punch item.
Instrumentation and record | Calibrated instrumentation identifiers and calibration dates; measured values; pass/fail dispositions per test point; witness signature and date. | ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §4.2 and §4.3 | Test record contains all instrument IDs, measured values and dispositions; signed by the witness engineer.
=== END TABLE ===

The cross-reference is defective. This package applies the ride-through verifications in IEEE 1547-2018 / IEEE 1547.1 for the Category II profile and the site’s approved settings sheet, which is the stricter and technically correct basis. Standards Engineering should correct the cross-reference at the next procedure revision.

Classification: Engineering Standard — Distribution Protection
Approved by: Manager, Standards Engineering
1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
•
IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
•
IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
•
IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
•
ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.


--- page 2 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 2
•
Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.
•
Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.
4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.
4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the
control cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of
communications shall not defeat local protection.
Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.


--- page 3 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 3
5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect
operable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of
clearance holds.
6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location
accessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer
premises.
4.3 DER-Side Protection
DER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection
protection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI
recloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.
DER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.
4.4 Grounding
The DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with
the grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's
grounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.
4.5 Anti-Islanding
The DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone
requirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage
and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive
scheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;
otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.
5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS
5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing
The POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:
(a) The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream
recloser.
(b) The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per
the site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the
site's operating procedure.
(c) Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study
prior to energization.
5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection
DER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent
reasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the
POI recloser shall trip as backup protection.
5.3 Direct Transfer Trip
Direct transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable
non-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening
of the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications
channel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.
5.4 Reclosing Blocking
Automatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the
DER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the


--- page 4 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 4
affected feeder warrants such a change. The determination shall be made per site by Distribution Protection
5.5 Settings Governance
All protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the
DER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in
the field without a written revision order.
6. TESTING
6.1 Factory Acceptance
The POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard
test protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to
shipment.
6.2 Site Acceptance
Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed
by Alleniom Utilities:
1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.
2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.
3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,
and reset.
4. End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.
5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.
6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.
7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.
6.3 Commissioning and Cutover
Cutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and
accepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system
operator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.
6.4 Periodic Testing
The POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. DER-side protective
devices shall be tested by the DER owner on a schedule not to exceed that of comparable utility-owned
equipment, with test records made available to Alleniom Utilities on request.
6.5 Post-Event Testing
Following any operation of the POI recloser attributable to a system disturbance, a DER-side event, or a
mis-operation, Distribution Protection Engineering shall review the event records and direct such retesting or
resetting as it determines appropriate before the site is returned to service.
End of DPS-07 Rev 2 — Distribution Protection Standard. Distribution: Alleniom Standards Engineering master file;
Distribution Protection Engineering; Distribution Operations; DER Program Office; APUC filing (informational).
Engineering and recorded in the site's interconnection file.

§1   PURPOSE
This standard establishes the minimum technical and operational requirements for real-time
telemetry and communications between in-scope Distributed Energy Resource (DER) facilities
and the Alleniom Utilities System Operations Center (SOC). It governs the equipment, data
content, refresh cadence, communications transport, and cybersecurity posture required for a
DER facility to be observed and dispatchable through the utility's Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition (SCADA) system.
TCS-02 is one component of Alleniom's DER interconnection framework. Its provisions are limited
to telemetry and communications. Requirements for interconnection classification, protective
functions, service agreements, commissioning, and other lifecycle activities are addressed in the
standards and procedures cited by the interconnection standard (DIS-01) and are outside the
scope of this document.
§2   SCOPE
TCS-02 applies to every in-scope DER site as defined by DIS-01 §3 — that is, every DER whose
nameplate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold of 500 kW. Sub-500 kW DER
handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process is outside the scope of this standard.
TCS-02 applies to:
•
a.   Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW).
•
b.   Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW).
•
c.   Aggregated DER facilities recognized as a single site under DIS-01 §3.4, where the
aggregate capacity meets or exceeds the DER Program threshold.
•
d.   DER commissioned on or after the effective date of this standard, and DER
commissioned before the effective date that undergo material modification, POI relocation, or
capacity change requiring a new interconnection application.

Where a DER site interfaces with the distribution system through a shared point of common
coupling with other generation, the aggregate facility is the object of this standard, and the
aggregate is measured and controlled as a single interconnected entity.
§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS
§3.1   Ownership and installation
Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
installation drawing.
§3.3   Functional requirements
Each RTU shall, at minimum:
•
a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station
instrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.
•
b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end
processors over an approved communications path (§4).
•
c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum
of seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon
restoration.
•
d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
diagnostic points.
•
e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
SCADA/EMS Engineering only.
§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements
The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation
drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.
§3.5   Time synchronization
The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.
§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification
§3.2   Approved models
The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU
service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power
plant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the
utility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).


--- page 3 ---
TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021
Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 3
Telemetry & Communications Standard
TCS-02
Prior to the RTU being accepted as commissioned, Alleniom shall perform an end-to-end
point-to-point test that verifies each required data point (§6) at the SCADA operator display,
exercises any control points released to SCADA, and validates alarm and quality flags.
Commissioning of the RTU is a prerequisite to the telemetry condition stated in §5.
§4   COMMUNICATIONS
§4.1   Communications transport
The RTU shall communicate with Alleniom SCADA over one of the transports approved by
SCADA/EMS Engineering:
•
a.   Utility-managed fiber to an Alleniom aggregation node, or
•
b.   Utility-provisioned licensed private wireless (point-to-multipoint), or
•
c.   Utility-provisioned cellular service on the approved carrier list, using SIM credentials held
by Alleniom.
Customer-owned or shared-use networks are not permitted as the primary telemetry transport.
Where site conditions do not permit any of the transports listed above, the site is not eligible for
interconnection under the DER Program until a suitable transport can be provisioned.
§4.2   SCADA protocol
The RTU shall communicate with SCADA using DNP3 Serial or DNP3 over TCP/IP. Secure
Authentication v5 shall be enabled on the DNP3 link where supported by the RTU. Configuration
parameters — DNP3 addresses, timeouts, unsolicited response classes, integrity poll intervals —
shall follow the site-specific configuration record issued by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§4.3   Availability
The end-to-end telemetry path (RTU, transport, front-end processor) shall be designed for a
monthly availability of not less than 99.5 percent, measured at the SCADA front-end. Persistent
loss of telemetry constitutes a departure from the site's interconnection basis and shall be
corrected by the customer and utility working together to the extent each owns the affected
equipment.
§4.4   Address and IP management
All IP addresses, DNP3 addresses, VLAN assignments, and routing between the RTU and
Alleniom SCADA are assigned and managed by Alleniom. Customer equipment shall not initiate
connections toward the RTU other than as expressly permitted in the site-specific configuration
record.
§5   TELEMETRY CONDITION FOR PERMISSION TO OPERATE
§5.   ≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry.
This requirement applies to all in-scope DER sites, including aggregated facilities under
DIS-01 §3.4.
Live telemetry, for the purposes of §5, means that the RTU installed under §3 is:
•
a.   Physically installed, configured, and end-to-end commissioned in accordance with §3.6;

•
b.   Communicating with Alleniom SCADA over an approved transport (§4) at the refresh
cadence required by §6; and
•
c.   Presenting all required data points (§6) as valid (not stale, not forced, not flagged
bad-quality) at the SCADA operator display at the moment Permission to Operate (PTO) is
issued.
Compliance with §5 is confirmed by the SOC Shift Supervisor on shift at the time PTO is
requested. The SOC's confirmation is recorded against the interconnection file. PTO shall not be
issued to any in-scope DER site until §5 is satisfied.
§6   DATA POINTS AND REFRESH RATES
§6.1   Required data points
Each in-scope DER site shall present, at minimum, the following analog and status points to
Alleniom SCADA. Where the site's arrangement includes multiple inverter blocks or multiple
aggregated facilities behind a common POI, values shall be reported both individually per block

§6.2   Refresh rates


--- page 5 ---

Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 5
Telemetry & Communications Standard
TCS-02
Analog values shall be updated to SCADA at intervals no longer than four (4) seconds using DNP3
Class 1/2 event reporting for point-on-change and Class 0 integrity poll no less frequently than
every sixty (60) seconds. Status points shall be reported by exception on change of state, with an
integrity poll no less frequently than every sixty (60) seconds. Cumulative energy registers shall be
reported no less frequently than every five (5) minutes.
§6.3   Data quality
Every value delivered to SCADA shall carry a DNP3 quality flag. Values shall be marked online,
restart, communications lost, or over-range as circumstances warrant. Values held constant by the
RTU during communications loss shall not be reported as online upon restoration; they shall be
reported with the communications-lost flag until fresh source values are acquired.
§6.4   Retention
Alleniom retains all telemetry from in-scope DER sites in the historian for a minimum of thirty-six
(36) months at the raw acquisition cadence, and indefinitely at hourly aggregation, for planning,
engineering analysis, and regulatory reporting.
§7   CYBERSECURITY
§7.1   Applicability
The RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any
customer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this
section. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security
program consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.
§7.2   Access control
Local and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to
Alleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication
against Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are
managed by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.
§7.3   Communications security
DNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All
communications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an
Alleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates
shall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.
§7.4   Firmware, configuration, and change management
RTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following
the Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a
cryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or
reconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.
§7.5   Logging and monitoring
The RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,
and firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.
Anomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response
procedure.


--- page 6 ---
TCS-02  Rev 1  |  Effective 06/01/2021
Alleniom Utilities  |  Standards Engineering
Page 6
Telemetry & Communications Standard
TCS-02
§7.6   Physical security
The RTU shall be housed in a locked, tamper-evident enclosure. Enclosure keys, cores, and any
physical access tokens are held by Alleniom. Physical intrusion of the enclosure shall generate a
status point (tamper alarm) reported to SCADA under §6.
§7.7   Incident response
The customer shall report, without delay, any known or suspected compromise of the RTU, its
enclosure, its communications transport, or any interface between customer equipment and
utility-owned telemetry equipment. Reports shall be directed to the Alleniom SOC and to
SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§7.8   Decommissioning
At end of life, the RTU and its cryptographic material are returned to Alleniom for secure disposal.
Customer equipment previously interfaced to the RTU shall be sanitized of any Alleniom-provided
credentials before it is repurposed or disposed of.
End of TCS-02.

§1 PURPOSE
ERP-9 establishes the procedure by which an interconnection application encountering a standards
conflict, a silence between standards, or site conditions falling outside the assumptions of a tabulated
requirement is referred to a per-site protection/SCADA engineering determination. The procedure exists so
that documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against
active applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,
on a schedule stated in §4.
This procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER
Program. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection
Standard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.


--- page 2 ---
§2 SCOPE
ERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one
or more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system
impact study:
(1)  Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to
the affected site.
(2)  An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic
on which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an
exception).
(3)  The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in
light of the site's specific protection arrangement.
Sub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application
of ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration
warrants site-specific protection engineering input.
Nothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a
determination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).
§3 REFERRAL ROUTING
Any standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site
protection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;
each site is resolved on its own protection scheme.
The reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11
(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection
diagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's
protection arrangement. Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11 to Distribution
Protection Engineering; where SCADA/EMS input is required, the Manager, Distribution Protection
Engineering routes a copy to the SCADA/EMS Engineering group for concurrent review.
Referral does not itself alter the application's status in the DER Program queue. The affected application
remains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the
referred question shall proceed in parallel.
The per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection
Engineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and is filed with the application record. The determination is binding for the
referred site and does not create a general rule across the program; a subsequent site presenting a similar
question is referred and determined on its own facts.
Where the site's protection arrangement, as determined under this section, differs from the tabular default
of DIS-01 §5 Table 5-1, the engineering determination on Form ER-11 supplements the site's
protective-equipment scoping and is provided to the DER Program Office and to the contracts desk for
incorporation into the interconnection service agreement.
Where the referral resolves a recurring pattern that Standards Engineering considers appropriate to reflect
in a future revision of a standard, the determinations are logged and reviewed as provided in §5.


--- page 3 ---
§4 TIMELINES
Timelines below run from the date on which Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11
to Distribution Protection Engineering. Business days exclude weekends and federal holidays.

Classification is made by the Manager, Distribution Protection Engineering, on receipt of Form ER-11.
Where the reviewer requests reclassification, the request is decided in writing within two business days.
Extensions to the timelines above are permitted only in writing, are issued by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and are copied to the DER Program Manager and Regulatory Affairs. Applications
shall not be held in queue pending revision of a standard where this procedure provides a determination
path; extensions do not authorize a screening hold outside this procedure.
§5 DOCUMENTATION
The completed Form ER-11, the engineering determination, and any supporting studies are filed with the
application record retained by Interconnection Studies for the retention period established by Regulatory
Affairs. A copy of the completed Form ER-11 is filed in the Standards Engineering ERP-9 register of
per-site determinations.
The ERP-9 register records, at minimum: the referral number, the receipt date, the Project ID, the site type
and feeder, the standards documents at issue, the assigned engineer, the determination date, and a short
summary of the determination. The register is reviewed by Standards Engineering quarterly for recurring
patterns; where a pattern warrants a standards revision proposal, Standards Engineering initiates that
revision separately from, and in parallel with, ongoing per-site determinations under this procedure. A
pending revision proposal does not stay determinations issued under this procedure and does not
authorize a screening hold on affected applications.
Determinations issued under ERP-9 are cited in the interconnection service agreement (ISA) drafted for
the affected site by reference to the ER-11 referral number and determination date. Modifications to the
site's protection arrangement subsequent to ISA execution are handled under the change-order provisions
of the executed ISA, subject to DIS-01 §7 where capacity or POI is affected.

The DER Interconnection Program administered under this section applies to applications for DER
interconnection at or above five hundred kilowatts (≥500 kW). Within the Program, DER shall be
classified according to the DER Interconnection Standard as follows:
(a)  Commercial small-scale DER — five hundred kilowatts to one megawatt (500 kW – 1
MW);
(b)  Medium-scale DER — one megawatt to five megawatts (1 MW – 5 MW).
The Program scope threshold is ≥500 kW. DER below five hundred kilowatts (sub-500 kW),
whether commercial or residential, are not administered under this section and shall instead be
processed under the Company's Simplified Small-Systems Process, which is filed separately
and is outside the DER Interconnection Program.
Aggregation, controlled-capacity recognition, and shared point-of-interconnection eligibility are
addressed in the DER Interconnection Standard and shall control the classification of any facility
whose nameplate rating, aggregate site rating, or point of common coupling brings it within
Program scope.

§12.3 Application Intake and Queue Position
A complete application shall establish the applicant's queue position as of the date the Company
determines the application to be complete. Applications determined to be incomplete shall be
returned with a written deficiency notice identifying each item requiring cure and the date by which
cure is required. Queue position is not transferable between applications except as expressly
provided in the DER Interconnection Standard.
§12.4 Deemed Withdrawal Following Notice of Impending Withdrawal or Cancellation
Upon issuance of a formal written Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation by the
Company, the applicant shall have thirty (30) business days from the date of the notice to submit
a substantive response curing the matter identified therein. If the applicant fails to respond within
thirty (30) business days, the application shall be deemed withdrawn and shall be closed from the
active queue without further action of the Company.
For purposes of this section, “business days” shall exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and federal
legal public holidays observed within the response window. Without limitation, the following
federal holidays falling within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized
as non-business days and shall not be counted:

The Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall be served in writing (certified mail or
verified electronic delivery) and shall state the date of issuance, the response deadline computed
under this section, and the consequence of non-response. The Company shall maintain a log of all
notices issued, dates of service, and dispositions.

§12.5 Construction-Payment Defaults
Where a construction work order or interconnection facilities invoice becomes payable and the
customer has not remitted the amount due, the Company shall inform the customer in writing of
the outstanding balance and shall issue a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days from
the date of that written notice.
For so long as the thirty (30) business-day payment deadline is running, the affected project shall
remain on hold in the queue and shall NOT be deemed withdrawn. The construction-payment
default procedure under this §12.5 is distinct from, and shall not be conflated with, the
deemed-withdrawal procedure under §12.4; the two mechanisms have different triggers, different
consequences, and different cure paths.
Upon receipt of full payment prior to expiration of the deadline, the Company shall promptly
release the hold and resume the affected work in queue order. If the deadline expires without
payment, the Company may pursue such remedies as are available under the applicable
Interconnection Service Agreement and this tariff, including, as a separate and subsequent step,
issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §12.4.

Interconnection service shall commence only upon execution of an Interconnection Service
Agreement (“ISA”) and the Company's written Permission to Operate. Material terms of an
executed ISA, including but not limited to nameplate facility capacity and the designated point of
interconnection, may not be modified by amendment. Post-execution changes to such material
terms require withdrawal of the affected application and re-application in accordance with the DER
Interconnection Standard.
§12.7 Nondiscriminatory Queue-Order Processing of Applications
Applications shall be processed by the Company in queue order on a nondiscriminatory basis.
No applicant shall be advanced or disadvantaged in the processing sequence by reason of
identity, affiliation, customer class, geography, or any other factor not expressly provided for in this
tariff or in the DER Interconnection Standard.

sequencing of screening, technical review, study assignment, and issuance of interconnection

EQUIPMENT DEPLOYMENT PRIORITIZATION
GUIDELINE
Doc no.
Rev
Effective Date

OG-17
Rev 1
04/07/2025
Alleniom Distribution
Operations
Document Control
Supersedes: none (initial issue).
Review cycle: annual, or on material change to supplier lead times or operating criticality categories.
Approving authority: VP, Distribution Operations.
Distribution: DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; DER Planning Group; System Operations Center
(SOC); Standards Engineering; Supply Chain — Distribution Equipment.
§1  SCOPE
This guideline governs deployment sequencing of constrained utility equipment (RTUs, reclosers) across
completed sites awaiting energization. It applies to Alleniom-owned devices installed by Distribution
Operations for the purpose of energizing a construction-complete distributed energy resource (DER) site,
when supplier lead times or quarterly delivery quantities constrain the number of sites that can be
equipped in a given deployment window.
This guideline does NOT apply to application processing. Nondiscriminatory queue-order treatment of
interconnection applications is governed by Interconnection Tariff §12.7 and by the procedures
administered by Interconnection Studies; nothing in this guideline modifies, displaces, or supplements
those procedures. The rankings established under §2 operate solely on sites for which interconnection
application processing is complete, the interconnection agreement (where required) is executed, and
construction is certified complete by the customer or its contractor.
Devices out of scope: customer-owned protective equipment; utility-owned equipment already installed at
the site; distribution-system reinforcement equipment scheduled under an approved capital work order.
Program scope for the underlying DER remains as defined in DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 and Interconnection Tariff
§12.2.
§2  COMMISSIONING CRITICALITY
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA
As a general rule, deployment priority for constrained equipment follows interconnection queue order,
consistent with the nondiscriminatory treatment principles of Interconnection Tariff §12.7.
A site may be advanced ahead of queue order under certain circumstances — the urgent nature of a
request, in particular for public infrastructure (schools, hospitals, water/wastewater facilities), or an
expedited deployment pathway on reasonable customer request — but only where substantiated by the
site's own recorded attributes (per §3), in order of priority: (1) essential-service function (water/wastewater,
emergency, health); (2) committed in-service or grant-funding deadline; (3) construction-complete date.
Among sites of the same critical nature, the deciding factor is interconnection queue order; requests not
substantiated by these attributes remain in queue order.


--- page 2 ---
OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline
Page 2
Factor definitions:
•
Essential-service function. A site whose primary served load is a public water or wastewater facility;
a hospital, emergency-response, or first-responder facility; or a public-health facility for which loss of
service is treated as an emergency by the responsible jurisdiction. Essential-service status is
evidenced by the customer's facility classification of record and, where applicable, the served-load
designation on the interconnection application.
•
Committed in-service or grant-funding deadline. A contractually committed in-service date, or a
date on which grant funding lapses if the site is not in service, established in a fully executed written
instrument between the customer and a governmental funder, project sponsor, or off-taker. Internal
customer construction targets, marketing dates, budget-cycle expectations, and school-year,
fiscal-year, or seasonal preferences do not constitute a committed deadline under this factor.
•
Construction-complete date. The calendar date on which the customer's construction of the site
was certified complete and ready for utility energization steps. Where more than one date is recorded,
the earlier of (a) the customer's written notice of construction completion and (b) the utility's on-site
verification, controls.
•
Queue date as tiebreaker. The interconnection queue date of the site's underlying application, used
only to break a tie among sites that rank equally on factors (1), (2), and (3).
External advocacy, correspondence volume, elected-official inquiries, and stakeholder communications
received in relation to a site do not enter the ranking. Ranking is determined from the raw attributes above,
evidenced by the source documents in §3.
§3  DOCUMENTATION
For each deployment window the DER Program Office shall assemble a deployment worksheet listing
every site meeting the eligibility conditions of §1, with the following fields drawn from the identified system
of record:
•
Site name and interconnection application ID (DER Program queue).
•
Customer / party of record and site service address (DER Program queue).
•
Nameplate capacity and program-scope classification per DIS-01 Rev 4 §3 (application file).
•
Devices required to energize (RTU, POI recloser, or both), quantities, and specification references
(Standards Engineering).
•
Construction-complete date and source of certification (project construction file).
•
Contracted in-service or grant-funding deadline, if any, with the executed instrument establishing it
attached by reference (customer submission).
•
Essential-service classification, if any, with the customer's facility classification of record attached by
reference (application file).
•
Interconnection queue date (DER Program queue).
The worksheet shall record the §2 factor on which each ranked site qualifies. Sites that do not qualify at
ranks (1) or (2) are ranked by (3) with (4) as tiebreaker. The worksheet, the ranked deployment list, and
the assigned equipment-set identifiers shall be retained in the DER Program equipment-planning file for
the applicable window and provided to the SOC concurrent with the coordination step described in §5.


--- page 3 ---
OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline
Page 3
Amendments to the worksheet arising after issuance — for example, receipt of previously missing
documentation for a listed site, or arrival of a new site into the waiting population — shall be recorded in an
addendum bearing its own date; prior ranked lists are not overwritten.
§4  VENDOR ENGAGEMENT EXPECTATIONS
Distribution Operations, working through Supply Chain, shall maintain rolling engagement with the current
approved suppliers of RTUs and POI reclosers with the following expectations:
•
Lead-time visibility. A monthly written statement of committed lead times, next scheduled delivery
date, and delivery quantity per device type, retained in the equipment-planning file. Any change to a
previously committed date or quantity is to be flagged in writing on receipt.
•
Order coverage. Standing purchase orders shall cover no fewer than the number of device sets
required to satisfy the sites eligible under §1 for the current deployment window plus the next
scheduled delivery window. Expedite requests shall be pursued where a delivery-date change would
displace a rank-(1) or rank-(2) site.
•
Alternate sourcing. Where committed lead times exceed the interval between deliveries, Supply
Chain shall document the shortcoming of the current approved suppliers and evaluate qualification of
additional vendors under Standards Engineering's certification procedures. Qualification effort shall
not condition or delay deployment decisions for the current window.
•
Substitution. Any proposed substitution of device model or configuration relative to the site's
approved specification is routed to Standards Engineering; substitutions are not accepted on
schedule pressure alone.
•
Escrow / spares. A minimum spare quantity per device type shall be held at the operations
warehouse, replenished on drawdown, and not consumed to accelerate a lower-ranked site ahead of
a higher-ranked site whose device set is en route.
Vendor engagement records are subject to audit by Regulatory Affairs on request.
§5  COORDINATION WITH THE SYSTEM OPERATIONS CENTER
The ranked deployment list issued under §3 is transmitted to the SOC concurrent with its issuance.
Coordination steps are as follows:
•
Pre-deployment briefing. For each device set scheduled to arrive in the deployment window, the
DER Program Office and the SOC Shift Supervisor confirm the receiving site, the anticipated
field-installation window, the commissioning sequence, and the telemetry integration steps required
for permission-to-operate (PTO). Nothing in this guideline modifies the SOC's PTO gating criteria;
TCS-02 §5 requires utility-owned RTU and SCADA telemetry with live telemetry established prior to
PTO for sites at or above 500 kW, and this guideline does not authorize interim or provisional
energization ahead of that condition.
•
Change control. A change to the ranked list after transmittal to the SOC — for example, arrival of a
new rank-(1) site, or documented lapse of a committed deadline previously credited at rank (2) — is
issued by written addendum jointly to Supply Chain and to the SOC. Verbal reprioritization is not to be
relied upon.
•
Field constraints. Where feeder condition, crew availability, or outage-window constraints prevent
installation at a higher-ranked site within the window, the SOC records the constraint and the DER
Program Office reissues the deployment assignment for that device set to the next-eligible site; the


--- page 4 ---
OG-17 Rev 1 — Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline
Page 4
higher-ranked site retains its rank for the following window.
•
Commissioning readiness. The SOC's PTO-hold log continues to govern which completed sites are
eligible for energization steps; sites without established telemetry remain on the hold log until the
utility-owned RTU is installed and telemetry is verified in accordance with TCS-02.
•
Reporting. A written record of device-set assignments, installation dates, commissioning outcomes,
and any addenda issued during the window is retained by the DER Program Office and made
available to Regulatory Affairs and to the SOC on request.
End of Guideline OG-17.

witness-clear and telemetry-live before the SOC can be asked to issue Permission to Operate (PTO).

edition footnote does not extend eligibility.
Consequence: Holcott is not carried and requires an on-site witness test before PTO. The field
crew’s “waiver eligible” pre-mark must be withdrawn and the checklist corrected before the test.
The CEL row to record for the historical listing is CEL-2024-Q4, Inverters row 29 — recorded as a
superseded listing, not as a current eligibility basis.

3.4 Lockmere Middle School — carried: NO (actual installed equipment)
The submitted Lockmere checklist records a Torvane Electric TE-180K, quantity four, with serial
numbers TE180K-24-11482, -11487, -11491 and -11502, and states that TE-180K appears on
CEL-2025-Q2. That statement is true of TE-180K in the abstract (CEL-2025-Q2 Inverters row 14),
but it is not true of the equipment actually installed. The commissioning wiki page for Lockmere
contains a file note by Evan Solberg (comment 15): “the inverter installed at Lockmere Middle is a
Selvix SV-720. It was substituted on site after this checklist was submitted and the checklist still
shows the original unit.”
The determination must follow the equipment actually installed, not the checklist’s original entry
(ENG-PRC-014 §4.1 requires the exact make and model installed; DIS-01 §3.3 requires classification
on the facility as physically configured). Selvix SV-720 is not on CEL-2025-Q2; its only listing is the
superseded CEL-2024-Q4 Inverters row 29. Lockmere therefore fails the carriage test,
notwithstanding the TE-180K row. The checklist serials and as-built/O&M documentation must also
be corrected: they currently describe four TE-180K units that are not the installed plant.
Consequence: Lockmere is not carried and requires an on-site witness test before PTO. Because the
substitution may also affect the approved protection settings (27/59, 81U/81O, 25, 32 and reclose-
block) and the as-built single-line, the revised settings and as-built documents for the actual Selvix
SV-720 must be on file before the test. If the substitution occurred after the 06/09/2025 AHJ
inspection, the AHJ record must be reconciled before PTO.

3.5 Marden Falls Water Reclamation Facility — carried: YES
The Marden Falls checklist identifies the installed inverter as a Solmery Power SM-245K-3P, four
units at 245 kW each, 980 kW AC aggregate (cover sheet and nameplate row). CEL-2025-Q2 lists
Solmery Power SM-245K-3P in the Inverters tab at row 7: 245 kW, UL 1741-SB, effective
01/27/2025. No substitution or field change is recorded. Marden Falls is carried on the current CEL
and is waiver-eligible under ENG-PRC-014 §3.
Consequence: no witness test is required on carriage grounds. Standards Engineering may proceed
with the waiver disposition. Marden Falls is one of the two arrays in the batch (with Lockmere)
whose checklist records live telemetry end-to-end with the SOC (telemetry provisioning row: “Pass
— utility-owned RTU installed and provisioned; SCADA points verified end-to-end with SOC per
TCS-02 §5”). Because Marden Falls is also carried, it is the only array that satisfies both the witness
and telemetry gates and can be put to the SOC for release on 07/14/2025, subject to the signed
waiver and the SOC’s live confirmation at the moment of PTO.

4.3 Boundaries of this witness scope
   Waiver disposition. This package does not grant or deny a waiver. It determines carriage and
    the witness-test consequence. Standards Engineering retains the waiver decision for
    Cravenwood and Marden Falls and must sign the disposition on the record.
   Telemetry commissioning. TCS-02 telemetry installation and end-to-end SCADA verification are
    separate from the witness test. They are nevertheless a PTO gate: no PTO without live telemetry
    at 500 kW and above (TCS-02 §5).
   Protection standards conflict. DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 requires a utility-owned POI recloser for every
    export-capable in-scope site with no exceptions; DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 states that a POI
    recloser is not required for Category 2 export sites. That conflict is routed under ERP-9 §3
    (Form ER-11) and is not resolved or used as a screening hold in this package. The DPS-07 §6.2
    site-acceptance items are included in the witness scope only where the site’s protection
    arrangement includes the relevant device.
   Post-PTO and periodic testing. Periodic recloser maintenance (DPS-07 §6.4) and post-event
    testing (§6.5) are outside this scope.
