# Independent review — Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx

Reviewer: Independent checking engineer. Subject: `/filesystem/Commissioning/Municipal/Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx` (MD5 41e3ce8b2036060707988600f907d53a; document-store copy `/DER_Program/Commissioning/Municipal/Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx` matches the delivered file). As-of date: 07/14/2025.

Method: read the instruction, the governing procedure (ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3), CEL-2025-Q2, CEL-2024-Q4, DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 Rev 1, ERP-9 Rev 2, the tariff, all six municipal checklists (original PDFs, not only the extracted text), the commissioning wiki, the OpenProject case and work packages, and the equipment/queue records. Rechecked every CEL row reference and every date; recomputed the schedule and the case/package match. Format check `ahpele_check.py` passes; the DOCX is valid and filed in the correct folder.

## Findings

1. **BLOCKING — The ride-through acceptance criterion is inverted, so the test plan would reject compliant ride-through or accept non-compliant tripping.**  
   - Requirement: IEEE 1547-2018 Category II ride-through, adopted by DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 and ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §4.2; IEEE 1547.1 test procedure. The DER must ride through voltage/frequency conditions **inside** the Category II ride-through envelope and may trip **outside** it within the specified time.  
   - Deliverable: Section 4.1, “Voltage and frequency ride-through” row, acceptance column: “No trip outside the Category II envelope; trip inside the envelope; each test point recorded pass/fail.”  
   - Should be: “No trip inside the Category II ride-through envelope; trip outside the envelope within the specified time; each test point recorded pass/fail.” The present wording reverses the pass/fail criterion.  
   - Evidence: Deliverable p.6 (rendered PDF), test-matrix row; the package’s own basis cites “IEEE 1547-2018 Category II; IEEE 1547.1; approved settings sheet.” The acceptance text is the opposite of the standard’s ride-through/trip regions.

2. **BLOCKING — The DPS-07 §6.2 site-acceptance scope omits mandatory activities and the 79 reclosing function, including for Lockmere where a POI recloser is recorded.**  
   - Requirement: DPS-07 Rev 2 §6.2 — “Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed by Alleniom Utilities: 1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits. 2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification. 3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function … 4. End-to-end trip testing … 5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering … 6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic. 7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.” DPS-07 §4.2 item 3 also requires “79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5,” and §6.3 requires all §6.2 activities to be complete and accepted in writing before cutover.  
   - Deliverable: Section 4.1 matrix covers DPS-07 §6.2 items 3–7 only; items 1 and 2 do not appear in the matrix or in the “before the witness test” record list. The matrix’s protective-function tests do not include ANSI 79 automatic reclosing. Section 4.3 says the DPS-07 §6.2 items are included “only where the site’s protection arrangement includes the relevant device,” but Lockmere’s checklist records a POI recloser and reclose-block (“POI recloser reclose block coordinated with DER breaker status contact,” Lockmere checklist p.2), so the POI-recloser site-acceptance items apply. The package also has no DPS-07 §6.1 factory-acceptance record or §6.3 written cutover acceptance in the before-PTO list.  
   - Should be: Add insulation resistance/dielectric withstand, CT/VT ratio-polarity-burden, and ANSI 79 reclosing tests to the witness scope for Lockmere (and any other site with a POI recloser), and add the §6.1 factory-acceptance and §6.3 written acceptance records to the records that must be on file before the test/PTO.  
   - Evidence: DPS-07 §4.2 item 3, §6.1, §6.2, §6.3; deliverable p.6 and §6.2 table; Lockmere checklist p.2.

3. **MAJOR — The SOC release table answers “YES” for Marden Falls on 07/14/2025 although its Standards Engineering waiver is unsigned; the record as it stands supports no releasable array.**  
   - Requirement: ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §4.3 — “PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination against the current CEL edition.” The task asks for the list “as the record stands at 07/14/2025.”  
   - Deliverable: Cover count “1 array ready to put to SOC for release”; Section 8 table “Marden Falls WRF … YES — the only array”; text “Both gates are met on the record”; release instruction “put Marden Falls WRF to the SOC for release.”  
   - Should be: State that **no array is releasable on 07/14/2025**. Marden Falls is the only candidate, but its witness gate is not met until Standards Engineering signs the waiver. The correct entry is “NO on 07/14/2025 — candidate only; release after the signed waiver and the SOC’s live-telemetry confirmation.”  
   - Evidence: Marden Falls checklist, p.1–2: “Standards Engineering review (waiver eligibility confirmation): Pending. Reviewed by: Pending. Date: Pending.” The package itself says “Standards Engineering must first sign the waiver” and “this package does not supply that signature.” A `YES` in the “SOC release on 07/14/2025?” column contradicts both the record and §4.3.

4. **MAJOR — Lockmere’s AHJ reconciliation is left conditional even though the record shows the substitution occurred after the 06/09/2025 inspection.**  
   - Requirement: The AHJ electrical inspection was signed off 06/09/2025 (Lockmere checklist p.1); the wiki note says the inverter was “substituted on site after this checklist was submitted” and the checklist is dated 06/18/2025. The substitution therefore post-dates the AHJ inspection and must be reconciled before PTO.  
   - Deliverable: Section 3.4 — “If the substitution occurred after the 06/09/2025 AHJ inspection, the AHJ record must be reconciled before PTO.” Section 6.1 — “AHJ reconciliation if the Lockmere substitution occurred after the 06/09/2025 inspection.” F-01 — “reconcile AHJ if substitution post-dates 06/09/2025.”  
   - Should be: State unconditionally that the substitution post-dates the 06/09/2025 inspection (checklist dated 06/18/2025; wiki comment 15 says after submission) and that AHJ re-inspection/reconciliation is a required prerequisite, not a contingency.  
   - Evidence: Lockmere checklist p.1 (permit BE-2025-0148, sign-off 06/09/2025), checklist date 06/18/2025; wiki comment 15 (“substituted on site after this checklist was submitted”).

5. **MAJOR — Marden Falls is put forward for release without establishing its DPS-07 §4.2 POI-recloser/ERP-9 status.**  
   - Requirement: DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 — “Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection (POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.” DIS-01 Table 5-1 says a POI recloser is not required for Category 2, creating a conflict that ERP-9 §3 requires to be resolved per site on Form ER-11. The package’s own requirements register (REQ-030) records this as a hard requirement.  
   - Deliverable: Section 8 “Marden Falls WRF … YES — the only array,” with only a caveat that “if any site has an open DPS-07 §4.2 / DIS-01 Table 5-1 POI-recloser determination under ERP-9, that determination must also clear before PTO.” The Marden checklist does not record a POI recloser or an ER-11 determination; the package’s before-PTO table has no ER-11/POI-recloser row.  
   - Should be: Verify and state Marden Falls’ protection arrangement (POI recloser installed, or a signed Form ER-11 determination on file) before listing it as releasable; add the ER-11 determination and/or POI-recloser acceptance record to the before-PTO record.  
   - Evidence: DPS-07 §4.2; Marden Falls checklist p.1 (no POI recloser identified); deliverable pp.10–11; `requirements.csv` REQ-030.

6. **MAJOR — The anti-islanding test scope does not require the DPS-07 §4.5 passive-scheme study, and the installed method is not established for Darnwick or Holcott.**  
   - Requirement: DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.5 — “Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site’s system impact study demonstrates the passive scheme’s detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder; otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.”  
   - Deliverable: Section 4.1 “Anti-islanding” row says “Passive and/or active anti-islanding function under an open-utility condition”; the before-test record list includes an “Approved protection settings sheet and coordination study” but not an anti-islanding study. The checklists do not state the method for Darnwick or Holcott; Lockmere’s checklist cites the Torvane TE-180K certification, but the actual installed equipment is a Selvix SV-720.  
   - Should be: Require the anti-islanding method to be documented and, if passive-only, the system impact study to be on file; test the method actually installed.  
   - Evidence: DPS-07 §4.5; deliverable p.6; Darnwick checklist §2.2; Holcott checklist B-3; Lockmere checklist §2.

7. **MAJOR — Marden Falls’ “telemetry complete” finding is not supported to TCS-02 §3.2 (approved RTU model), which the package’s own requirements register lists as a hard requirement.**  
   - Requirement: TCS-02 Rev 1 §3.2 — “The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted.”  
   - Deliverable: Section 8 Marden Falls telemetry gate “Complete — RTU installed, SCADA verified end-to-end with SOC”; Section 6.2 “Live telemetry: RTU installed, configured and end-to-end commissioned; approved transport; all required points valid,” but no approved RTU model or asset record. The Marden checklist records only “Utility-owned RTU installed and provisioned,” with no model or asset ID (unlike Lockmere, which records RTU asset RTU-LKM-171-04 but still no model).  
   - Should be: Verify the RTU model/asset against TCS-02 §3.2 and record it before stating the telemetry gate is complete. If the model cannot be confirmed, the SOC release list must carry it as an open telemetry item.  
   - Evidence: TCS-02 §3.2; Marden Falls checklist p.1; deliverable p.10; `requirements.csv` REQ-039.

8. **MINOR — Finding F-08 is factually wrong: the Marden Falls checklist does name the procedure.**  
   - Requirement: The findings table must be accurate; F-08 says the checklist “cites ‘Per §3’ without naming the procedure.”  
   - Deliverable: F-08 — “Marden Falls checklist cites ‘Per §3’ without naming the procedure”; action “Correct the citation to ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §3 at countersignature.”  
   - Should be: Withdraw F-08. The original PDF says “Basis: Per ENG-PRC-014 §3, sites whose inverter model appears on the current Certified Equipment List edition…” (Marden Falls checklist p.1). The corpus extract dropped “ENG-PRC-014” and the author relied on the extract.  
   - Evidence: `pdftotext -layout /filesystem/Commissioning/Municipal/Checklist_Marden_Falls_WRF.pdf`, p.1; corpus text shows “Per  §3.”

   - Requirement: The findings table must be accurate; F-09 says the cover sheet has a blank commissioning date.  
   - Deliverable: F-09 — “Darnwick checklist lacks a commissioning date and an EPC name. Cover sheet has a blank commissioning date…”  
   - Should be: Remove the date part. The Darnwick PDF header says “Inverter model (per cover sheet): Arvexa PV-750 · Commissioning date: 06/15/2025,” and the sign-off is 06/15/2025. Only the EPC name is missing (“(see project file)”). The package’s own Section 2.1 table already says “signed 06/15/2025.”  
   - Evidence: Darnwick checklist p.1 and signature block; corpus text dropped the date.

10. **MINOR — Finding F-07 mischaracterizes the Withdrawal Notice Log.**  
    - Requirement: The log is the register of “Notices of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation (Tariff §12.4)” issued by the Company, not a register of voluntary customer withdrawals.  
    - Deliverable: F-07 — “Tresbay withdrawal is not in the Withdrawal Notice Log … The queue record and case record do not fully agree.”

    - Requirement: DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.1 — aggregate nameplate is the sum of manufacturer-rated AC output ratings; §3.3 — classification is on the facility as physically configured.  
    - Deliverable: Section 2.1 “Recorded capacity” and Section 3 “Capacity” show Holcott 510 kW and Darnwick 640 kW, while the installed equipment is a Selvix SV-720 (720 kW) and an Arvexa PV-750 (750 kW by model designation; datasheet not in file).

ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3  ·  Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office Page 1
ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE
DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
§1  PURPOSE
This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
dispositions.
Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).
§2  SCOPE
Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
scope of this procedure.
Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.
§3  WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.
The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:
1. The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
construction.
2. Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
3. Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
4. Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
themselves listed in the body of the current edition.
Alleniom Utilities · DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com

§4  PROCEDURE
§4.1  Look up model against current CEL.
The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
“supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
commissioning checklist.
If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
required” and forwards to §4.2.
Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.
§4.2  Schedule an on-site witness test.
Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
accordance with §4.3.

date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.

for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated

# Independent review — Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx

Reviewer: Independent checking engineer. Subject: `/filesystem/Commissioning/Municipal/Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx` (MD5 41e3ce8b2036060707988600f907d53a; document-store copy `/DER_Program/Commissioning/Municipal/Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx` matches the delivered file). As-of date: 07/14/2025.

Method: read the instruction, the governing procedure (ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3), CEL-2025-Q2, CEL-2024-Q4, DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 Rev 1, ERP-9 Rev 2, the tariff, all six municipal checklists (original PDFs, not only the extracted text), the commissioning wiki, the OpenProject case and work packages, and the equipment/queue records. Rechecked every CEL row reference and every date; recomputed the schedule and the case/package match. Format check `ahpele_check.py` passes; the DOCX is valid and filed in the correct folder.

## Findings

1. **BLOCKING — The ride-through acceptance criterion is inverted, so the test plan would reject compliant ride-through or accept non-compliant tripping.**  
   - Requirement: IEEE 1547-2018 Category II ride-through, adopted by DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 and ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §4.2; IEEE 1547.1 test procedure. The DER must ride through voltage/frequency conditions **inside** the Category II ride-through envelope and may trip **outside** it within the specified time.  
   - Deliverable: Section 4.1, “Voltage and frequency ride-through” row, acceptance column: “No trip outside the Category II envelope; trip inside the envelope; each test point recorded pass/fail.”  
   - Should be: “No trip inside the Category II ride-through envelope; trip outside the envelope within the specified time; each test point recorded pass/fail.” The present wording reverses the pass/fail criterion.  
   - Evidence: Deliverable p.6 (rendered PDF), test-matrix row; the package’s own basis cites “IEEE 1547-2018 Category II; IEEE 1547.1; approved settings sheet.” The acceptance text is the opposite of the standard’s ride-through/trip regions.

2. **BLOCKING — The DPS-07 §6.2 site-acceptance scope omits mandatory activities and the 79 reclosing function, including for Lockmere where a POI recloser is recorded.**  
   - Requirement: DPS-07 Rev 2 §6.2 — “Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed by Alleniom Utilities: 1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits. 2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification. 3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function … 4. End-to-end trip testing … 5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering … 6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic. 7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.” DPS-07 §4.2 item 3 also requires “79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5,” and §6.3 requires all §6.2 activities to be complete and accepted in writing before cutover.  
   - Deliverable: Section 4.1 matrix covers DPS-07 §6.2 items 3–7 only; items 1 and 2 do not appear in the matrix or in the “before the witness test” record list. The matrix’s protective-function tests do not include ANSI 79 automatic reclosing. Section 4.3 says the DPS-07 §6.2 items are included “only where the site’s protection arrangement includes the relevant device,” but Lockmere’s checklist records a POI recloser and reclose-block (“POI recloser reclose block coordinated with DER breaker status contact,” Lockmere checklist p.2), so the POI-recloser site-acceptance items apply. The package also has no DPS-07 §6.1 factory-acceptance record or §6.3 written cutover acceptance in the before-PTO list.  
   - Should be: Add insulation resistance/dielectric withstand, CT/VT ratio-polarity-burden, and ANSI 79 reclosing tests to the witness scope for Lockmere (and any other site with a POI recloser), and add the §6.1 factory-acceptance and §6.3 written acceptance records to the records that must be on file before the test/PTO.  
   - Evidence: DPS-07 §4.2 item 3, §6.1, §6.2, §6.3; deliverable p.6 and §6.2 table; Lockmere checklist p.2.

3. **MAJOR — The SOC release table answers “YES” for Marden Falls on 07/14/2025 although its Standards Engineering waiver is unsigned; the record as it stands supports no releasable array.**  
   - Requirement: ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §4.3 — “PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination against the current CEL edition.” The task asks for the list “as the record stands at 07/14/2025.”  
   - Deliverable: Cover count “1 array ready to put to SOC for release”; Section 8 table “Marden Falls WRF … YES — the only array”; text “Both gates are met on the record”; release instruction “put Marden Falls WRF to the SOC for release.”  
   - Should be: State that **no array is releasable on 07/14/2025**. Marden Falls is the only candidate, but its witness gate is not met until Standards Engineering signs the waiver. The correct entry is “NO on 07/14/2025 — candidate only; release after the signed waiver and the SOC’s live-telemetry confirmation.”  
   - Evidence: Marden Falls checklist, p.1–2: “Standards Engineering review (waiver eligibility confirmation): Pending. Reviewed by: Pending. Date: Pending.” The package itself says “Standards Engineering must first sign the waiver” and “this package does not supply that signature.” A `YES` in the “SOC release on 07/14/2025?” column contradicts both the record and §4.3.

4. **MAJOR — Lockmere’s AHJ reconciliation is left conditional even though the record shows the substitution occurred after the 06/09/2025 inspection.**  
   - Requirement: The AHJ electrical inspection was signed off 06/09/2025 (Lockmere checklist p.1); the wiki note says the inverter was “substituted on site after this checklist was submitted” and the checklist is dated 06/18/2025. The substitution therefore post-dates the AHJ inspection and must be reconciled before PTO.  
   - Deliverable: Section 3.4 — “If the substitution occurred after the 06/09/2025 AHJ inspection, the AHJ record must be reconciled before PTO.” Section 6.1 — “AHJ reconciliation if the Lockmere substitution occurred after the 06/09/2025 inspection.” F-01 — “reconcile AHJ if substitution post-dates 06/09/2025.”  
   - Should be: State unconditionally that the substitution post-dates the 06/09/2025 inspection (checklist dated 06/18/2025; wiki comment 15 says after submission) and that AHJ re-inspection/reconciliation is a required prerequisite, not a contingency.  
   - Evidence: Lockmere checklist p.1 (permit BE-2025-0148, sign-off 06/09/2025), checklist date 06/18/2025; wiki comment 15 (“substituted on site after this checklist was submitted”).

5. **MAJOR — Marden Falls is put forward for release without establishing its DPS-07 §4.2 POI-recloser/ERP-9 status.**  
   - Requirement: DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 — “Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection (POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.” DIS-01 Table 5-1 says a POI recloser is not required for Category 2, creating a conflict that ERP-9 §3 requires to be resolved per site on Form ER-11. The package’s own requirements register (REQ-030) records this as a hard requirement.  
   - Deliverable: Section 8 “Marden Falls WRF … YES — the only array,” with only a caveat that “if any site has an open DPS-07 §4.2 / DIS-01 Table 5-1 POI-recloser determination under ERP-9, that determination must also clear before PTO.” Section 4.3 says the conflict “is routed under ERP-9 §3 (Form ER-11),” but no Form ER-11 for any of the six arrays is in the record, and the 07/14/2025 Standards Conflict Hold List (12 applications) does not include them. The Marden checklist does not record a POI recloser or an ER-11 determination; the package’s before-PTO table has no ER-11/POI-recloser row.  
   - Should be: Verify and state Marden Falls’ protection arrangement (POI recloser installed, or a signed Form ER-11 determination on file) before listing it as releasable; add the ER-11 determination and/or POI-recloser acceptance record to the before-PTO record. Correct the “is routed” statement: no ER-11 referral for the six arrays is on file.  
   - Evidence: DPS-07 §4.2; Marden Falls checklist p.1 (no POI recloser identified); deliverable pp.8, 10–11; `requirements.csv` REQ-030; `Standards_Conflict_Hold_List.xlsx` (12 applications, none of the six); ERP-9 Precedent Register (ER-11-2025-004/009/014 only).

6. **MAJOR — The anti-islanding test scope does not require the DPS-07 §4.5 passive-scheme study, and the installed method is not established for Darnwick or Holcott.**  
   - Requirement: DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.5 — “Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site’s system impact study demonstrates the passive scheme’s detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder; otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.”  
   - Deliverable: Section 4.1 “Anti-islanding” row says “Passive and/or active anti-islanding function under an open-utility condition”; the before-test record list includes an “Approved protection settings sheet and coordination study” but not an anti-islanding study. The checklists do not state the method for Darnwick or Holcott; Lockmere’s checklist cites the Torvane TE-180K certification, but the actual installed equipment is a Selvix SV-720.  
   - Should be: Require the anti-islanding method to be documented and, if passive-only, the system impact study to be on file; test the method actually installed.  
   - Evidence: DPS-07 §4.5; deliverable p.6; Darnwick checklist §2.2; Holcott checklist B-3; Lockmere checklist §2.

7. **MAJOR — Marden Falls’ “telemetry complete” finding is not supported to TCS-02 §3.2 (approved RTU model), which the package’s own requirements register lists as a hard requirement.**  
   - Requirement: TCS-02 Rev 1 §3.2 — “The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted.”  
   - Deliverable: Section 8 Marden Falls telemetry gate “Complete — RTU installed, SCADA verified end-to-end with SOC”; Section 6.2 “Live telemetry: RTU installed, configured and end-to-end commissioned; approved transport; all required points valid,” but no approved RTU model or asset record. The Marden checklist records only “Utility-owned RTU installed and provisioned,” with no model or asset ID (unlike Lockmere, which records RTU asset RTU-LKM-171-04 but still no model).  
   - Should be: Verify the RTU model/asset against TCS-02 §3.2 and record it before stating the telemetry gate is complete. If the model cannot be confirmed, the SOC release list must carry it as an open telemetry item.  
   - Evidence: TCS-02 §3.2; Marden Falls checklist p.1; deliverable p.10; `requirements.csv` REQ-039.

8. **MINOR — Finding F-08 is factually wrong: the Marden Falls checklist does name the procedure.**  
   - Requirement: The findings table must be accurate; F-08 says the checklist “cites ‘Per §3’ without naming the procedure.”  
   - Deliverable: F-08 — “Marden Falls checklist cites ‘Per §3’ without naming the procedure”; action “Correct the citation to ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §3 at countersignature.”  
   - Should be: Withdraw F-08. The original PDF says “Basis: Per ENG-PRC-014 §3, sites whose inverter model appears on the current Certified Equipment List edition…” (Marden Falls checklist p.1). The corpus extract dropped “ENG-PRC-014” and the author relied on the extract.  
   - Evidence: `pdftotext -layout /filesystem/Commissioning/Municipal/Checklist_Marden_Falls_WRF.pdf`, p.1; corpus text shows “Per  §3.”

9. **MINOR — Finding F-09 is factually wrong on the commissioning date: the Darnwick checklist records 06/15/2025.**  
   - Requirement: The findings table must be accurate; F-09 says the cover sheet has a blank commissioning date.  
   - Deliverable: F-09 — “Darnwick checklist lacks a commissioning date and an EPC name. Cover sheet has a blank commissioning date…”  
   - Should be: Remove the date part. The Darnwick PDF header says “Inverter model (per cover sheet): Arvexa PV-750 · Commissioning date: 06/15/2025,” and the sign-off is 06/15/2025. Only the EPC name is missing (“(see project file)”). The package’s own Section 2.1 table already says “signed 06/15/2025.”  
   - Evidence: Darnwick checklist p.1 and signature block; corpus text dropped the date.

10. **MINOR — Finding F-07 mischaracterizes the Withdrawal Notice Log.**  
    - Requirement: The log is the register of “Notices of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation (Tariff §12.4)” issued by the Company, not a register of voluntary customer withdrawals.  
    - Deliverable: F-07 — “Tresbay withdrawal is not in the Withdrawal Notice Log … The queue record and case record do not fully agree.”  
    - Should be: Withdraw or reword F-07. A voluntary applicant withdrawal is not a §12.4 notice and would not appear in that log. If a voluntary-withdrawal register is wanted, identify the correct record; the absence of a Tresbay entry in the notice log is not a record gap.  
    - Evidence: `Withdrawal_Notice_Log.xlsx`, header A5 “Notices of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation (Tariff §12.4)”; Tariff §12.4; case WP45 note of voluntary withdrawal 07/09/2025.

11. **MINOR — The capacity columns use the checklist nameplate (510 kW / 640 kW) instead of the installed inverter rating (720 kW / 750 kW), although F-10 recognizes the mismatch.**  
    - Requirement: DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.1 — aggregate nameplate is the sum of manufacturer-rated AC output ratings; §3.3 — classification is on the facility as physically configured.  
    - Deliverable: Section 2.1 “Recorded capacity” and Section 3 “Capacity” show Holcott 510 kW and Darnwick 640 kW, while the installed equipment is a Selvix SV-720 (720 kW) and an Arvexa PV-750 (750 kW by model designation; datasheet not in file).  
    - Should be: Label the columns “recorded/claimed capacity” and state that the physical nameplate is 720 kW / 750 kW unless a controlled limit under DIS-01 §3.6 is recognized. Both remain in the 500 kW–1 MW class, so the carriage and scope calls do not change; the capacity basis does.  
    - Evidence: Holcott checklist p.1; CEL-2024-Q4 row 29; Darnwick checklist p.1; deliverable F-10.

12. **MINOR — Section 2.1 says Cravenwood “Sections 1–4 and 6 pass,” but Section 6.4 (Standards Engineering concurrence) is pending.**  
    - Requirement: Accurate status reporting.  
    - Deliverable: Section 2.1 table, Cravenwood row: “Checklist Sections 1–4 and 6 pass; Section 5 telemetry pending.” The Marden row says “Checklist items pass,” but its Standards review is also pending.  
    - Should be: “Sections 1–4 pass; Section 5 telemetry pending; Section 6 waiver recommendation pending Standards concurrence” for Cravenwood, and the same qualification for Marden.  
    - Evidence: Cravenwood checklist §6.4 (“pending signature”); Marden checklist p.2 (“Standards Engineering review … Pending”).

13. **MINOR — There is no contingency for a Standards Engineering waiver denial for Cravenwood or Marden Falls.**  
    - Requirement: ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §4.1 — “Waiver disposition remains at the discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination … is a necessary but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.” §4.3 requires either a signed witness-test disposition or a signed waiver disposition before PTO.  
    - Deliverable: Sections 3.1 and 3.5 say the witness test is “not required on carriage grounds” and “Standards Engineering may proceed with the waiver disposition.” The SOC release list assumes Marden’s waiver will be signed; no fallback witness-test date or scheduling item is proposed if it is denied.  
    - Should be: State that a waiver denial for Cravenwood or Marden Falls converts the array to a witness-test array, requiring a new scheduling item and a test before PTO; add a reserve date or a decision deadline that still leaves time before 08/08/2025.  
    - Evidence: ENG-PRC-014 §4.1, §4.3; deliverable §§3.1, 3.5, 8; case WP45 has no fallback item.

14. **MINOR — Two test-matrix citations are imprecise.**  
    - Requirement: Each test must cite the clause that actually supports it.  
    - Deliverable: “Grounding, labels and visual” cites “DIS-01 Rev 4 §5” (DIS-01 §5 is “Protective and Control Equipment,” not grounding/labels); “Reconnect and synchronization” cites “DPS-07 Rev 2 §5.1” (coordination with feeder reclosing, not reconnect delay).  
    - Should be: Cite the correct clauses (e.g., DIS-01 Table 5-1 / NEC 690/705 for labels and disconnects; DPS-07 §5.1 for reclose coordination and IEEE 1547.1 for reconnect timing).  
    - Evidence: DIS-01 §5 heading; DPS-07 §5.1 heading; deliverable p.6.

## Items checked and found acceptable

- Scope: six checklists reviewed; Tresbay excluded on the 07/09/2025 case record; five arrays in scope. The package’s Section 2 table and Section 8 Tresbay row are consistent with the case description.
- CEL row references: SM-215K-3P is Inverters row 6 (215 kW, UL 1741-SB, 11/18/2024); SM-245K-3P is row 7 (245 kW, 01/27/2025); TE-180K is row 14 (180 kW, 12/09/2024); SV-720 is CEL-2024-Q4 row 29 (720 kW, 10/31/2024). All confirmed against the workbooks.
- Carriage calls: Cravenwood YES; Marden Falls YES; Darnwick NO (Arvexa PV-750 absent from both CEL editions); Holcott NO (SV-720 only on superseded CEL-2024-Q4); Lockmere NO (actual installed SV-720 per wiki comment 15, not the checklist TE-180K). All five calls are supported by the record.
- Case tracking: WP45 is Closed/100% with assignee Evan Solberg; WP47, WP48 and WP49 are New with due dates 07/22, 07/24 and 07/29/2025; the three “includes” relations exist; the package’s three witness arrays match the three scheduling items. The case closure condition in the instruction is met.
- Schedule arithmetic: 07/22, 07/24 and 07/29/2025 are Tue/Thu/Tue; the 5-business-day prerequisite dates (07/15, 07/17, 07/22) and the 08/08/2025 latest-test / 08/11/2025 signed-record / 08/15/2025 response arithmetic are correct.
- Filing and format: exact file name; document-store folder `/DER_Program/Commissioning/Municipal`; store copy hash matches; DOCX opens and passes `ahpele_check.py`; 13 pages; no placeholder cells.
- Requirement scan: `ahpele_reqscan.py --check` reports 54/54 strong project-document candidates reviewed, 0 unreviewed; `--register requirements.csv` reports rows=57, notfound=0, unmatched=0, multi=0. This confirms the author’s scan coverage; it does not cure the technical gaps above.

## Bottom line

The package gets the central carriage calls right: Cravenwood and Marden Falls are carried on CEL-2025-Q2; Darnwick, Holcott and Lockmere are not; the three scheduling items match the three witness-test arrays. It is not ready to issue as a verified determination because the ride-through acceptance criterion is inverted (Finding 1), the DPS-07 §6.2/§4.2 witness scope is incomplete (Finding 2), and the SOC release answer is stated as a `YES` for Marden Falls while the waiver is unsigned (Finding 3). Findings 4–7 are material record/technical gaps that must be closed before the tests and PTO. Findings 8–14 are corrections to the findings table, citations and the waiver-denial contingency.

## Bottom line

The package gets the central carriage calls right: Cravenwood and Marden Falls are carried on CEL-2025-Q2; Darnwick, Holcott and Lockmere are not; the three scheduling items match the three witness-test arrays. exit_code=0
# Independent review — Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx

Reviewer: Independent checking engineer. Subject: `/filesystem/Commissioning/Municipal/Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx` (MD5 41e3ce8b2036060707988600f907d53a; document-store copy `/DER_Program/Commissioning/Municipal/Municipal_Witness_Test_Package.docx` matches the delivered file). As-of date: 07/14/2025.

Method: read the instruction, the governing procedure (ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3), CEL-2025-Q2, CEL-2024-Q4, DIS-01 Rev 4, DPS-07 Rev 2, TCS-02 Rev 1, ERP-9 Rev 2, the tariff, all six municipal checklists (original PDFs, not only the extracted text), the commissioning wiki, the OpenProject case and work packages, and the equipment/queue records. Rechecked every CEL row reference and every date; recomputed the schedule and the case/package match. Format check `ahpele_check.py` passes; the DOCX is valid and filed in the correct folder.

## Findings

1. **BLOCKING — The ride-through acceptance criterion is inverted, so the test plan would reject compliant ride-through or accept non-compliant tripping.**  
   - Requirement: IEEE 1547-2018 Category II ride-through, adopted by DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 and ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §4.2; IEEE 1547.1 test procedure. The DER must ride through voltage/frequency conditions **inside** the Category II ride-through envelope and may trip **outside** it within the specified time.  
   - Deliverable: Section 4.1, “Voltage and frequency ride-through” row, acceptance column: “No trip outside the Category II envelope; trip inside the envelope; each test point recorded pass/fail.”  
   - Should be: “No trip inside the Category II ride-through envelope; trip outside the envelope within the specified time; each test point recorded pass/fail.” The present wording reverses the pass/fail criterion.  
   - Evidence: Deliverable p.6 (rendered PDF), test-matrix row; the package’s own basis cites “IEEE 1547-2018 Category II; IEEE 1547.1; approved settings sheet.” The acceptance text is the opposite of the standard’s ride-through/trip regions.

2. **BLOCKING — The DPS-07 §6.2 site-acceptance scope omits mandatory activities and the 79 reclosing function, including for Lockmere where a POI recloser is recorded.**  
   - Requirement: DPS-07 Rev 2 §6.2 — “Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed by Alleniom Utilities: 1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits. 2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification. 3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function … 4. End-to-end trip testing … 5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering … 6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic. 7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.” DPS-07 §4.2 item 3 also requires “79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5,” and §6.3 requires all §6.2 activities to be complete and accepted in writing before cutover.  
   - Deliverable: Section 4.1 matrix covers DPS-07 §6.2 items 3–7 only; items 1 and 2 do not appear in the matrix or in the “before the witness test” record list. The matrix’s protective-function tests do not include ANSI 79 automatic reclosing. Section 4.3 says the DPS-07 §6.2 items are included “only where the site’s protection arrangement includes the relevant device,” but Lockmere’s checklist records a POI recloser and reclose-block (“POI recloser reclose block coordinated with DER breaker status contact,” Lockmere checklist p.2), so the POI-recloser site-acceptance items apply. The package also has no DPS-07 §6.1 factory-acceptance record or §6.3 written cutover acceptance in the before-PTO list.  
   - Should be: Add insulation resistance/dielectric withstand, CT/VT ratio-polarity-burden, and ANSI 79 reclosing tests to the witness scope for Lockmere (and any other site with a POI recloser), and add the §6.1 factory-acceptance and §6.3 written acceptance records to the records that must be on file before the test/PTO.  
   - Evidence: DPS-07 §4.2 item 3, §6.1, §6.2, §6.3; deliverable p.6 and §6.2 table; Lockmere checklist p.2.

3. **MAJOR — The SOC release table answers “YES” for Marden Falls on 07/14/2025 although its Standards Engineering waiver is unsigned; the record as it stands supports no releasable array.**  
   - Requirement: ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §4.3 — “PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination against the current CEL edition.” The task asks for the list “as the record stands at 07/14/2025.”  
   - Deliverable: Cover count “1 array ready to put to SOC for release”; Section 8 table “Marden Falls WRF … YES — the only array”; text “Both gates are met on the record”; release instruction “put Marden Falls WRF to the SOC for release.”  
   - Should be: State that **no array is releasable on 07/14/2025**. Marden Falls is the only candidate, but its witness gate is not met until Standards Engineering signs the waiver. The correct entry is “NO on 07/14/2025 — candidate only; release after the signed waiver and the SOC’s live-telemetry confirmation.”  
   - Evidence: Marden Falls checklist, p.1–2: “Standards Engineering review (waiver eligibility confirmation): Pending. Reviewed by: Pending. Date: Pending.” The package itself says “Standards Engineering must first sign the waiver” and “this package does not supply that signature.” A `YES` in the “SOC release on 07/14/2025?” column contradicts both the record and §4.3.

4. **MAJOR — Lockmere’s AHJ reconciliation is left conditional even though the record shows the substitution occurred after the 06/09/2025 inspection.**  
   - Requirement: The AHJ electrical inspection was signed off 06/09/2025 (Lockmere checklist p.1); the wiki note says the inverter was “substituted on site after this checklist was submitted” and the checklist is dated 06/18/2025. The substitution therefore post-dates the AHJ inspection and must be reconciled before PTO.  
   - Deliverable: Section 3.4 — “If the substitution occurred after the 06/09/2025 AHJ inspection, the AHJ record must be reconciled before PTO.” Section 6.1 — “AHJ reconciliation if the Lockmere substitution occurred after the 06/09/2025 inspection.” F-01 — “reconcile AHJ if substitution post-dates 06/09/2025.”  
   - Should be: State unconditionally that the substitution post-dates the 06/09/2025 inspection (checklist dated 06/18/2025; wiki comment 15 says after submission) and that AHJ re-inspection/reconciliation is a required prerequisite, not a contingency.  
   - Evidence: Lockmere checklist p.1 (permit BE-2025-0148, sign-off 06/09/2025), checklist date 06/18/2025; wiki comment 15 (“substituted on site after this checklist was submitted”).

5. **MAJOR — Marden Falls is put forward for release without establishing its DPS-07 §4.2 POI-recloser/ERP-9 status.**  
   - Requirement: DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 — “Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection (POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.” DIS-01 Table 5-1 says a POI recloser is not required for Category 2, creating a conflict that ERP-9 §3 requires to be resolved per site on Form ER-11. The package’s own requirements register (REQ-030) records this as a hard requirement.  
   - Deliverable: Section 8 “Marden Falls WRF … YES — the only array,” with only a caveat that “if any site has an open DPS-07 §4.2 / DIS-01 Table 5-1 POI-recloser determination under ERP-9, that determination must also clear before PTO.” Section 4.3 says the conflict “is routed under ERP-9 §3 (Form ER-11),” but no Form ER-11 for any of the six arrays is in the record, and the 07/14/2025 Standards Conflict Hold List (12 applications) does not include them. The Marden checklist does not record a POI recloser or an ER-11 determination; the package’s before-PTO table has no ER-11/POI-recloser row.  
   - Should be: Verify and state Marden Falls’ protection arrangement (POI recloser installed, or a signed Form ER-11 determination on file) before listing it as releasable; add the ER-11 determination and/or POI-recloser acceptance record to the before-PTO record. Correct the “is routed” statement: no ER-11 referral for the six arrays is on file.  
   - Evidence: DPS-07 §4.2; Marden Falls checklist p.1 (no POI recloser identified); deliverable pp.8, 10–11; `requirements.csv` REQ-030; `Standards_Conflict_Hold_List.xlsx` (12 applications, none of the six); ERP-9 Precedent Register (ER-11-2025-004/009/014 only).

6. **MAJOR — The anti-islanding test scope does not require the DPS-07 §4.5 passive-scheme study, and the installed method is not established for Darnwick or Holcott.**  
   - Requirement: DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.5 — “Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site’s system impact study demonstrates the passive scheme’s detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder; otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.”  
   - Deliverable: Section 4.1 “Anti-islanding” row says “Passive and/or active anti-islanding function under an open-utility condition”; the before-test record list includes an “Approved protection settings sheet and coordination study” but not an anti-islanding study. The checklists do not state the method for Darnwick or Holcott; Lockmere’s checklist cites the Torvane TE-180K certification, but the actual installed equipment is a Selvix SV-720.  
   - Should be: Require the anti-islanding method to be documented and, if passive-only, the system impact study to be on file; test the method actually installed.  
   - Evidence: DPS-07 §4.5; deliverable p.6; Darnwick checklist §2.2; Holcott checklist B-3; Lockmere checklist §2.

7. **MAJOR — Marden Falls’ “telemetry complete” finding is not supported to TCS-02 §3.2 (approved RTU model), which the package’s own requirements register lists as a hard requirement.**  
   - Requirement: TCS-02 Rev 1 §3.2 — “The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted.”  
   - Deliverable: Section 8 Marden Falls telemetry gate “Complete — RTU installed, SCADA verified end-to-end with SOC”; Section 6.2 “Live telemetry: RTU installed, configured and end-to-end commissioned; approved transport; all required points valid,” but no approved RTU model, asset record or approved-transport evidence. The Marden checklist records only “Utility-owned RTU installed and provisioned,” with no model, asset ID or transport (unlike Lockmere, which records RTU asset RTU-LKM-171-04 and a cellular backhaul but still no model).  
   - Should be: Verify the RTU model/asset against TCS-02 §3.2 and the transport against TCS-02 §4.1, and record them before stating the telemetry gate is complete. If the model or transport cannot be confirmed, the SOC release list must carry it as an open telemetry item.  
   - Evidence: TCS-02 §3.2 and §4.1; Marden Falls checklist p.1; deliverable p.10; `requirements.csv` REQ-039.

8. **MINOR — Finding F-08 is factually wrong: the Marden Falls checklist does name the procedure.**  
   - Requirement: The findings table must be accurate; F-08 says the checklist “cites ‘Per §3’ without naming the procedure.”  
   - Deliverable: F-08 — “Marden Falls checklist cites ‘Per §3’ without naming the procedure”; action “Correct the citation to ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §3 at countersignature.”  
   - Should be: Withdraw F-08. The original PDF says “Basis: Per ENG-PRC-014 §3, sites whose inverter model appears on the current Certified Equipment List edition…” (Marden Falls checklist p.1). The corpus extract dropped “ENG-PRC-014” and the author relied on the extract.  
   - Evidence: `pdftotext -layout /filesystem/Commissioning/Municipal/Checklist_Marden_Falls_WRF.pdf`, p.1; corpus text shows “Per  §3.”

9. **MINOR — Finding F-09 is factually wrong on the commissioning date: the Darnwick checklist records 06/15/2025.**  
   - Requirement: The findings table must be accurate; F-09 says the cover sheet has a blank commissioning date.  
   - Deliverable: F-09 — “Darnwick checklist lacks a commissioning date and an EPC name. Cover sheet has a blank commissioning date…”  
   - Should be: Remove the date part. The Darnwick PDF header says “Inverter model (per cover sheet): Arvexa PV-750 · Commissioning date: 06/15/2025,” and the sign-off is 06/15/2025. Only the EPC name is missing (“(see project file)”). The package’s own Section 2.1 table already says “signed 06/15/2025.”  
   - Evidence: Darnwick checklist p.1 and signature block; corpus text dropped the date.

10. **MINOR — Finding F-07 mischaracterizes the Withdrawal Notice Log.**  
    - Requirement: The log is the register of “Notices of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation (Tariff §12.4)” issued by the Company, not a register of voluntary customer withdrawals.  
    - Deliverable: F-07 — “Tresbay withdrawal is not in the Withdrawal Notice Log … The queue record and case record do not fully agree.”  
    - Should be: Withdraw or reword F-07. A voluntary applicant withdrawal is not a §12.4 notice and would not appear in that log. If a voluntary-withdrawal register is wanted, identify the correct record; the absence of a Tresbay entry in the notice log is not a record gap.  
    - Evidence: `Withdrawal_Notice_Log.xlsx`, header A5 “Notices of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation (Tariff §12.4)”; Tariff §12.4; case WP45 note of voluntary withdrawal 07/09/2025.

11. **MINOR — The capacity columns use the checklist nameplate (510 kW / 640 kW) instead of the installed inverter rating (720 kW / 750 kW), although F-10 recognizes the mismatch.**  
    - Requirement: DIS-01 Rev 4 §3.1 — aggregate nameplate is the sum of manufacturer-rated AC output ratings; §3.3 — classification is on the facility as physically configured.  
    - Deliverable: Section 2.1 “Recorded capacity” and Section 3 “Capacity” show Holcott 510 kW and Darnwick 640 kW, while the installed equipment is a Selvix SV-720 (720 kW) and an Arvexa PV-750 (750 kW by model designation; datasheet not in file).  
    - Should be: Label the columns “recorded/claimed capacity” and state that the physical nameplate is 720 kW / 750 kW unless a controlled limit under DIS-01 §3.6 is recognized. Both remain in the 500 kW–1 MW class, so the carriage and scope calls do not change; the capacity basis does.  
    - Evidence: Holcott checklist p.1; CEL-2024-Q4 row 29; Darnwick checklist p.1; deliverable F-10.

12. **MINOR — Section 2.1 says Cravenwood “Sections 1–4 and 6 pass,” but Section 6.4 (Standards Engineering concurrence) is pending.**  
    - Requirement: Accurate status reporting.  
    - Deliverable: Section 2.1 table, Cravenwood row: “Checklist Sections 1–4 and 6 pass; Section 5 telemetry pending.” The Marden row says “Checklist items pass,” but its Standards review is also pending.  
    - Should be: “Sections 1–4 pass; Section 5 telemetry pending; Section 6 waiver recommendation pending Standards concurrence” for Cravenwood, and the same qualification for Marden.  
    - Evidence: Cravenwood checklist §6.4 (“pending signature”); Marden checklist p.2 (“Standards Engineering review … Pending”).

13. **MINOR — There is no contingency for a Standards Engineering waiver denial for Cravenwood or Marden Falls.**  
    - Requirement: ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 §4.1 — “Waiver disposition remains at the discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination … is a necessary but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.” §4.3 requires either a signed witness-test disposition or a signed waiver disposition before PTO.  
    - Deliverable: Sections 3.1 and 3.5 say the witness test is “not required on carriage grounds” and “Standards Engineering may proceed with the waiver disposition.” The SOC release list assumes Marden’s waiver will be signed; no fallback witness-test date or scheduling item is proposed if it is denied.  
    - Should be: State that a waiver denial for Cravenwood or Marden Falls converts the array to a witness-test array, requiring a new scheduling item and a test before PTO; add a reserve date or a decision deadline that still leaves time before 08/08/2025.  
    - Evidence: ENG-PRC-014 §4.1, §4.3; deliverable §§3.1, 3.5, 8; case WP45 has no fallback item.

14. **MINOR — Two test-matrix citations are imprecise.**  
    - Requirement: Each test must cite the clause that actually supports it.  
    - Deliverable: “Grounding, labels and visual” cites “DIS-01 Rev 4 §5” (DIS-01 §5 is “Protective and Control Equipment,” not grounding/labels); “Reconnect and synchronization” cites “DPS-07 Rev 2 §5.1” (coordination with feeder reclosing, not reconnect delay).  
    - Should be: Cite the correct clauses (e.g., DIS-01 Table 5-1 / NEC 690/705 for labels and disconnects; DPS-07 §5.1 for reclose coordination and IEEE 1547.1 for reconnect timing).  
    - Evidence: DIS-01 §5 heading; DPS-07 §5.1 heading; deliverable p.6.

## Items checked and found acceptable

- Scope: six checklists reviewed; Tresbay excluded on the 07/09/2025 case record; five arrays in scope. The package’s Section 2 table and Section 8 Tresbay row are consistent with the case description.
- CEL row references: SM-215K-3P is Inverters row 6 (215 kW, UL 1741-SB, 11/18/2024); SM-245K-3P is row 7 (245 kW, 01/27/2025); TE-180K is row 14 (180 kW, 12/09/2024); SV-720 is CEL-2024-Q4 row 29 (720 kW, 10/31/2024). All confirmed against the workbooks.
- Carriage calls: Cravenwood YES; Marden Falls YES; Darnwick NO (Arvexa PV-750 absent from both CEL editions); Holcott NO (SV-720 only on superseded CEL-2024-Q4); Lockmere NO (actual installed SV-720 per wiki comment 15, not the checklist TE-180K). All five calls are supported by the record.
- Case tracking: WP45 is Closed/100% with assignee Evan Solberg; WP47, WP48 and WP49 are New with due dates 07/22, 07/24 and 07/29/2025; the three “includes” relations exist; the package’s three witness arrays match the three scheduling items. The case closure condition in the instruction is met.
- Schedule arithmetic: 07/22, 07/24 and 07/29/2025 are Tue/Thu/Tue; the 5-business-day prerequisite dates (07/15, 07/17, 07/22) and the 08/08/2025 latest-test / 08/11/2025 signed-record / 08/15/2025 response arithmetic are correct.
- Filing and format: exact file name; document-store folder `/DER_Program/Commissioning/Municipal`; store copy hash matches; DOCX opens and passes `ahpele_check.py`; 13 pages; no placeholder cells.
- Requirement scan: `ahpele_reqscan.py --check` reports 54/54 strong project-document candidates reviewed, 0 unreviewed; `--register requirements.csv` reports rows=57, notfound=0, unmatched=0, multi=0. This confirms the author’s scan coverage; it does not cure the technical gaps above.

## Bottom line

The package gets the central carriage calls right: Cravenwood and Marden Falls are carried on CEL-2025-Q2; Darnwick, Holcott and Lockmere are not; the three scheduling items match the three witness-test arrays. It is not ready to issue as a verified determination because the ride-through acceptance criterion is inverted (Finding 1), the DPS-07 §6.2/§4.2 witness scope is incomplete (Finding 2), and the SOC release answer is stated as a `YES` for Marden Falls while the waiver is unsigned (Finding 3). Findings 4–7 are material record/technical gaps that must be closed before the tests and PTO. Findings 8–14 are corrections to the findings table, status/labelling, citations and the waiver-denial contingency.

 ALLENIOM UTILITIES — DER PROGRAM OFFICE

 DER WITNESS TEST & WAIVER PROCEDURE
 Doc no. ENG-PRC-014 · Rev 3 · 04/30/2025 · Owner: Standards Engineering (Evan Solberg)
 Alleniom Utilities · DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com



 §1 PURPOSE
 This procedure establishes when Alleniom Utilities personnel must witness commissioning tests of a
 customer’s Distributed Energy Resource (DER) prior to issuance of Permission to Operate (PTO), and
 when the on-site witness test may be waived on the basis of the equipment installed at the facility. It is the
 controlling document for the DER Program commissioning group and for Standards Engineering waiver
 dispositions.

 Companion documents: Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard DIS-01 Rev 4; Telemetry &
 Communications Standard TCS-02; the current edition of the Alleniom Certified Equipment List (CEL).

 §2 SCOPE
 Applies to every in-scope DER facility interconnecting to the Alleniom distribution system under the DER
 Program (commercial small-scale 500 kW – 1 MW and medium-scale 1 MW – 5 MW). Domestic rooftop
 DER and sub-500 kW facilities routed through the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the
 scope of this procedure.

 Applies to the initial commissioning of a new interconnection, to re-commissioning following a capacity
 change or protective-equipment replacement, and to the disposition of any request to waive the on-site
 witness test in favor of an accepted commissioning-agent test record.

 §3 WAIVER ELIGIBILITY RULE
 Witness-test waivers apply ONLY to equipment listed on the CURRENT edition of the Certified Equipment
 List at the waiver date. Equipment not carried on the current CEL edition requires an on-site witness test
 before Permission to Operate (PTO) is issued. Listings appearing solely on a superseded CEL edition do
 NOT confer waiver eligibility on the current-edition date.

 The following are corollaries of the rule and are provided for the avoidance of doubt:

 1.     The “waiver date” is the date on which Standards Engineering signs the waiver disposition, not the
        date on which the applicant filed the interconnection application, executed the ISA, or completed
        construction.
 2.     Every protective device and every inverter (or power conversion system) installed at the facility must
        appear on the current CEL edition. A facility with any single unlisted component is ineligible.
 3.     Withdrawal of an equipment listing at the time of a CEL republication is a substantive event. A listing
        that was carried on a prior edition and was not carried forward into the successor edition confers no
        waiver eligibility once the successor edition takes effect.
 4.     Front-matter footnotes, cross-references, or historical annotations in the current CEL that describe a
        prior edition’s contents are informational only. They do not extend eligibility to models that are not
        themselves listed in the body of the current edition.



ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 · Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office                                                            Page 1
  5.     The CEL edition in force on the waiver date is the sole reference. A model that was listed at the time
        an application was filed, but is no longer listed on the waiver date, requires the on-site witness test.

 §4 PROCEDURE

 §4.1 Look up model against current CEL.
 The commissioning coordinator retrieves the current edition of the Certified Equipment List from the
 Standards Engineering document repository. The coordinator confirms the edition identifier and the
 “supersedes” reference on the CEL cover page, and verifies that no more recent edition has been
 published between the file date shown on the coordinator’s copy and the waiver disposition date. For each
 inverter and each protective device installed at the facility, the coordinator locates the exact make, model,
 and firmware family in the body of the current CEL and records the CEL row reference on the
 commissioning checklist.

 If any installed model is not present in the body of the current CEL — including any model that appears
 solely on a superseded CEL edition — the facility is ineligible for a witness-test waiver and an on-site
 witness test is required prior to PTO. Superseded editions of the CEL are archived and are not to be used
 to establish eligibility under this section. The coordinator marks the commissioning checklist “witness test
 required” and forwards to §4.2.

 Where every installed model is confirmed on the current CEL, the coordinator marks the checklist “waiver
 eligible” and forwards to Standards Engineering for written disposition. Waiver disposition remains at the
 discretion of Standards Engineering; a positive eligibility determination under this section is a necessary
 but not sufficient condition for issuance of a waiver.

 §4.2 Schedule an on-site witness test.
 Where a witness test is required, the commissioning coordinator schedules the test with the customer or
 the customer’s commissioning agent, targeting the earliest mutually available date consistent with the
 applicant’s construction-complete status and the availability of an Alleniom Utilities witness engineer.
 Testing shall be performed per IEEE 1547.1 and shall include, at minimum, the protective-function trip
 tests, the anti-islanding test, and the ride-through verifications specified in DIS-01 Rev 4 §6. The customer
 or commissioning agent supplies the test plan, calibrated instrumentation, and the qualified personnel to
 operate the equipment; the Alleniom witness engineer observes, records, and dispositions the test in
 accordance with §4.3.

 Where the required on-site witness test cannot be scheduled prior to the applicant’s targeted energization
 date, the facility remains without PTO. On-site witness testing is not to be deferred to a post-PTO date
 under any circumstance, and PTO is not to be issued conditionally against a future witness test.

 §4.3 Documentation.
 The commissioning coordinator maintains a single commissioning record for each facility. The record shall
 include, at minimum:

 •      the completed commissioning checklist, including the CEL edition identifier consulted, the CEL row
        reference for each listed model, and the “waiver eligible” or “witness test required” determination;
 •      for waiver-eligible facilities, the written Standards Engineering waiver disposition, signed and dated
        by the Standards Engineer of record;




ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 · Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office                                                  Page 2
  •      for witness-tested facilities, the witness engineer’s test record, including instrument identifiers,
        measured values, pass/fail dispositions per test point, and the witness engineer’s signature and
        date;
 •      the manufacturer’s certificate of conformance, factory test report, or equivalent evidence supporting
        the CEL listing relied upon;
 •      correspondence with the customer or commissioning agent bearing on scheduling, deferrals, or
        test-plan negotiation.
 The commissioning record is retained in the facility interconnection file and is a prerequisite to PTO
 issuance by the System Operations Center. PTO shall not be issued in the absence of either (a) a signed
 witness-test disposition or (b) a signed waiver disposition supported by a §4.1 eligibility determination
 against the current CEL edition.



 End of procedure. See DIS-01 Rev 4 for interconnection standards, TCS-02 for telemetry requirements, and the
 current CEL edition for the list of qualifying equipment. Revisions to this procedure are issued by Standards
 Engineering and take effect on the date shown in the document-control block above.




ENG-PRC-014 Rev 3 · Alleniom Utilities DER Program Office                                                Page 3

  Rev            Date             Summary

  Rev 2          09/01/2018       Alignment with IEEE 1547-2018. Introduced Category 1/2/3 protective-equipment table.

  Rev 3          12/01/2021       Program-scope threshold set at 500 kW; added §3.4 aggregation.

 §1 Purpose and Scope
 This standard establishes the technical and procedural requirements for interconnection of distributed energy
 resources (DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. It is based on IEEE 1547-2018 and applicable state
 interconnection rules filed with the Alleron Public Utilities Commission (APUC), and it applies to all DER classes
 defined in §3.

 DIS-01 Rev 4 governs:

      • classification of DER facilities by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling (§3);
      • eligibility to share an existing point of interconnection where legacy equipment is on site (§3.5);
      • recognition of a controlled operating limit below nameplate (§3.6);
      • protective and control equipment requirements by class and category (§5);



DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard                                                                            Page 1
                                                                                           DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024



      • treatment of post-execution changes to executed interconnection service agreements (§7).
 This standard is read together with the APUC-filed interconnection tariff (§12). Where a topic is addressed by both
 this standard and the tariff, the tariff controls. Requirements for real-time monitoring and communications integration
 are established under TCS-02 and are not restated here except by cross-reference.




 §2 References
 The following documents are referenced within this standard. Unless otherwise noted, the latest published revision
 applies.

      • IEEE 1547-2018 — IEEE Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources
      with Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
      • DPS-07 Rev 2 — Alleniom Distribution Protection Standard (effective 09/15/2023). Establishes distribution
      protection requirements including protective devices at points of interconnection with export-capable in-scope
      facilities.
      • TCS-02 — Alleniom Telemetry & Communications Standard (effective 06/01/2021). Governs utility-owned RTU
      installation and SCADA telemetry for DER at and above the program-scope threshold; establishes the condition
      for permission to operate.
      • CEL-2025-Q2 — Alleniom Certified Equipment List (published 04/30/2025). Listing basis: UL 1741-SB and UL
      3141. The CEL front matter restates §3.6 of this standard.
      • ERP-9 — Alleniom Engineering Referral Procedure (Form ER-11). §3 routes any standards




 Definitions of terms used in this standard follow IEEE 1547-2018 and, where applicable, the definitions in the
 APUC-filed tariff. The terms aggregate nameplate capacity and point of common coupling (PCC) have the meanings
 assigned by IEEE 1547-2018 and reflected in Company practice. The terms point of interconnection (POI),
 export-capable, and pure-generation site are used in accordance with their ordinary meaning in utility
 interconnection practice.
 §3 DER Classification
 DER facilities are classified by aggregate nameplate capacity at the point of common coupling, in accordance with
 IEEE 1547-2018. Class thresholds, applicable review path, and equipment references are stated in Table 3-1.

 Commercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW; medium-scale 1 MW–5 MW; program scope ≥500 kW; sub-500 kW DER
 (commercial and residential) is handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process, outside the DER Program.

 The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
 class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.

 §3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
 Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
 interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
 govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.

 §3.2 Point of common coupling
 The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
 distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
 the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.

 §3.3 Determination on the basis of application
 Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
 and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
 the address of record govern.

 §3.4 Aggregation
 Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.

 Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
 to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
 in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
 resulting program-scope determination.

 An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
 application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
 the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
 the Company existing-DER register.

 §3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
 A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
 to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
 existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
 own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.




DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard                                                                           Page 3
                                                                                              DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024



 The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:

   1. Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
      current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
      applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
      feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
   2. Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
      the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
      its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
      Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
 Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
 applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
 under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.

 §3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
 A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
 Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
 recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
 32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.

 Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
 program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:

   1. A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
      applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
      setpoint range.
   2. An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
      enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
      times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
 These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
 Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.

 Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
 recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:

      • Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
      monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
      triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
      • POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
      no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
      Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
      the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
      additional utility hardware.
 Enforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does
 not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.

 No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
 an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.

 §7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions
 Post-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not
 permitted for capacity or POI changes.

 Scope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by
 both parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without
 invoking this section.

 Principal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection
 service agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as
 executed.

 Required path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of
 interconnection after ISA execution shall:

   1. Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;
   2. File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and
   3. Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.
 The new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested
 change is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the
 applicant as involving new or existing equipment.

 the same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the
 change-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.

 reservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in
 queue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application
 receives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.
